questions.q: Let $\overset{\to}{a} = \overset{^}{i} + 4\overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}, \overset{\to}{b} = 3\overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} + 7\overset{^}{k}$ and $\overset{\to}{c} = 2\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + 4\overset{^}{k}$. If a vector $\overset{\to}{d}$ satisfies $\overset{\to}{d} \times \overset{\to}{b} = \overset{\to}{c} \times \overset{\to}{b}$ and $\overset{\to}{d} \cdot \overset{\to}{a} = 24,$ then ${\left|\overset{\to}{d}\right|}^{2}$ is equal to
questions.solution:
We have been given that

$\overset{\to}{d} \times \overset{\to}{b} = \overset{\to}{c} \times \overset{\to}{b}$

$⇒ ( \overset{\to}{d} - \overset{\to}{c} ) \times \overset{\to}{b} = 0$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{d} - \overset{\to}{c} = \lambda\overset{\to}{b} ( ∵ \overset{\to}{d} \ne \overset{\to}{c} )$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{d} = \overset{\to}{c} + \lambda\overset{\to}{b}$

It is given that $\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{d} = 24$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{c} + \lambda\overset{\to}{b} \cdot \overset{\to}{a} = 24$

$⇒ 6 + \lambda ( 3 - 8 + 14 ) = 24$

$⇒ 9\lambda = 18$

$⇒ \lambda = 2$

$∴ \overset{\to}{d} = \overset{\to}{c} + 2\overset{\to}{b}$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{d} = 8\overset{^}{i} - 5\overset{^}{j} + 18\overset{^}{k}$

$| \overset{\to}{d}{|}^{2} = 64 + 25 + 324$= 413$

Hence, this is the correct option.

questions.q: Let $\overset{\to}{a} = 3\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}$ and $\overset{\to}{c} = 2\overset{^}{i} - 3\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k} .$ If $\overset{\to}{b}$ is a vector such that $\overset{\to}{a} = \overset{\to}{b} \times \overset{\to}{c}$ and $| \overset{\to}{b}{|}^{2} = 50,$ then $\left|72 - {\left|\overset{\to}{b} + \overset{\to}{c}\right|$}^{2}\right|$ is equal to $__________ .
questions.solution:
Given,

$\overset{\to}{a} = 3\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}$ and $\overset{\to}{c} = 2\overset{^}{i} - 3\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k} .$

And $\overset{\to}{b}$ is a vector such that $\overset{\to}{a} = \overset{\to}{b} \times \overset{\to}{c}$ and $| \overset{\to}{b}{|}^{2} = 50,$

Now solving, $| \overset{\to}{a} | = | \overset{\to}{b} \times \overset{\to}{c} |$

$⇒ \sqrt{{3}^{2} + {1}^{2} + {1}^{2}} = | \overset{\to}{b} | \cdot \sqrt{{2}^{2} + {3}^{2} + {3}^{2}} \cdot sin\theta$

$⇒ \sqrt{11} = \sqrt{50} \cdot \sqrt{22} \cdot sin\theta$

$∴ sin\theta = \dfrac{1}{10}$ or $cos\theta = \dfrac{\sqrt{99}}{10}$

Now solving,$\left|72 - {\left|\overset{\to}{b} + \overset{\to}{c}\right|}^{2}\right|$ we get,

$\left|72 - {\left|\overset{\to}{b} + \overset{\to}{c}\right|}^{2}\right|$

$= \left|72 - \left({\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|}^{2} + {\left|\overset{\to}{c}\right|}^{2} + 2\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|\left|\overset{\to}{c}\right|cos\theta\right)\right|$

$= \left|72 - \left(50 + 22 + 2 \times 5\sqrt{2} . \sqrt{22}\dfrac{\sqrt{99}}{10}\right)\right|$

$= \left|72 - \left(72 + \dfrac{2 \times 5 \times 2 \times 11 \times 3}{10}\right\right|$

$= \left|66\right| = 66$

questions.q: Let $a, b, c$ be three distinct real numbers, none equal to one. If the vectors $a\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}, \overset{^}{i} + b\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$ and $\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + c\overset{^}{k}$ are coplanar, then $\dfrac{1}{1 - a} + \dfrac{1}{1 - b} + \dfrac{1}{1 - c}$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Given that the vectors are coplanar.

That means the determinant is equal to zero.

$⇒ \left|\begin{cases}a & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & b & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & c\end{cases}\right| = 0$

$⇒ {R}_{1} \to {R}_{1} – {R}_{2}$ and ${R}_{2} \to {R}_{2} – {R}_{3}$

$⇒ \left|\begin{cases}a - 1 & 1 - b & 0 \\ 0 & b - 1 & 1 - c \\ 1 & 1 & c\end{cases}\right| = 0$

Expand the determinant along ${C}_{1}$.

$⇒ ( a - 1 ) [ c ( b - 1 ) - ( 1 - c ) ] + 1 [ ( 1 - b ) ( 1 - c ) ] = 0$

$⇒ c ( a - 1 ) ( b - 1 ) - ( a - 1 ) ( 1 - c ) + ( 1 - b ) ( 1 - c ) = 0$

$⇒ c ( 1 - a ) ( 1 - b ) + ( 1 - a ) ( 1 - c ) + ( 1 - b ) ( 1 - c ) + \left(1 - a\right)\left(1 - b\right)\left(1 - c\right) = \left(1 - a\right)\left(1 - b\right)\left(1 - c\right)$

$⇒ ( 1 - a ) ( 1 - b ) + ( 1 - a ) ( 1 - c ) + ( 1 - b ) ( 1 - c ) = \left(1 - a\right)\left(1 - b\right)\left(1 - c\right)$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{1 - a} + \dfrac{1}{1 - b} + \dfrac{1}{1 - c} = 1$

Hence this is the required option.

questions.q: Let $\lambda \in \mathbb{Z}, \overset{\to}{a} = \lambda\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}$ and $\overset{\to}{b} = 3\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}$. Let $\overset{\to}{c}$ be a vector such that $\left(\overset{\to}{a} + \overset{\to}{b} + \overset{\to}{c}\right) \times \overset{\to}{c} = \overset{\to}{0}, \overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{c} = - 17$ and $\overset{\to}{b} \cdot \overset{\to}{c} = - 20$. Then ${\left|\overset{\to}{c} \times \left(\lambda\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}\right)\right|}^{2}$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Given that

$\overset{\to}{a} = \lambda\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}$

$\overset{\to}{b} = 3\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}$

Also $\left(\overset{\to}{a} + \overset{\to}{b} + \overset{\to}{c}\right) \times \overset{\to}{c} = \overset{\to}{0}$

$⇒ k\left(\overset{\to}{a} + \overset{\to}{b}\right) = \overset{\to}{c}$

$\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{c} = - 17$ and $\overset{\to}{b} \cdot \overset{\to}{c} = - 20$

Now, Take $\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{c} = - 17$

$⇒ k\left(\lambda\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}\right) \cdot \left(\lambda\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k} + 3\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}\right) = - 17$

$⇒ k\left({\lambda}^{2} + 3\lambda + 0 - 1\right) = - 17$

$⇒ k\left({\lambda}^{2} + 3\lambda - 1\right) = - 17 . . . . ( 1 )$

Similarly, on taking $\overset{\to}{b} \cdot \overset{\to}{c} = - 20$, we get,

$k\left(3\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}\right) \cdot \left(\lambda\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k} + 3\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}\right) = - 20$

$⇒ k\left(3\lambda + 9 + 2\right) = - 20$

$⇒ k\left(3\lambda + 11\right) = - 20 . . . ( 2 )$

Now on solving equation $\left(1\right) \text{$ and $} \left(2\right)$ we get,

$⇒ 20{\lambda}^{2} + 9\lambda - 207 = 0$

$⇒ \lambda = 3, \dfrac{- 69}{20}$

For $\lambda = 3, k = - 1$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{c} = - 1 \left(\overset{\to}{a} + \overset{\to}{b}\right)

$⇒ - $\left(\left(\lambda + 3\right)$\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{k}\right) = - 6\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{k}$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{c} \times $\left(\lambda\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}\right)$ = $\left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ - 6 & 0 & - 1 \\ 3 & 1 & 1\end{cases}\right|$ = \overset{^}{i} - 3\overset{^}{j} + 6\overset{^}{k}$

Similarly, on taking $\overset{\to}{b} \cdot \overset{\to}{c} = - 20$, we get,

$k\left(3\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}\right) \cdot \left(\lambda\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k} + 3\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}\right) = - 20$

questions.q: Let the plane $x + 3y - 2z + 6 = 0$ meet the co-ordinate axes at the points $A, B, C$. If the orthocenter of the triangle $ABC$ is $\left(\alpha, \beta, \dfrac{6}{7}\right)$, then $98{\left(\alpha + \beta\right)}^{2}$ is equal to __________.
questions.solution:
Given,

The plane $x + 3y - 2z + 6 = 0$ meet the co-ordinate axes at the points $A, B, C$,

So, $A\left(- 6, 0, 0\right), B\left(0, - 2, 0\right) \text{ and } C\left(0, 0, 3\right)$

And the orthocenter of the triangle $ABC$ is $\left(\alpha, \beta, \dfrac{6}{7}\right)$,

We know that, circumcentre of triangle is point of intersection of perpendicular bisectors,

So, plotting the diagram we get,

Now from diagram we can see that $O\text{to midpoint of}BC ⊥ BC$

So, by perpendicular vector formula we get,

$\left(x - 0\right) \times 0 + \left(y + 1\right) \times 2 + \left(z - \dfrac{3}{2}\right) \times 3 = 0$

$⇒ 4y + 6z - 5 = 0 . . . . . . . \left(1\right)$

Similarly, for side $AC$ we get,

$\left(x + 3\right) \times \left(- 6\right) + \left(y - 0\right) \times 0 + \left(z - \dfrac{3}{2}\right)\left(- 3\right) = 0$

$⇒ 4x + 2z + 9 = 0 . . . . . . . . . \left(2\right)$

Similarly, for side $AB$ we get,

$⇒ \left(x + 3\right) \times \left(- 6\right) + \left(y + 1\right) \times 2 + \left(z - 0\right) \times 0 = 0$

$⇒ 3x - y + 8 = 0 . . . . . . . . . \left(3\right)$

Now from equation $\left(1\right), \left(2\right) \text{ and } \left(3\right)$ we get,

$x = \dfrac{- 9}{4} - \dfrac{z}{2}, y = \dfrac{5}{4} - \dfrac{3}{2}z, z = z$

Now using the relation between centroid, circumcentre and orthocentre, we get,

$⇒ G = \left(\dfrac{\alpha - \dfrac{9}{2} - z}{3}, \dfrac{\beta + \dfrac{5}{2} - 3z}{3}, \dfrac{\dfrac{6}{7} + 2z}{3}\right)$

$⇒ \left(- 2, - \dfrac{2}{3}, 1\right) = \left(\dfrac{\alpha - \dfrac{9}{2} - z}{3}, \dfrac{\beta + \dfrac{5}{2} - 3z}{3}, \dfrac{\dfrac{6}{7} + 2z}{3}\right)$

Now on comparing both side we get,

$⇒ z = \dfrac{15}{14}, \alpha = - \dfrac{3}{7}, \beta = - \dfrac{9}{7}$

$⇒ 98{\left(\alpha + \beta\right)}^{2} = 98 \times \dfrac{144}{49} = 288$

questions.q: If four distinct points with position vectors $\overset{\to}{a}, \overset{\to}{b}, \overset{\to}{c}$ and $\overset{\to}{d}$ are coplanar, then $[ \overset{\to}{a}\overset{\to}{b}\overset{\to}{c} ]$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Given that $\overset{\to}{a}, \overset{\to}{b}, \overset{\to}{c}, \overset{\to}{d}$ are coplanar.

$⇒ \overset{\to}{b} - \overset{\to}{a}, \overset{\to}{c} - \overset{\to}{a}, \overset{\to}{d} - \overset{\to}{a}$ are also coplanar.

$⇒ \left[\begin{cases}\overset{\to}{b} - \overset{\to}{a} & \overset{\to}{c} - \overset{\to}{a} & \overset{\to}{d} - \overset{\to}{a}\end{cases}\right] = 0$

$⇒ \left(\overset{\to}{b} - \overset{\to}{a}\right) . \left(\left(\overset{\to}{c} - \overset{\to}{a}\right) \times \left(\overset{\to}{d} - \overset{\to}{a}\right)\right) = 0$

$⇒ \left(\overset{\to}{b} - \overset{\to}{a}\right) . \left(\overset{\to}{c} \times \overset{\to}{d} - \overset{\to}{c} \times \overset{\to}{a} - \overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{d}\right) = 0 ( Since\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{a} = 0 )$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{b} . \left(\overset{\to}{c} \times \overset{\to}{d}\right) - \overset{\to}{b} . \left(\overset{\to}{c} \times \overset{\to}{a}\right) - \overset{\to}{b} . \left(\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{d}\right) - \overset{\to}{a} . \left(\overset{\to}{c} \times \overset{\to}{d}\right) + \overset{\to}{a} . \left(\overset{\to}{c} \times \overset{\to}{a}\right) + \overset{\to}{a} . \left(\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{d}\right) = 0$

$⇒ \left[\begin{cases}\overset{\to}{b} & \overset{\to}{c} & \overset{\to}{d}\end{cases}\right] - \left[\begin{cases}\overset{\to}{b} & \overset{\to}{c} & \overset{\to}{a}\end{cases}\right] - \left[\begin{cases}\overset{\to}{b} & \overset{\to}{a} & \overset{\to}{d}\end{cases}\right] - \left[\begin{cases}\overset{\to}{a} & \overset{\to}{c} & \overset{\to}{d}\end{cases}\right] = 0$

We know that $\left[\begin{cases}\overset{\to}{x} & \overset{\to}{y} & \overset{\to}{z}\end{cases}\right] = \left[\begin{cases}\overset{\to}{y} & \overset{\to}{z} & \overset{\to}{x}\end{cases}\right] = \left[\begin{cases}\overset{\to}{z} & \overset{\to}{x} & \overset{\to}{y}\end{cases}\right]$ and $\left[\begin{cases}\overset{\to}{x} & \overset{\to}{y} & \overset{\to}{z}\end{cases}\right] = - \left[\begin{cases}\overset{\to}{x} & \overset{\to}{z} & \overset{\to}{y}\end{cases}\right]$

$⇒ \left[\begin{cases}\overset{\to}{b} & \overset{\to}{c} & \overset{\to}{d}\end{cases}\right] + \left[\begin{cases}\overset{\to}{a} & \overset{\to}{b} & \overset{\to}{d}\end{cases}\right] + \left[\begin{cases}\overset{\to}{a} & \overset{\to}{d} & \overset{\to}{c}\end{cases}\right] = \left[\begin{cases}\overset{\to}{a} & \overset{\to}{b} & \overset{\to}{c}\end{cases}\right]$

$⇒ \left[\begin{cases}\overset{\to}{c} & \overset{\to}{d} & \overset{\to}{b}\end{cases}\right] + \left[\begin{cases}\overset{\to}{b} & \overset{\to}{d} & \overset{\to}{a}\end{cases}\right] + \left[\begin{cases}\overset{\to}{d} & \overset{\to}{c} & \overset{\to}{a}\end{cases}\right] = \left[\begin{cases}\overset{\to}{a} & \overset{\to}{b} & \overset{\to}{c}\end{cases}\right]$

Hence, the required answer is $\left[\begin{cases}\overset{\to}{d} & \overset{\to}{c} & \overset{\to}{a}\end{cases}\right] + \left[\begin{cases}\overset{\to}{b} & \overset{\to}{d} & \overset{\to}{a}\end{cases}\right] + \left[\begin{cases}\overset{\to}{c} & \overset{\to}{d} & \overset{\to}{b}\end{cases}\right]$

$⇒ \left[\begin{cases}\overset{\to}{b} & \overset{\to}{c} & \overset{\to}{d}\end{cases}\right] - \left[\begin{cases}\overset{\to}{b} & \overset{\to}{c} & \overset{\to}{a}\end{cases}\right] - \left[\begin{cases}\overset{\to}{b} & \overset{\to}{a} & \overset{\to}{d}\end{cases}\right] - \left[\begin{cases}\overset{\to}{a} & \overset{\to}{c} & \overset{\to}{d}\end{cases}\right] = 0$

$⇒ \left[\begin{cases}\overset{\to}{b} & \overset{\to}{c} & \overset{\to}{d}\end{cases}\right] + \left[\begin{cases}\overset{\to}{a} & \overset{\to}{b} & \overset{\to}{d}\end{cases}\right] + \left[\begin{cases}\overset{\to}{a} & \overset{\to}{d} & \overset{\to}{c}\end{cases}\right] = \left[\begin{cases}\overset{\to}{a} & \overset{\to}{b} & \overset{\to}{c}\end{cases}\right]$

$⇒ \left[\begin{cases}\overset{\to}{c} & \overset{\to}{d} & \overset{\to}{b}\end{cases}\right] + \left[\begin{cases}\overset{\to}{b} & \overset{\to}{d} & \overset{\to}{a}\end{cases}\right] + \left[\begin{cases}\overset{\to}{d} & \overset{\to}{c} & \overset{\to}{a}\end{cases}\right] = \left[\begin{cases}\overset{\to}{a} & \overset{\to}{b} & \overset{\to}{c}\end{cases}\right]$

Hence, the required answer is $\left[\begin{cases}\overset{\to}{d} & \overset{\to}{c} & \overset{\to}{a}\end{cases}\right] + \left[\begin{cases}\overset{\to}{b} & \overset{\to}{d} & \overset{\to}{a}\end{cases}\right] + \left[\begin{cases}\overset{\to}{c} & \overset{\to}{d} & \overset{\to}{b}\end{cases}\right]$

questions.q: Let $\overset{\to}{a} = \overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}$ and $\overset{\to}{b} = \overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}$. If $\overset{\to}{c}$ is a vector such that $\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{c} = 11, \overset{\to}{b} \cdot \left(\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{c}\right) = 27$ and $\overset{\to}{b} \cdot \overset{\to}{c} =$- \sqrt{3} | \overset{\to}{b} |$, then $| \overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{c}{|}^{2}$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Given,

$\overset{\to}{a} = \overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}$, $\overset{\to}{b} = \overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}$, $\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{c} = 11$, $\overset{\to}{b} \cdot \left(\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{c}\right) = 27$ and $\overset{\to}{b} \cdot \overset{\to}{c} = - \sqrt{3}\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|$

Now finding, $\left(\overset{\to}{b} \times \overset{\to}{a}\right)$ we get,

$\left(\overset{\to}{b} \times \overset{\to}{a}\right) = \left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 1 & 1 & - 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 3\end{cases}\right| = 5\overset{^}{i} - 4\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$

Let $\overset{\to}{c} = {c}_{1}\overset{^}{i} + {c}_{2}\overset{^}{j} + {c}_{3}\overset{^}{k}$

Now solving, $\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{c} = 11$ we get,

${c}_{1} + 2{c}_{2} + 3{c}_{3} = 11 . . . . . . . \left(1\right)$

Now solving, $\overset{\to}{b} \cdot \overset{\to}{c} = - \sqrt{3}\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|$ we get,

${c}_{1} + {c}_{2} - {c}_{3} = - \sqrt{3}\sqrt{3}$

${c}_{1} + {c}_{2} - {c}_{3} = - 3 . . . . . . . . . . \left(2\right)$

Now solving $\left(\overset{\to}{b} \times \overset{\to}{a}\right) \cdot \overset{\to}{c} = 27$ we get,

$5{c}_{1} - 4{c}_{2} + {c}_{3} = 27 . . . . . . . . . . . \left(3\right)$

Now on solving equation $\left(1\right), \left(2\right) \text{ and } \left(3\right)$ we get,

$\overset{\to}{c} = 3\overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} + 4\overset{^}{k}$

Hence, ${\left|\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{c}\right|}^{2} = {\left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 3 & - 2 & + 4\end{cases}\right|}^{2}$= {\left|14\overset{^}{i} + 5\overset{^}{j} - 8\overset{^}{k}\right|}^{2}$

$⇒ | \overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{c}{|}^{2} = {14}^{2} + {5}^{2} + {8}^{2} = 285$

For any vector $\overset{\to}{a} = {a}_{1}\overset{^}{i} + {a}_{2}\overset{^}{j} + {a}_{3}\overset{^}{k}$, with $10\left|{a}_{i}\right| < 1, i = 1, 2, 3$, consider the following statements:
$\left(A\right)$ : $max\left\{\left|{a}_{1}\right|, \left|{a}_{2}\right|, \left|{a}_{3}\right|\right\} \le \left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|$
$\left(B\right)$ : $| \overset{\to}{a} | \le 3max\left\{\left|{a}_{1}\right|, \left|{a}_{2}\right|, \left|{a}_{3}\right|\right\}$
questions.solution:
Given,

$\overset{\to}{a} = {a}_{1}\overset{^}{i} + {a}_{2}\overset{^}{j} + {a}_{3}\overset{^}{k}$, with $10\left|{a}_{i}\right| < 1, i = 1, 2, 3$,

Let us assume that $\left|{a}_{1}\right| \le \left|{a}_{2}\right| \le \left|{a}_{3}\right|$

Now we know that,

${\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|}^{2} = {\left|\overset{\to}{a}1\right|}^{2} + {\left|\overset{\to}{a}2\right|}^{2} + {\left|\overset{\to}{a}3\right|}^{2}$

Given,

$\overset{\to}{a}$ be a non-zero vector parallel to the line of intersection of the two planes described by $\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j}, \overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{k}$,

So finding the normal vector to the above plane, we get,

And normal vector to planes $\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j}, \overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}$ will be,

$\overset{\to}{n}2 = \left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 1 & - 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & - 1\end{cases}\right| = \overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$

Now $\overset{\to}{a} = \lambda\left(\overset{\to}{n}1 \times \overset{\to}{n}2\right)$

So, direction ratio of $\overset{\to}{a} = \left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 1 & - 1 & - 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 1\end{cases}\right|= - 2\overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}$

Hence, direction ratio of $\overset{\to}{a} = \left(0, - 2, 2\right) = \left(0, - 1, 1\right)$

Now given, $\overset{\to}{b} = 2\overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$

And $\overset{\to}{a} = \lambda ( - \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k} )$

So, $\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{b} = 6 = \lambda ( 2 + 1 )$

$⇒ \lambda = 2$

$∴ \overset{\to}{a} = - 2\overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}$

questions.q: Let $\overset{\to}{a} = 2\overset{^}{i} + 7\overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}, \overset{^}{b} = 3\overset{^}{i} + 5\overset{^}{k}$ and $\overset{\to}{c} = \overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}$  Let $\overset{\to}{d}$ be a vector which is perpendicular to both $\overset{\to}{a} and \overset{\to}{b}$, and $\overset{\to}{c} \cdot \overset{\to}{d} = 12$. Then $\left(- \overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}\right) \cdot \left(\overset{\to}{c} \times \overset{\to}{d}\right)  is equal to$
questions.solution:
Given,

$\overset{\to}{a} = 2\overset{^}{i} + 7\overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}, \overset{^}{b} = 3\overset{^}{i} + 5\overset{^}{k}$ and $\overset{\to}{c} = \overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}$

And $\overset{\to}{d}$ be a vector which is perpendicular to both $\overset{\to}{a} and \overset{\to}{b}$,

So, $\overset{\to}{d} = \lambda\left(\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b}\right)

Now finding, $\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b} = $\left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 2 & 7 & - 1 \\ 3 & 0 & 5\end{cases}\right|$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b} = 35\overset{^}{i} - 13\overset{^}{j} - 21\overset{^}{k}$

So, $\overset{\to}{d} = \lambda\left(35\overset{^}{i} - 13\overset{^}{j} - 21\overset{^}{k}\right)

Also given,

$\overset{\to}{c} \cdot \overset{\to}{d} = 12$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{c} \cdot \overset{\to}{d} = $\left(\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}\right) \cdot \lambda\left(35\overset{^}{i} - 13\overset{^}{j} - 21\overset{^}{k}\right)

$⇒ \lambda ( 35 + 13 - 42 ) = 12$

$⇒ \lambda = 2$

So, $\overset{\to}{c} \times \overset{\to}{d} = 2 \times $\left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 1 & - 1 & 2 \\ 35 & - 13 & - 21\end{cases}\right|$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{c} \times \overset{\to}{d} = 2\left(47\overset{^}{i} + 91\overset{^}{j} + 22\overset{^}{k}\right)

Now finding,

\left(- \overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}\right) \cdot \left(\overset{\to}{c} \times \overset{\to}{d}\right) = 2 \left(- \overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}\right)\left(47\overset{^}{i} + 91\overset{^}{j} + 22\overset{^}{k}\right)$

$⇒ \left(- \overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}\right) \cdot \left(\overset{\to}{c} \times \overset{\to}{d}\right) = 2 \left(- 47 + 91 - 22\right) = 44$

questions.q: An arc $PQ$ of a circle subtends a right angle at its centre $O$. The mid point of the arc $PQ$ is $R$. If $\overset{\to}{OP} = \overset{\to}{u}, \overset{\to}{OR} = \overset{\to}{v}$ and $\overset{\to}{OQ} = \alpha\overset{\to}{u} + \beta\overset{\to}{v}$, then $\alpha, {\beta}^{2}$, are the roots of the equation
questions.solution:
Given,

An arc $PQ$ of a circle subtends a right angle at its centre $O$. The mid point of the arc $PQ$ is $R$,

And $\overset{\to}{OP} = \overset{\to}{u}, \overset{\to}{OR} = \overset{\to}{v}$ and $\overset{\to}{OQ} = \alpha\overset{\to}{u} + \beta\overset{\to}{v}$,

So, plotting the diagram of the given value we get,

Now given, $\overset{\to}{OQ} = \alpha\overset{\to}{u} + \beta\overset{\to}{v}$

Where, $\overset{\to}{OR} = \overset{\to}{v}$ and $\overset{\to}{OP} = \overset{\to}{u}$

Now $\left|\overset{\to}{OP}\right| = \left|\overset{\to}{OQ}\right| = \text{radius}$, so $R$ will lie on angle bisector of $\overset{\to}{OQ} and \overset{\to}{OP}$

Now using the perpendicular condition we get,

$\overset{\to}{OQ} \cdot \overset{\to}{OP} = 0$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{OQ} \cdot \overset{\to}{OP} = \alpha{\left|\overset{\to}{u}\right|}^{2} + \beta \cdot \left(\overset{\to}{v} \cdot \overset{\to}{u}\right) = 0$

$⇒ \alpha{\left|\overset{\to}{u}\right|}^{2} + \beta \cdot \left(\left|\overset{\to}{v}\right|\left|\overset{\to}{u}\right|cos{45}^{°}\right) = 0$

$⇒ \alpha + \beta \cdot cos{45}^{°} = 0\left\{\text{as}\left|\overset{\to}{u}\right| = \left|\overset{\to}{v}\right| = \text{radius}\right\}$

$⇒ \alpha = \dfrac{- \beta}{\sqrt{2}}$

Now solving, $\overset{\to}{OQ} \cdot \overset{\to}{OR} = \left|\overset{\to}{OQ}\right|\left|\overset{\to}{OR}\right|cos{45}^{°} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}{r}^{2}$

$⇒ \left(\alpha\overset{\to}{v} + \beta\overset{\to}{v}\right) \cdot \left(\overset{\to}{v}\right) = \dfrac{{r}^{2}}{\sqrt{2}}$

$⇒ \alpha \cdot \dfrac{{r}^{2}}{\sqrt{2}} + \beta \cdot {r}^{2} = \dfrac{{r}^{2}}{\sqrt{2}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{\alpha}{\sqrt{2}} + \beta = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

$⇒ \beta = \sqrt{2} \left\{\text{as}\alpha = \dfrac{- \beta}{\sqrt{2}}\right\}$

So, $\alpha = - 1$

Now finding the equation with roots $\alpha = - 1, {\beta}^{2} = 2$ we get, ${x}^{2} - x - 2 = 0$

If the position vectors of the points $A, B$ and $C$ are $- 2\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} - 3k, 2\overset{^}{i} + 4\overset{^}{j} - 2k$ and $- 4\overset{^}{i} ^ + 2\overset{^}{j} - k$ respectively, then the projection of the vector $\overset{\to}{OP}$ on a vector perpendicular to the vectors $\overset{\to}{AB}$ and $\overset{\to}{AC}$ is
questions.solution:
Given,

$O$ be the origin and the position vector of the point $P$ be $- \overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}$,

So, $\overset{\to}{OP} = - \overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}$

Also given the position vectors of the points $A, B$ and $C$ are $- 2\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} - 3\overset{^}{k}, 2\overset{^}{i} + 4\overset{^}{j} - 2\overset{^}{k}$ and $- 4\overset{^}{i} ^ + 2\overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}$

Now finding,

$\overset{\to}{AB} = 4\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$

$\overset{\to}{AC} = - 2\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}$

And $\overset{\to}{AB} \times \overset{\to}{AC} = \left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 4 & 3 & 1 \\ - 2 & 1 & 2\end{cases}\right|$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{AB} \times \overset{\to}{AC} = 5 \overset{^}{i} - 10 \overset{^}{j} + 10 \overset{^}{k}$

Now finding the Projection of $\overset{\to}{OP}$ on vector perpendicular to $\overset{\to}{AB} \text{ and } \overset{\to}{AC}$ we get,

Projection$= \left|\dfrac{\overset{\to}{OP} \cdot \left(\overset{\to}{AB} \times \overset{\to}{AC}\right)}{\left|\overset{\to}{AB} \times \overset{\to}{AC}\right|}\right|$

$= \dfrac{5\left(- \overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}\right)\left(\overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}\right)}{5\sqrt{1 + 4 + 4}}$= 3$

questions.q: Let the vectors $\overset{\to}{{u}_{1}} = \overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + a\overset{^}{k}, \overset{\to}{{u}_{2}} = \overset{^}{i} + b\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k},$ and $\overset{\to}{{u}_{3}} = c\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$ be coplanar. If the vectors $\overset{\to}{{v}_{1}} = \left(a + b\right)\overset{^}{i} + c\overset{^}{j} + c\overset{^}{k}, \overset{\to}{{v}_{2}} = a\overset{^}{i} + \left(b + c\right)\overset{^}{j} + a\overset{^}{k}$ and  $\overset{\to}{v}3 = b\overset{^}{i} + b\overset{^}{j} + \left(c + a\right)\overset{^}{k}$ are also coplanar, then $6\left(a + b + c\right)$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Given: $\overset{\to}{u}1 = \overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + a\overset{^}{k}, \overset{\to}{u}2 = \overset{^}{i} + b\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$ and $\overset{\to}{u}3 = c\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$ are coplanar.

Also given that,$\overset{\to}{v}1 = \left(a + b\right)\overset{^}{i} + c\overset{^}{j} + c\overset{^}{k}, \overset{\to}{v}2 = a\overset{^}{i} + \left(b + c\right)\overset{^}{j} + a\overset{^}{k}$and $\overset{\to}{v}3 = b\overset{^}{i} + b\overset{^}{j} + \left(c + a\right)\overset{^}{k}$ are coplanar.

Now, using the condition of coplanar we get,

$⇒ \left|\begin{cases}1 & 1 & a \\ 1 & b & 1 \\ c & 1 & 1\end{cases}\right| = 0$

Expanding the determinant along ${R}_{1}$.

$⇒ \left(b - 1\right) - \left(1 - c\right) + a\left(1 - bc\right) = 0$

$⇒ a + b + c = 2 + abc . . . . . \left(i\right)$

Again using the coplanar condition we get,

$⇒ \left|\begin{cases}a + b & c & c \\ a & b + c & a \\ b & b & c + a\end{cases}\right| = 0$

Apply row transformations, $\left({R}_{3} \to {R}_{3} - \left({R}_{1} + {R}_{2}\right)\right)$

$⇒ \left|\begin{cases}a + b & c & c \\ a & b + c & a \\ - 2a & - 2c & 0\end{cases}\right| = 0$

Expand the determinant along ${R}_{1}$.

$⇒ \left(a + b\right)\left(0 + 2ac\right) - c\left(0 + 2{a}^{2}\right) + c\left(- 2ac + 2a\left(b + c\right)\right) = 0$

$⇒ 2{a}^{2}c + 2abc - 2{a}^{2}c - 2a{c}^{2} + 2abc + 2a{c}^{2} = 0$

$⇒ abc = 0$

$∴ a + b + c = 2$ (From eq $\left(i\right)$)

$∴ 6\left(a + b + c\right) = 12$

Hence this is the correct option.

questions.q: The area of the quadrilateral $ABCD$ with vertices $A ( 2, 1, 1 ) , B ( 1, 2, 5 ) , C ( - 2, - 3, 5 )$ and $D ( 1, - 6, - 7 )$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Given,

The quadrilateral $ABCD$ with vertices $A ( 2, 1, 1 ) , B ( 1, 2, 5 ) , C ( - 2, - 3, 5 )$ and $D ( 1, - 6, - 7 )$

Now finding, $\overset{\to}{AB} = - \overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + 4\overset{^}{k}$ and $\overset{\to}{AD} = - \overset{^}{i} - 7\overset{^}{j} - 8\overset{^}{k}$

And plotting the diagram we get,

Now we know that,

Area of $∆ ABD$ is given by,

$= \dfrac{1}{2}\left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ - 1 & 1 & 4 \\ - 1 & - 7 & 8\end{cases}\right|$

$= | 10\overset{^}{i} - 6\overset{^}{j} + 4\overset{^}{k} | = 2\sqrt{38}$

Now finding, $\overset{\to}{CB} = 3\overset{^}{i} + 5\overset{^}{j}$ and $\overset{\to}{CD} = 3\overset{^}{i} - 3\overset{^}{j} - 12\overset{^}{k}$
So, Area of $∆ CBD = \dfrac{1}{2}\left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 3 & - 3 & - 12 \\ 3 & 5 & 0\end{cases}\right|$

$= | 6 ( 5\overset{^}{i} - 3\overset{^}{j} - 2\overset{^}{k} ) |$

$= 6\sqrt{38}$
$∴$ Area of quadrilateral $ABCD = 8\sqrt{38}$ square units

questions.q: If the points with position vectors  $\alpha\overset{^}{i} + 10\overset{^}{j} + 13\overset{^}{k}, 6\overset{^}{i} + 11\overset{^}{j} + 11\overset{^}{k}, \dfrac{9}{2}\overset{^}{i} + \beta\overset{^}{j} - 8\overset{^}{k}$ are collinear, then ${\left(19\alpha - 6\beta\right)}^{2}$ is equal to
questions.solution:
The given position vectors can be written as

  • $A ( \alpha, 10, 13 )$
  • $B ( 6, 11, 11 )$
  • $C\left(\dfrac{9}{2}, \beta, - 8\right)$

Also given that these three points are collinear.

Let us assume that the point $B$ divides $AB, BC$ in the ratio $k: 1$.

Since, $A, B, C$ are collinear

On applying section formula for $z$ co-ordinate we get,

$11 = \dfrac{- 8k + 13}{k + 1}$

$⇒ 11k + 11 = - 8k + 13$

$⇒ 19k = 2$

$⇒ k = \dfrac{2}{19}$

$∴$Ratio$= 2: 19$

Now, $\dfrac{\alpha \times 19 + \left(\dfrac{9}{2}\right) \times 2}{2 + 19} = 6$

$⇒ 19\alpha = 117$

$⇒ \alpha = \dfrac{117}{19}$

Now similarly, $\dfrac{2\beta + 190}{21} = 11$

$⇒ \beta = \dfrac{41}{2}$

$∴ {\left(19\alpha - 6\beta\right)}^{2} = {\left(117 - 123\right)}^{2} = 36$

Hence this is the correct option.

questions.q: Let $\overset{\to}{a} = 6\overset{^}{i} + 9\overset{^}{j} + 12\overset{^}{k}, \overset{\to}{b} = \alpha\overset{^}{i} + 11\overset{^}{j} - 2\overset{^}{k}$ and $\overset{\to}{c}$ be vectors such that $\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{c} = \overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b}$ If $\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{c} = - 12,$ and $\overset{\to}{c} \cdot \left(\overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}\right) = 5$ then $\overset{\to}{c} \cdot \left(\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}\right)$ is equal to $_______$
questions.solution:
Given,

$\overset{\to}{a} = 6\overset{^}{i} + 9\overset{^}{j} + 12\overset{^}{k}, \overset{\to}{b} = \alpha\overset{^}{i} + 11\overset{^}{j} - 2\overset{^}{k}$ and $\overset{\to}{c}$ be vectors such that $\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{c} = \overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b}$,

$\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{c} - \overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b} = 0$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{a} \times \left(\overset{\to}{c} - \overset{\to}{b}\right) = 0$

So, $\overset{\to}{a} \text{ and } \left(\overset{\to}{c} - \overset{\to}{b}\right)$ are parallel vectors,

Hence, $\lambda\overset{\to}{a} = \overset{\to}{c} - \overset{\to}{b}$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{c} = \overset{\to}{b} + \lambda\overset{\to}{a}$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{c} = \overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{b} + \lambda{\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|}^{2}$

$⇒ - 12 = \left(6\alpha + 75\right) + \lambda\left(261\right)$

$⇒ 2\alpha + 87\lambda = - 29 . . . . ( i )$

Now again using $\overset{\to}{c} = \overset{\to}{b} + \lambda\overset{\to}{a}$ we get,

$\overset{\to}{c} = \overset{^}{i}\left(\alpha + 6\lambda\right) + \overset{^}{j} ( 11 + 9\lambda ) + \overset{^}{k} ( - 2 + 12\lambda )$

Also given $\overset{\to}{c} \cdot \left(\overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}\right) = 5$

$⇒ \left(\alpha + 6\lambda\right) - 2 ( 11 + 9\lambda ) + ( - 2 + 12\lambda ) = 5$

$⇒ \alpha = 29$

So, $2\alpha + 87\lambda = - 29$

$⇒ \lambda = - 1$

Hence, $\overset{\to}{c} = 23\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} - 14\overset{^}{k}$

So, the value of $\overset{\to}{c} \cdot ( \overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k} ) = 23 + 2 - 14 = 11$

questions.q: Let the vectors $\overset{\to}{a}, \overset{\to}{b}, \overset{\to}{c}$ represent three coterminous edges of a parallelopiped of volume $V$. Then the volume of the parallelopiped, whose coterminous edges are represented by $\overset{\to}{a}, \overset{\to}{b} + \overset{\to}{c}$ and $\overset{\to}{a} + 2\overset{\to}{b} + 3\overset{\to}{c}$ is equal to
questions.solution:
We know that,

Volume of parallelepiped whose edges determined by vectors $\overset{\to}{a}, \overset{\to}{b}, \overset{\to}{c}$ is $\left[\begin{cases}\overset{\to}{a} & \overset{\to}{b} & \overset{\to}{c}\end{cases}\right]$.

Now it is given that $V$ is volume of parallelepiped $\overset{\to}{a}, \overset{\to}{b}, \overset{\to}{c}$, so required volume of parallelepiped with new edges will be

$= \left[\begin{cases}\overset{\to}{a} & \overset{\to}{b} + \overset{\to}{c} & \overset{\to}{a} + 2\overset{\to}{b} + 3\overset{\to}{c}\end{cases}\right]$

$= \left|\begin{cases}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 3\end{cases}\right|\left[\begin{cases}\overset{\to}{a} & \overset{\to}{b} & \overset{\to}{c}\end{cases}\right]$

$= \left\{\left(1\right)\left(3 - 2\right) - 0 + 0\right\}\left[\begin{cases}\overset{\to}{a} & \overset{\to}{b} & \overset{\to}{c}\end{cases}\right]$

$= \left[\begin{cases}\overset{\to}{a} & \overset{\to}{b} & \overset{\to}{c}\end{cases}\right]$

$= V$

Hence this is the correct option.

$= \left[\begin{cases}\overset{\to}{a} & \overset{\to}{b} & \overset{\to}{c}\end{cases}\right]$

questions.q: The sum of all values of $\alpha$, for which the points whose position vectors are $\overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}, 2\overset{^}{i} - 3\overset{^}{j} + 4\overset{^}{k}, \left(\alpha + 1\right)\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{k}$ and $9\overset{^}{i} + \left(\alpha - 8\right)\overset{^}{j} + 6\overset{^}{k}$ are coplanar, is equal to
questions.solution:
Let the given vectors be $\overset{\to}{A} = \overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}, \overset{\to}{B} = 2\overset{^}{i} - 3\overset{^}{j} + 4\overset{^}{k}, \overset{\to}{C} = \left(\alpha + 1\right)\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{k}and\overset{\to}{D} = 9\overset{^}{i} + \left(\alpha - 8\right)\overset{^}{j} + 6\overset{^}{k}$

We know that if the vectors are coplanar then $\left[\begin{cases}\overset{\to}{AB} & \overset{\to}{AC} & \overset{\to}{AD}\end{cases}\right] = 0$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{AB} = \left(2\overset{^}{i} - 3\overset{^}{j} + 4\overset{^}{k}\right) - \left(\overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}\right) = \overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{AC} = \left(\left(\alpha + 1\right)\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{k}\right) - \left(\overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}\right) = \alpha\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{AD} = \left(9\overset{^}{i} + \left(\alpha - 8\right)\overset{^}{j} + 6\overset{^}{k}\right) - \left(\overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}\right) = 8\overset{^}{i} + \left(\alpha - 6\right)\overset{^}{j} + 3k$

Now,

$⇒ \left|\begin{cases}1 & - 1 & 1 \\ \alpha & 2 & - 1 \\ 8 & \alpha - 6 & 3\end{cases}\right| = 0$

$⇒ 1\left(6 + \alpha - 6\right) + \left(3\alpha + 8\right) + \left({\alpha}^{2} - 6\alpha - 16\right) = 0$

On Simplifying we get,

$⇒ {\alpha}^{2} - 2\alpha - 8 = 0$

Therefore, sum of the roots is $- \left(- 2\right) = 2$.

questions.solution:
Given that:

$A ( 5, 5, 2\lambda )$, $B\left(1, 2, 3\right)$, $C\left(- 2, \lambda, 4\right)$ and

$D\left(- 1, 5, 6\right)$.

Now,

$\overset{\to}{AB} ≡ ( - 4, - 3, 3 - 2\lambda )$

$\overset{\to}{AC} ≡ ( - 7, \lambda - 5, 4 - 2\lambda )$

$\overset{\to}{AD} ≡ ( - 6, 0, 6 - 2\lambda )$

Given that $A, B, C\text{and}D$ are coplanar.

$∴ [ \overset{\to}{AB}\overset{\to}{AC}\overset{\to}{AD} ] = 0$

$⇒ \left|\begin{cases}- 4 & - 3 & 3 - 2\lambda \\ - 7 & \lambda - 5 & 4 - 2\lambda \\ - 6 & 0 & 6 - 2\lambda\end{cases}\right| = 0$

Expand the determinant along the first row.

$⇒ - 4\left[\left(\lambda - 5\right)\left(6 - 2\lambda\right) - 0\right] - \left(- 3\right)\left[- 7\left(6 - 2\lambda\right) - \left(- 6\right)\left(4 - 2\lambda\right)\right] + \left(3 - 2\lambda\right)\left[0 - \left(- 6\right)\left(\lambda - 5\right)\right]$

On solving the above equation we get,

$∴ \lambda = 3, \lambda = 2$

We have two values of $\lambda$.

$⇒ \mathop{∑}_{\lambda \in s} ( \lambda + 2{)}^{2} = {\left(3 + 2\right)}^{2} + {\left(2 + 2\right)}^{2}$

$= 41$

Hence, $\mathop{∑}_{\lambda \in s} ( \lambda + 2{)}^{2} = 41$

questions.q: Let $\overset{\to}{a} = 2\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} + 4\overset{^}{k}, \overset{\to}{b} = \overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} - 2\overset{^}{k}$ and $\overset{\to}{c} = - \overset{^}{i} + 4\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k} .$ If $\overset{\to}{d}$ is a vector perpendicular to both $\overset{\to}{b}$ and $\overset{\to}{c},$ and $\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{d} = 18,$ then $| \overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{d}{|}^{2}$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Given that,

$\overset{\to}{a} = 2\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} + 4\overset{^}{k}, \overset{\to}{b} = \overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} - 2\overset{^}{k}$ and $\overset{\to}{c} = - \overset{^}{i} + 4\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k} .$

Let us find $\overset{\to}{b} \times \overset{\to}{c}$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{b} \times \overset{\to}{c} = \left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 1 & - 2 & - 2 \\ - 1 & 4 & 3\end{cases}\right|$

$= \left(- 6 + 8\right)\overset{^}{i} - \left(3 - 2\right)\overset{^}{j} + \left(4 - 2\right)\overset{^}{k}$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{b} \times \overset{\to}{c} = 2\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}$

Since $\overset{\to}{d}$ is perpendicular to both $\overset{\to}{b}\text{and}\overset{\to}{c}$

$∴ \overset{\to}{d} = \lambda ( 2\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k} )$

Also $\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{d} = 18$

$⇒ \lambda\left(2\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} + 4\overset{^}{k}\right) . ( 2\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k} ) = 18$

$⇒ 9\lambda = 18$

$⇒ \lambda = 2$

Now let us apply LaGrange's identity which is as follows,

$∴ | \overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{d}{|}^{2} = | \overset{\to}{a}{|}^{2} \cdot | \overset{\to}{d}{|}^{2} - ( \overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{d}{)}^{2}$

$= {\left|2\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} + 4\overset{^}{k}\right|}^{2}{\left|4\overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} + 4\overset{^}{k}\right|}^{2} - {\left(18\right)}^{2}$

$= 720$

questions.q: Let $\overset{\to}{a} = 5\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} - 3\overset{^}{k}$ and $\overset{\to}{b} = \overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} + 5\overset{^}{k}$ be two vectors. Then which one of the following statements is TRUE?
options: Projection of $\overset{\to}{a}$ on $\overset{\to}{b}$ is $\dfrac{- 13}{\sqrt{35}}$ and the direction of the projection vector is opposite to the direction of $\overset{\to}{b}$
Projection of $\overset{\to}{a}$ on $\overset{\to}{b}$ is $\dfrac{- 17}{\sqrt{35}}$ and the direction of the projection vector is opposite to the direction of $\overset{\to}{b}$
Projection of $\overset{\to}{a}$ on $\overset{\to}{b}$ is $\dfrac{17}{\sqrt{35}}$ and the direction of the projection vector is opposite to the direction of $\overset{\to}{b}$
Projection of $\overset{\to}{a}$ on $\overset{\to}{b}$ is $\dfrac{13}{\sqrt{35}}$ and the direction of the projection vector is opposite to the direction of $\overset{\to}{a}$
questions.solution:
Given

$\overset{\to}{a} = 5\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} - 3\overset{^}{k}$

So, $\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right| = \sqrt{{5}^{2} + {1}^{2} + {3}^{2}} = \sqrt{35}$

$\overset{\to}{b} = \overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} + 5\overset{^}{k}$

So, $\sqrt{{5}^{2} + {1}^{2} + {3}^{2}} = \sqrt{35}$

So, $\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{b} = 5 - 3 - 15 = - 13$

Now finding the projection of $\overset{\to}{a}$ on $\overset{\to}{b}$ using the formula we get,

$\dfrac{\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{b}}{\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|} = - \dfrac{13}{\sqrt{35}}$

And projection of $\overset{\to}{b}$ on $\overset{\to}{a}$ is given by,

$\dfrac{\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{b}}{\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|} = - \dfrac{13}{\sqrt{35}}$

If $\overset{\to}{r}$ is a vector such that $\overset{\to}{r} \times \overset{\to}{a} = \overset{\to}{c} \times \overset{\to}{a}$ and $\overset{\to}{r} \cdot \overset{\to}{b} = 0$, then $| \overset{\to}{r} |$ is equal to:
questions.solution:
Given data as below:

$\overset{\to}{a} = 2\overset{^}{i} - 7\overset{^}{j} + 5\overset{^}{k}$

$\overset{\to}{b} = \overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{k}$

$\overset{\to}{c} = \overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} - 3\overset{^}{k}$

Given, $\overset{\to}{r} \times \overset{\to}{a} = \overset{\to}{c} \times \overset{\to}{a}$

$⇒ ( \overset{\to}{r} - \overset{\to}{c} ) \times \overset{\to}{a} = 0$

It means $( \overset{\to}{r} - \overset{\to}{c} )$ is parallel to $\overset{\to}{a}$,

$∴ \overset{\to}{r} = \overset{\to}{c} + \lambda\overset{\to}{a} . . . . . . . ( 1 )$

Given, $\overset{\to}{r} \cdot \overset{\to}{b} = 0$

From equation (1),

$\left(\overset{\to}{c} + \lambda\overset{\to}{a}\right) \cdot \overset{\to}{b} = 0$

$⇒ \left(\overset{\to}{c} \cdot \overset{\to}{b}\right) + \lambda\left(\overset{\to}{b} \cdot \overset{\to}{a}\right) = 0$

$⇒ - 2 + \lambda ( 7 ) = 0 ⇒ \lambda = \dfrac{2}{7}$

On putting values in equation (1) we get,

$∴ \overset{\to}{r} = \overset{\to}{c} + \dfrac{2}{7}\overset{\to}{a} = \dfrac{1}{7} ( 11\overset{^}{i} - 11\overset{^}{k} )$

$| \overset{\to}{r} | = \dfrac{11\sqrt{2}}{7}$

questions.q: Let $\overset{\to}{v} = \alpha\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} - 3\overset{^}{k}, \overset{\to}{w} = 2\alpha\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}$, and $\overset{\to}{u}$ be a vector such that $\left|\overset{\to}{u}\right| = \alpha > 0$. If the minimum value of the scalar triple product $\left[\overset{\to}{u}\overset{\to}{v}\overset{\to}{w}\right]$ is $- \alpha\sqrt{3401}$, and ${\left|\overset{\to}{u} . \overset{^}{i}\right|}^{2} = \dfrac{m}{n}$ where $m and n$ are coprime natural numbers, then $m + n$ is equal to _____ .
questions.solution:
We have,

$\left[\overset{\to}{u}\overset{\to}{v}\overset{\to}{w}\right] = \overset{\to}{u} \cdot \left(\overset{\to}{v} \times \overset{\to}{w}\right)

Now,

$min$\left(\left[\overset{\to}{u}\overset{\to}{v}\overset{\to}{w}\right]$\right) = - \alpha\sqrt{3401}$

$⇒ - $\left|\overset{\to}{u}\right|\left|\overset{\to}{v} \times \overset{\to}{w}\right|$ = - \alpha\sqrt{3401}$

$⇒ \alpha$\left|\overset{\to}{v} \times \overset{\to}{w}\right| = \alpha\sqrt{3401}$

$⇒ \left|\overset{\to}{v} \times \overset{\to}{w}\right|$ = \sqrt{3401}$

$⇒ $\left|\left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ \alpha & 2 & - 3 \\ 2\alpha & 1 & - 1\end{cases}\right|$\right| = \sqrt{3401}$

$⇒ $\left|\overset{^}{i} - 5\alpha\overset{^}{j} - 3\alpha\overset{^}{k}\right| = \sqrt{3401}$

$⇒ \sqrt{1 + 25{\alpha}^{2} + 9{\alpha}^{2}} = \sqrt{3401}$

$⇒ 34{\alpha}^{2} = 3400$

$⇒ {\alpha}^{2} = 100$

$⇒ \alpha = 10$ (as $\alpha > 0$)

So,

questions.q: $A\left(2, 6, 2\right), B\left(- 4, 0, \lambda\right), C\left(2, 3, - 1\right)$ and $D\left(4, 5, 0\right), \left|\lambda\right| \le 5$ are the vertices of a quadrilateral $ABCD$. If its area is $18$ square units, then $5 - 6\lambda$ is equal to _____ .
questions.solution:
Given:

$A\left(2, 6, 2\right), B\left(- 4, 0, \lambda\right), C\left(2, 3, - 1\right)D\left(4, 5, 0\right)$

Area of quadrilateral

$= \dfrac{1}{2}\left|\overset{\to}{AC} \times \overset{\to}{BD}\right| = 18$

$⇒ \left|\overset{\to}{AC} \times \overset{\to}{BD}\right|36$

Now,

$\overset{\to}{AC} \times \overset{\to}{BD} = \left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 0 & - 3 & - 3 \\ 8 & 5 & - \lambda\end{cases}\right|$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{AC} \times \overset{\to}{BD} = \left(3\lambda + 15\right)\overset{^}{i} - \left(0 + 24\right)\overset{^}{j} + \left(0 + 24\right)\overset{^}{k}$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{AC} \times \overset{\to}{BD} = \left(3\lambda + 15\right)\overset{^}{i} - 24\overset{^}{j} + 24\overset{^}{k}$

So,

$\left|\overset{\to}{AC} \times \overset{\to}{BD}\right| = 36$

$⇒ \sqrt{{\left(3\lambda + 15\right)}^{2} + {\left(24\right)}^{2} + {\left(24\right)}^{2}} = 36$

$⇒ 9{\lambda}^{2} + 225 + 90\lambda = 1296 - 1152$

$⇒ 9{\lambda}^{2} + 90\lambda - 81 = 0$

$= {\lambda}^{2} + 10\lambda + 9 = 0$

$⇒ \lambda = - 1, - 9$

Since,

$\left|\lambda\right| \le 5 ⇒ \lambda = - 1$

Therefore,

$5 - 6\lambda = 5 - 6\left(- 1\right) = 11$

If $\overset{\to}{r}$ is a vector such that, $\overset{\to}{r} \times \overset{\to}{b} = \overset{\to}{c} \times \overset{\to}{b}$ and $\overset{\to}{r} \cdot \overset{\to}{a} = 0$, then $25{\left|\overset{\to}{r}\right|}^{2}$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Given,

$\overset{\to}{r} \times \overset{\to}{b} = \overset{\to}{c} \times \overset{\to}{b}$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{r} \times \overset{\to}{b} - \overset{\to}{c} \times \overset{\to}{b} = 0$

$\left(\overset{\to}{r} - \overset{\to}{c}\right) \times \overset{\to}{b} = 0$

Hence, we can say that $\overset{\to}{r} - \overset{\to}{c}$ is parallel to vector $\overset{\to}{b}$,

Now let , $\overset{\to}{r} - \overset{\to}{c} = \lambda\overset{\to}{b}$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{r} = \overset{\to}{c} + \lambda\overset{\to}{b} . . . . . . \left(1\right)$

$∵ \overset{\to}{r} \cdot \overset{\to}{a} = 0 ⇒ \overset{\to}{c} \cdot \overset{\to}{a} + \lambda\left(\overset{\to}{b} \cdot \overset{\to}{a}\right) = 0$

$⇒ \lambda = \dfrac{- \overset{\to}{c} \cdot \overset{\to}{a}}{\overset{\to}{b} \cdot \overset{\to}{a}} = \dfrac{- 8}{5}$

Now putting the value of $\lambda$ in equation $\left(1\right)$ we get,

$\overset{\to}{r} = \overset{\to}{c} - \dfrac{8}{5}\overset{\to}{b} = \left(5\overset{^}{i} - 3\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}\right) - \dfrac{8}{5}\left(\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}\right)$

$⇒ 5\overset{\to}{r} = 17\overset{^}{i} - 7\overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}$

$⇒ 25{\left|\overset{\to}{r}\right|}^{2} = {\left(17\right)}^{2} + {\left(- 7\right)}^{2} + {\left(- 1\right)}^{2}$

$⇒ 25{\left|\overset{\to}{r}\right|}^{2} = 289 + 49 + 1 = 339$

questions.q: Let $\overset{\to}{a}, \overset{\to}{b}, \overset{\to}{c}$ be three vectors such that $\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right| = \sqrt{31}, 4\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right| = \left|\overset{\to}{c}\right| = 2$ and $2\left(\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b}\right) = 3\left(\overset{\to}{c} \times \overset{\to}{a}\right)$. If the angle between $\overset{\to}{b}$ and $\overset{\to}{c}$ is $\dfrac{2\pi}{3}$, then ${\left(\dfrac{\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{c}}{\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{b}}\right)}^{2}$ is equal to _____ .
questions.solution:
Given,

$\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right| = \sqrt{31}, 4\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right| = \left|\overset{\to}{c}\right| = 2$, $2\left(\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b}\right) = 3\left(\overset{\to}{c} \times \overset{\to}{a}\right)$ and angle between $\overset{\to}{b} \text{ and } \overset{\to}{c}$ is given as $\dfrac{2\pi}{3}$

Now solving, $3\left(\overset{\to}{c} \times \overset{\to}{a}\right) + 2\left(\overset{\to}{b} \times \overset{\to}{a}\right) = 0$

$⇒ \left(3\overset{\to}{c} \times 2\overset{\to}{b}\right) \times \overset{\to}{a} = 0$

Means $\left(3\overset{\to}{c} \times 2\overset{\to}{b}\right) \text{ and } \overset{\to}{a}$ are parallel vector,

So, let $3\overset{\to}{c} \times 2\overset{\to}{b} = \lambda\overset{\to}{a}$

Now squaring both sides we get,
$9{\left|\overset{\to}{c}\right|}^{2} + 4{\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|}^{2} + 12\left(\overset{\to}{b} \cdot \overset{\to}{c}\right) = {\lambda}^{2}{\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|}^{2}$

$⇒ 36 + 1 + 12 \times \dfrac{1}{2} \times 2\left(cos\left(2\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)\right) = {\lambda}^{2}\left(31\right)$

$⇒ {\lambda}^{2} = 1$

$⇒ \lambda = \pm 1$

Now putting the value of $\lambda$ in $\left(3\overset{\to}{c} \times 2\overset{\to}{b}\right) = \lambda\overset{\to}{a}$ we get,

$3\overset{\to}{c} + 2\overset{\to}{b} = \pm \overset{\to}{a} \ldots \left(1\right)$

Now taking dot product with $\overset{\to}{b}$ in above equation we get,

$3\left(\overset{\to}{b} \cdot \overset{\to}{c}\right) + 2\left(\overset{\to}{b} \cdot \overset{\to}{b}\right) = \pm \overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{b}$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{b} = \pm \left(- \dfrac{3}{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}\right) = \pm \left(- 1\right)$

$⇒ {\left(\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{b}\right)}^{2} = 1$

Again taking $3\left(\overset{\to}{c} \times \overset{\to}{a}\right) = 2\left(\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b}\right)$ and sqauring both side,

$⇒ {\left(\overset{\to}{c} \times \overset{\to}{a}\right)}^{2} = \dfrac{4}{9}{\left(\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b}\right)}^{2}$

$⇒ {\left(\overset{\to}{c} \times \overset{\to}{a}\right)}^{2} = \dfrac{4}{9}\left[{\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|}^{2}{\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|}^{2} - {\left(\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{b}\right)}^{2}\right]$

$⇒ {\left(\overset{\to}{c} \times \overset{\to}{a}\right)}^{2} = \dfrac{4}{9}\left[\dfrac{31}{4} - \left(1\right)\right]$

$⇒ {\left(\overset{\to}{c} \times \overset{\to}{a}\right)}^{2} = \dfrac{4}{9} \times \dfrac{27}{4} = 3$

Hence, the value of ${\left(\dfrac{\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{c}}{\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{b}}\right)}^{2} = \dfrac{3}{1} = 3$.

questions.q:
Let $\overset{\to}{a} = 2\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$, and $\overset{\to}{b} and \overset{\to}{c}$ be two nonzero vectors such that $\left|\overset{\to}{a} + \overset{\to}{b} + \overset{\to}{c}\right| = \left|\overset{\to}{a} + \overset{\to}{b} - \overset{\to}{c}\right|$ and \overset{\to}{b} \cdot \overset{\to}{c} = 0. Consider the $following two statement:

\left(A\right)\left|\overset{\to}{a} + \lambda\overset{\to}{c}\right| \ge \left|\overset{\to}{a}\right| for all$\lambda \in $\mathbb{R}$.

$\left(B\right) \overset{\to}{a}$ and $\overset{\to}{c}$ are always parallel
questions.solution:
Given,

$\left|\overset{\to}{a} + \overset{\to}{b} + \overset{\to}{c}\right| = \left|\overset{\to}{a} + \overset{\to}{b} - \overset{\to}{c}\right|

Now squaring both side we get,

$⇒ {$\left|\overset{\to}{a} + \overset{\to}{b} + \overset{\to}{c}\right|$}^{2} = {$\left|\overset{\to}{a} + \overset{\to}{b} - \overset{\to}{c}\right|$}^{2}$

$⇒ {$\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|$}^{2} + {$\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|$}^{2} + {$\left|\overset{\to}{c}\right|}^{2} + 2 \left(\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{b}\right) + 2 \left(\overset{\to}{b} \cdot \overset{\to}{c}\right) + 2 \left(\overset{\to}{c} \cdot \overset{\to}{a}\right) = {\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|$}^{2} + {$\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|}^{2} + {\left|\overset{\to}{c}\right|}^{2} + 2 \left(\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{b}\right) - 2\left(\overset{\to}{b} \cdot \overset{\to}{c}\right) - 2\left(\overset{\to}{c} \cdot \overset{\to}{a}\right)

$⇒ 2 $\left(\overset{\to}{b} \cdot \overset{\to}{c}\right)$ + 2 $\left(\overset{\to}{c} \cdot \overset{\to}{a}\right)$ = - 2 $\left(\overset{\to}{b} \cdot \overset{\to}{c}\right) + 2 \left(\overset{\to}{c} \cdot \overset{\to}{a}\right)

$⇒ 4$\left[\left(\overset{\to}{b} \cdot \overset{\to}{c}\right) + \left(\overset{\to}{c} \cdot \overset{\to}{a}\right)\right] = 0$

Now here given $\overset{\to}{b} \cdot \overset{\to}{c} = 0$, so

$\overset{\to}{c} \cdot \overset{\to}{a} = 0$ which means $\overset{\to}{c} \text{$ and $} \overset{\to}{a}$ are perpendicular vector, so statement $\left(B\right)$ is false,

Now statement $\left(A\right)$: $\left|\overset{\to}{a} + \lambda\overset{\to}{c}\right| \ge \left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|

$⇒ {$\left|\overset{\to}{a} + \lambda\overset{\to}{c}\right|$}^{2} \ge {$\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|$}^{2}$

$⇒ {$\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|$}^{2} + \lambda{$\left|\overset{\to}{c}\right|$}^{2} + 2$\left(\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{c}\right)$ \ge {$\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|$}^{2}$

$⇒ \lambda{$\left|\overset{\to}{c}\right|$}^{2} + 2$\left(\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{c}\right)$ \ge 0$

$⇒ \lambda{$\left|\overset{\to}{c}\right|$}^{2} \ge 0$

This is not always true, since $\lambda \in R$.

Hence, we can say that statement \left(A\right) is true$ and $statement \left(B\right) is false.

$

$⇒ {$\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|$}^{2} + {$\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|$}^{2} + {$\left|\overset{\to}{c}\right|}^{2} + 2 \left(\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{b}\right) + 2 \left(\overset{\to}{b} \cdot \overset{\to}{c}\right) + 2 \left(\overset{\to}{c} \cdot \overset{\to}{a}\right) = {\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|$}^{2} + {$\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|}^{2} + {\left|\overset{\to}{c}\right|}^{2} + 2 \left(\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{b}\right) - 2\left(\overset{\to}{b} \cdot \overset{\to}{c}\right) - 2\left(\overset{\to}{c} \cdot \overset{\to}{a}\right)

$⇒ 2 $\left(\overset{\to}{b} \cdot \overset{\to}{c}\right)$ + 2 $\left(\overset{\to}{c} \cdot \overset{\to}{a}\right)$ = - 2 $\left(\overset{\to}{b} \cdot \overset{\to}{c}\right) + 2 \left(\overset{\to}{c} \cdot \overset{\to}{a}\right)

$⇒ 4$\left[\left(\overset{\to}{b} \cdot \overset{\to}{c}\right) + \left(\overset{\to}{c} \cdot \overset{\to}{a}\right)\right] = 0$

Now here given $\overset{\to}{b} \cdot \overset{\to}{c} = 0$, so

$\overset{\to}{c} \cdot \overset{\to}{a} = 0$ which means $\overset{\to}{c} \text{$ and $} \overset{\to}{a}$ are perpendicular vector, so statement $\left(B\right)$ is false,

Now statement $\left(A\right)$: $\left|\overset{\to}{a} + \lambda\overset{\to}{c}\right| \ge \left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|

$⇒ {$\left|\overset{\to}{a} + \lambda\overset{\to}{c}\right|$}^{2} \ge {$\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|$}^{2}$

$⇒ {$\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|$}^{2} + \lambda{$\left|\overset{\to}{c}\right|$}^{2} + 2$\left(\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{c}\right)$ \ge {$\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|$}^{2}$

$⇒ \lambda{$\left|\overset{\to}{c}\right|$}^{2} + 2$\left(\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{c}\right)$ \ge 0$

$⇒ \lambda{$\left|\overset{\to}{c}\right|$}^{2} \ge 0$

This is not always true, since $\lambda \in R$.

Hence, we can say that statement \left(A\right) is true$ and $statement \left(B\right) is false.

questions.q: Let $\overset{\to}{a}$ and $\overset{\to}{b}$ be two vector such that $\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right| = \sqrt{14}, \left|\overset{\to}{b}\right| = \sqrt{6}$ and $\left|\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b}\right| = \sqrt{48}$. Then ${\left(\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{b}\right)}^{2}$ is equal to _____ .
questions.solution:
Given,

$\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right| = \sqrt{14}, \left|\overset{\to}{b}\right| = \sqrt{6} \text{$ and $} \left|\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b}\right| = \sqrt{48}$

Now we know that,

${\left|\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b}\right|}^{2} + {\left|\left(\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{b}\right)\right|}^{2} = {\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|}^{2}{\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|}^{2}\sin^{2}\theta + {\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|}^{2}{\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|}^{2}\cos^{2}\theta$

$⇒ {\left|\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b}\right|}^{2} + {\left|\left(\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{b}\right)\right|}^{2} = {\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|}^{2}{\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|}^{2}$

$\left\{\text{as}\cos^{2}\theta + \sin^{2}\theta = 1\right\}$

$⇒ 48 + {\left|\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{b}\right|}^{2} = 14 \times 6$

$⇒ {\left|\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{b}\right|}^{2} = 84 - 48 = 36$.

questions.q: Let $\lambda \in \mathbb{R}, \overset{\to}{a} = \lambda\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} - 3\overset{^}{k}, \overset{\to}{b} = \overset{^}{i} - \lambda\overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}$, If $( ( \overset{\to}{a} + \overset{\to}{b} ) \times ( \overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b} ) ) \times ( \overset{\to}{a} - \overset{\to}{b} ) = 8\overset{^}{i} - 40\overset{^}{j} - 24\overset{^}{k}$ then $| \lambda ( \overset{\to}{a} + \overset{\to}{b} ) \times ( \overset{\to}{a} - \overset{\to}{b} ) {|}^{2}$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Given,

$\overset{\to}{a} = \lambda\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} - 3\overset{^}{k}$

$\overset{\to}{b} = \overset{^}{i} - \lambda\overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}$

Also given,

$( ( \overset{\to}{a} + \overset{\to}{b} ) \times ( \overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b} ) ) \times ( \overset{\to}{a} - \overset{\to}{b} ) = 8\overset{^}{i} - 40\overset{^}{j} - 24\overset{^}{k}$

$⇒ ( \overset{\to}{b} - \overset{\to}{a} ) \times ( ( \overset{\to}{a} + \overset{\to}{b} ) \times ( \overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b} ) ) = 8\overset{^}{i} - 40\overset{^}{j} - 24\overset{^}{k}$

Now using vector triple product,

$\overset{\to}{A} \times ( \overset{\to}{B} \times \overset{\to}{C} ) = ( \overset{\to}{A} . \overset{\to}{C} ) \overset{\to}{B} - ( \overset{\to}{A} . \overset{\to}{B} ) \overset{\to}{C}$ we get,

$⇒ ( ( \overset{\to}{b} - \overset{\to}{a} ) \cdot ( \overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b} ) ) ( \overset{\to}{a} + \overset{\to}{b} ) - ( ( \overset{\to}{b} - \overset{\to}{a} ) \cdot ( \overset{\to}{a} + \overset{\to}{b} ) ) ( \overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b} ) = 8\overset{^}{i} - 40\overset{^}{j} - 24\overset{^}{k}$

$⇒ 0 + ( ( \overset{\to}{a} - \overset{\to}{b} ) \cdot ( \overset{\to}{a} + \overset{\to}{b} ) ) ( \overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b} ) = 8\overset{^}{i} - 40\overset{^}{j} - 24\overset{^}{k} . . . . . ( 1 )$

$( ( \overset{\to}{a} - \overset{\to}{b} ) \cdot ( \overset{\to}{a} + \overset{\to}{b} ) ) = \left[\left(\lambda - 1\right)\overset{^}{i} + \left(2 + \lambda\right)\overset{^}{j} - 5\overset{^}{k}\right] . \left[\left(\lambda + 1\right)\overset{^}{i} + \left(2 - \lambda\right)\overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}\right]$

$⇒ ( ( \overset{\to}{a} - \overset{\to}{b} ) \cdot ( \overset{\to}{a} + \overset{\to}{b} ) ) = 8$

From equation (1) we get,

$⇒ 8 ( \overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b} ) = 8\overset{^}{i} - 40\overset{^}{j} - 24\overset{^}{k}$

Now, $\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b} = \left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ \lambda & 2 & - 3 \\ 1 & - \lambda & 2\end{cases}\right|$

$= ( 4 - 3\lambda ) \overset{^}{i} - ( 2\lambda + 3 ) \overset{^}{j} + \left(- {\lambda}^{2} - 2\right)\overset{^}{k}$

$⇒ \lambda = 1$

$∴ \overset{\to}{a} = \overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} - 3\overset{^}{k}$

$\overset{\to}{b} = \overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{a} + \overset{\to}{b} = 2\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}, \overset{\to}{a} - \overset{\to}{b} = 3\overset{^}{j} - 5\overset{^}{k}$

$⇒ ( \overset{\to}{a} + \overset{\to}{b} ) \times ( \overset{\to}{a} - \overset{\to}{b} ) = \left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 2 & 1 & - 1 \\ 0 & 3 & - 5\end{cases}\right| = 2\overset{^}{i} + 10\overset{^}{j} + 6\overset{^}{k}$

$⇒ \left|( \overset{\to}{a} + \overset{\to}{b} ) \times ( \overset{\to}{a} - \overset{\to}{b} )\right| = \sqrt{4 + 100 + 36}$

Now,

${\left|\lambda ( \overset{\to}{a} + \overset{\to}{b} ) \times ( \overset{\to}{a} - \overset{\to}{b} )\right|}^{2} = {\lambda}^{2}{\left|( \overset{\to}{a} + \overset{\to}{b} ) \times ( \overset{\to}{a} - \overset{\to}{b} )\right|}^{2}$

$∴$ Required answer $= 4 + 100 + 36 = 140$

questions.q: If $\overset{\to}{a}, \overset{\to}{b}, \overset{\to}{c}$ are three non-zero vectors and $\overset{^}{n}$ is a unit vector perpendicular to $\overset{\to}{c}$ such that $\overset{\to}{a} = \alpha\overset{\to}{b} - \overset{^}{n}, \left(\alpha \ne 0\right)$ and $\overset{\to}{b} \cdot \overset{\to}{c} = 12$, then $\left|\overset{\to}{c} \times \left(\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b}\right)\right|$ is equal to:
questions.solution:
Given:

$\overset{\to}{a} = \alpha\overset{\to}{b} - \overset{^}{n}$ where, $\alpha \ne 0$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{c} = \alpha\left(\overset{\to}{b} \cdot \overset{\to}{c}\right) - \left(\overset{^}{n} \cdot \overset{\to}{c}\right)$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{c} = 12\alpha - 0$

Since, $\overset{^}{n} ⊥ \overset{\to}{c} ⇒ \left(\overset{^}{n} \cdot \overset{\to}{c}\right) = 0$.

Now,

$\overset{\to}{c} \times \left(\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b}\right) = \left(\overset{\to}{c} \cdot \overset{\to}{b}\right)\overset{\to}{a} - \left(\overset{\to}{c} \cdot \overset{\to}{a}\right)\overset{\to}{b}$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{c} \times \left(\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b}\right) = 12\overset{\to}{a} - 12\alpha\overset{\to}{b}$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{c} \times \left(\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b}\right) = 12\left(\overset{\to}{a} - \alpha\overset{\to}{b}\right)$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{c} \times \left(\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b}\right) = 12\left(- \overset{^}{n}\right)$

$⇒ \left|\overset{\to}{c} \times \left(\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b}\right)\right| = \left|12\left(- \overset{^}{n}\right)\right|$

$⇒ \left|\overset{\to}{c} \times \left(\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b}\right)\right| = 12\left|\left(- \overset{^}{n}\right)\right|$

$⇒ \left|\overset{\to}{c} \times \left(\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b}\right)\right| = 12$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\overset{\to}{a} = \overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{k}, \overset{\to}{b} = \overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}, \overset{\to}{c} = 7\overset{^}{i} - 3\overset{^}{j} + 4\overset{^}{k}, \overset{\to}{r} \times \overset{\to}{b} + \overset{\to}{b} \times \overset{\to}{c} = \overset{\to}{0}$ and $\overset{\to}{r} \cdot \overset{\to}{a} = 0$ then $\overset{\to}{r} . \overset{\to}{c}$ is equal to:
questions.solution:
Given,

$\overset{\to}{r} \times \overset{\to}{b} + \overset{\to}{b} \times \overset{\to}{c} = \overset{\to}{0}$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{r} \times \overset{\to}{b} - \overset{\to}{c} \times \overset{\to}{b} = \overset{\to}{0}$

$⇒ \left(\overset{\to}{r} - \overset{\to}{c}\right) \times \overset{\to}{b} = 0$

$⇒ \left(\overset{\to}{r} - \overset{\to}{c}\right) | | \overset{\to}{b}$

Therefore, $\overset{\to}{r} - \overset{\to}{c} = \lambda\overset{\to}{b}$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{r} = \overset{\to}{c} + \lambda\overset{\to}{b}$

Also,

$\overset{\to}{r} \cdot \overset{\to}{a} = 0$ (given)

$⇒ \left(\overset{\to}{c} + \lambda\overset{\to}{b}\right) \cdot \overset{\to}{a} = 0$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{c} \cdot \overset{\to}{a} + \lambda\overset{\to}{b} \cdot \overset{\to}{a} = 0$

$⇒ \lambda = \dfrac{- \overset{\to}{c} \cdot \overset{\to}{a}}{\overset{\to}{b} \cdot \overset{\to}{a}}$

Now,

questions.q: Let $\overset{\to}{a} = 4\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j}$ and $\overset{\to}{b} = 3\overset{^}{i} - 4\overset{^}{j} + 5\overset{^}{k}$  and $\overset{\to}{c}$ is a vector such that $\overset{\to}{c} \cdot ( \overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b} ) + 25 = 0, \overset{\to}{c} \cdot ( \overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k} ) = 4$ and projection of $\overset{\to}{c}$ on $\overset{\to}{a}$ is $1$ , then the projection of $\overset{\to}{c}$ on $\overset{\to}{b}$ equals:
questions.solution:
Given:

$\overset{\to}{a} = 4\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j}$

$\overset{\to}{b} = 3\overset{^}{i} - 4\overset{^}{j} + 5\overset{^}{k}$

So,

$\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b} = \left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 4 & 3 & 0 \\ 3 & - 4 & 5\end{cases}\right|$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b} = 15\overset{^}{i} - 20\overset{^}{j} - 25\overset{^}{k}$

Let $\overset{\to}{c} = x\overset{^}{i} + y\overset{^}{j} + z\overset{^}{k}$

Then,

$\overset{\to}{c} \cdot ( \overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b} ) + 25 = 0$

$⇒ 15x - 20y - 25z + 25 = 0$

$⇒ 3x - 4y - 5z = - 5 . . . \left(1\right)$

Also,

$\overset{\to}{c} \cdot \left(\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}\right) = 4$

$⇒ x + y + z = 4 . . . . \left(2\right)$

And projection of $\overset{\to}{c}$ on $\overset{\to}{a}$ is

$\dfrac{\overset{\to}{c} \cdot \overset{\to}{a}}{| \overset{\to}{a} |} = 1$

$⇒ \dfrac{\left(x\overset{^}{i} + y\overset{^}{j} + z\overset{^}{k}\right) \cdot \left(4\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j}\right)}{\sqrt{16 + 9}} = 1$

$⇒ 4x + 3y = 5 . . . . \left(3\right)$

Solving $\left(1\right), \left(2\right) \text{ and } \left(3\right)$, we get

$x = 2, y = - 1, z = 3$

So,

$\overset{\to}{c} = 2\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}$

Projection of $\overset{\to}{c}$ on $\overset{\to}{b}$ is

$\dfrac{\overset{\to}{c} \cdot \overset{\to}{b}}{\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|} = \dfrac{\left(2\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}\right) \cdot \left(3\overset{^}{i} - 4\overset{^}{j} + 5\overset{^}{k}\right)}{\sqrt{9 + 16 + 25}} = \dfrac{25}{5\sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{5}{\sqrt{2}}$

questions.solution:
Given,

$\overset{\to}{a} = \lambda\overset{^}{i} + \mu\overset{^}{j} + 4\overset{^}{k}, \overset{\to}{b} = - 2\overset{^}{i} + 4\overset{^}{j} - 2\overset{^}{k}$ and $\overset{\to}{c} = 2\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$ are coplanar

So, $\left|\begin{cases}\lambda & \mu & 4 \\ - 2 & 4 & - 2 \\ 2 & 3 & 1\end{cases}\right| = 0$

$⇒ \lambda ( 10 ) - \mu ( 2 ) + 4 ( - 14 ) = 0$

$⇒ 10\lambda - 2\mu = 56$

$⇒ 5\lambda - \mu = 28 . . . . . \left(1\right)$

And given projection of $\overset{\to}{a}$ on $\overset{\to}{b}$ is $\sqrt{54}$

$⇒ \dfrac{\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{b}}{| \overset{\to}{b} |} = \sqrt{54}$

$⇒ \dfrac{- 2\lambda + 4\mu - 8}{\sqrt{24}} = \sqrt{54}$

$⇒ - 2\lambda + 4\mu - 8 = \sqrt{54 \times 24} . . . . \left(2\right)$

By solving equation $\left(1\right) \text{ and } \left(2\right)$ we get,

$⇒ \lambda + \mu = 24$

questions.solution:

$\overset{\to}{a}, \overset{\to}{b}$ and $\overset{\to}{c}$ be three non-zero non-coplanar vectors,

So, $\overset{\to}{AB} = ( \lambda - 1 ) \overset{\to}{a} - 2\overset{\to}{b} + 3\overset{\to}{c}$

$\overset{\to}{AC} = - 2\overset{\to}{a} + 3\overset{\to}{b} - 4\overset{\to}{c}$

$\overset{\to}{AD} = \overset{\to}{a} - 3\overset{\to}{b} + 5\overset{\to}{c}$

Now using the condition of coplanar we get,

$\left|\begin{cases}\lambda - 1 & - 2 & 3 \\ - 2 & 3 & - 4 \\ 1 & - 3 & 5\end{cases}\right| = 0$

$⇒ ( \lambda - 1 ) ( 15 - 12 ) + 2 ( - 10 + 4 ) + 3 ( 6 - 3 ) = 0$

questions.solution:
Let

$\overset{\to}{b} = x\overset{^}{i} + y\overset{^}{j} + z\overset{^}{k}$

Then,

$\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b} = \left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ - 1 & - 1 & 1 \\ x & y & z\end{cases}\right|$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b} = - \left(y + z\right)\overset{^}{i} + \left(x + z\right)\overset{^}{j} + \left(x - y\right)\overset{^}{k}$

So,

$- \left(y + z\right)\overset{^}{i} + \left(x + z\right)\overset{^}{j} + \left(x - y\right)\overset{^}{k} = \overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + 0\overset{^}{k}$

Hence,

$y + z = - 1x + z = - 1x - y = 0 ⇒ x = y$

Also,

$\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{b} = 1$

$⇒ - x - y + z = 1$

$⇒ - 2x + z = 1$

$⇒ z = 2x + 1$

$⇒ - 1 - x = 2x + 1$

$⇒ 3x = - 2 ⇒ x = - \dfrac{2}{3}$

So, $y = - \dfrac{2}{3}; z = - \dfrac{1}{3}$

Hence,

$\overset{\to}{b} = - \dfrac{2}{3}\overset{^}{i} - \dfrac{2}{3}\overset{^}{j} - \dfrac{1}{3}\overset{^}{k}$

$⇒ 6\overset{\to}{b} = - 4\overset{^}{i} - 4\overset{^}{j} - 2\overset{^}{k}$

So,

$\overset{\to}{a} - 6\overset{\to}{b} = 3\left(\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}\right)$

questions.q: Let $\overset{\to}{a}, \overset{\to}{b}$ and $\overset{\to}{c}$ be three non zero vectors such that $\overset{\to}{b} \cdot \overset{\to}{c} = 0$ and $\overset{\to}{a} \times ( \overset{\to}{b} \times \overset{\to}{c} ) = \dfrac{\overset{\to}{b} - \overset{\to}{c}}{2}$. If $\overset{\to}{d}$ be a vector such that $\overset{\to}{b} \cdot \overset{\to}{d} = \overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{b}$, then $( \overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b} ) \cdot ( \overset{\to}{c} \times \overset{\to}{d} )$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Given,

$\overset{\to}{a} \times \left(\overset{\to}{b} \times \overset{\to}{c}\right) = \dfrac{\overset{\to}{b} - \overset{\to}{c}}{2}$

Using the vector triple cross product we have,

$\overset{\to}{a} \times \left(\overset{\to}{b} \times \overset{\to}{c}\right) = \left(\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{c}\right)\overset{\to}{b} - \left(\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{b}\right)\overset{\to}{c}$

So, $( \overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{c} ) \overset{\to}{b} - ( \overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{b} ) \overset{\to}{c} = \dfrac{\overset{\to}{b} - \overset{\to}{c}}{2}$

On comparing both sides we get,

$\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{c} = \dfrac{1}{2}, \overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{b} = \dfrac{1}{2}$

$∵ \overset{\to}{b} \cdot \overset{\to}{d} = \overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{b}$

$∴ \overset{\to}{b} \cdot \overset{\to}{d} = \dfrac{1}{2}$

Using vector cross-product formulae we have

$( \overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b} ) \cdot ( \overset{\to}{c} \times \overset{\to}{d} ) = \overset{\to}{a} \cdot ( \overset{\to}{b} \times ( \overset{\to}{c} \times \overset{\to}{d} ) )$

$= \overset{\to}{a} \cdot ( ( \overset{\to}{b} \cdot \overset{\to}{d} ) \overset{\to}{c} - ( \overset{\to}{b} \cdot \overset{\to}{c} ) \overset{\to}{d} ) \left(∵ \overset{\to}{b} \cdot \overset{\to}{c} = 0\right)

$= ( \overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{c} ) ( \overset{\to}{b} \cdot \overset{\to}{d} ) = $\dfrac{1}{2}$ \times $\dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{1}{4}

questions.question: Let $\overset{\to}{a}, \overset{\to}{b}$ and $\overset{\to}{c}$ be three non zero vectors such that $\overset{\to}{b} \cdot \overset{\to}{c} = 0$ and $\overset{\to}{a} \times ( \overset{\to}{b} \times \overset{\to}{c} ) = \dfrac{\overset{\to}{b} - \overset{\to}{c}}{2}$. If $\overset{\to}{d}$ be a vector such that $\overset{\to}{b} \cdot \overset{\to}{d} = \overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{b}$, then $( \overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b} ) \cdot ( \overset{\to}{c} \times \overset{\to}{d} )$ is equal to
questions.explanation:
Given,

$\overset{\to}{a} \times \left(\overset{\to}{b} \times \overset{\to}{c}\right) = \dfrac{\overset{\to}{b} - \overset{\to}{c}}{2}$

Using the vector triple cross product we have,

$\overset{\to}{a} \times \left(\overset{\to}{b} \times \overset{\to}{c}\right) = \left(\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{c}\right)\overset{\to}{b} - \left(\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{b}\right)\overset{\to}{c}$

So, $( \overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{c} ) \overset{\to}{b} - ( \overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{b} ) \overset{\to}{c} = \dfrac{\overset{\to}{b} - \overset{\to}{c}}{2}$

On comparing both sides we get,

$\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{c} = \dfrac{1}{2}, \overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{b} = \dfrac{1}{2}$

$∵ \overset{\to}{b} \cdot \overset{\to}{d} = \overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{b}$

$∴ \overset{\to}{b} \cdot \overset{\to}{d} = \dfrac{1}{2}$

Using vector cross-product formulae we have

$( \overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b} ) \cdot ( \overset{\to}{c} \times \overset{\to}{d} ) = \overset{\to}{a} \cdot ( \overset{\to}{b} \times ( \overset{\to}{c} \times \overset{\to}{d} ) )$

$= \overset{\to}{a} \cdot ( ( \overset{\to}{b} \cdot \overset{\to}{d} ) \overset{\to}{c} - ( \overset{\to}{b} \cdot \overset{\to}{c} ) \overset{\to}{d} ) \left(∵ \overset{\to}{b} \cdot \overset{\to}{c} = 0\right)

$= ( \overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{c} ) ( \overset{\to}{b} \cdot \overset{\to}{d} ) = $\dfrac{1}{2}$ \times $\dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{1}{4}

$

questions.solution:
Given,

The vector $\overset{\to}{a} = - \overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$ is rotated through a right angle, passing through the $y$-axis in its way and the resulting vector is $\overset{\to}{b}$

Now taking, $\overset{\to}{b} = \lambda\overset{\to}{a} \times \left(\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{^}{j}\right)$ {note here we have taken cross vector with $\overset{^}{j}$ as it is rotated along $y -$axis}

$⇒ \overset{\to}{b} = \lambda\left(- \overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}\right) \times \left(\left(- \overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}\right) \times \overset{^}{j}\right)$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{b} = \lambda\left(- \overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}\right) \times \left(- \overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{k}\right)$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{b} = \lambda\left(- 2\overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}\right)$

Also magnitude of both vector will be equal,

So,$\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right| = \left|\overset{\to}{a}\right| ⇒ \sqrt{6} = \sqrt{12}\left|\lambda\right|$

$⇒ \lambda = \pm \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

(Now $\lambda = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$ rejected $∵ \overset{\to}{b}$ makes acute angle with y axis )

So, $\overset{\to}{b} = - \sqrt{2}\left(- \overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}\right)$

Now projection of $3\overset{\to}{a} + \sqrt{2}\overset{\to}{b}$ on $\overset{\to}{c}$ is given by,

$\dfrac{\left(3\overset{\to}{a} + \sqrt{2b}\right) \cdot \overset{\to}{c}}{\left|\overset{\to}{c}\right|} = 3\sqrt{2}$

questions.q: Let $\overset{\to}{\alpha} = 4\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} + 5\overset{^}{k}$  and $\overset{\to}{\beta} = \overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} - 4\overset{^}{k}$. Let $\overset{\to}{\beta}1$ be parallel to $\overset{\to}{\alpha}$ and $\overset{\to}{\beta}2$ be perpendicular to $\overset{\to}{\alpha}$. If $\overset{\to}{\beta} = \overset{\to}{\beta}1 + \overset{\to}{\beta}2$, then the value of $5\overset{\to}{\beta}2 \cdot \left(\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}\right)$ is
questions.solution:
Given that $\overset{\to}{\alpha} = 4\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} + 5\overset{^}{k}$ and $\overset{\to}{\beta} = \overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} - 4\overset{^}{k} and \overset{\to}{\beta} = \overset{\to}{{\beta}_{1}} + \overset{\to}{{\beta}_{2}}$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{{\beta}_{2}} = \overset{\to}{\beta} - \overset{\to}{{\beta}_{1}} . . . . . . . . . . \left(1\right)

since $\overset{\to}{\beta}1$ is parallel to $\overset{\to}{\alpha}$, $\overset{\to}{{\beta}_{1}} = t\overset{\to}{\alpha}$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{{\beta}_{1}} = t $\left(4\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} + 5\overset{^}{k}\right) = 4t\overset{^}{i} + 3t\overset{^}{j} + 5t\overset{^}{k} . . . . . . . . . \left(2\right)

Substituting the $values of\overset{\to}{{\beta}_{1}} and \overset{\to}{\alpha} in ( 1 )$, we get$

$\overset{\to}{{\beta}_{2}} = \overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} - 4\overset{^}{k} - \left(4t\overset{^}{i} + 3t\overset{^}{j} + 5t\overset{^}{k}\right)$ = $\left(1 - 4t\right)\overset{^}{i} + \left(2 - 3t\right)\overset{^}{j} + \left(- 4 - 5t\right)\overset{^}{k} . . . . . . . . . . . . \left(3\right)

since $\overset{\to}{{\beta}_{2}}$ is perpendicular to $\overset{\to}{\alpha}$, so $\overset{\to}{{\beta}_{2}} \cdot \overset{\to}{\alpha} = 0$

$⇒ $\left[\left(1 - 4t\right)$\overset{^}{i} + $\left(2 - 3t\right)$\overset{^}{j} + $\left(- 4 - 5t\right)$\overset{^}{k}\right] \cdot $\left[4\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} + 5\overset{^}{k}\right]$ = 0$

$⇒ 4$\left(1 - 4t\right)$ + 3$\left(2 - 3t\right)$ + 5$\left(- 4 - 5t\right)$ = 0$

$⇒ 4 - 16t + 6 - 9t - 20 - 25t = 0$

$⇒ - 50t = 10⇒ t = $\dfrac{- 1}{5}

From \left(2\right)$ and $\left(3\right), we get$\overset{\to}{{\beta}_{1}} = $\dfrac{- 1}{5}\left(4\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} + 5\overset{^}{k}\right)$

$\overset{\to}{{\beta}_{2}} = \dfrac{9}{5}\overset{^}{i} + \dfrac{13}{5}\overset{^}{j} - 3\overset{^}{k} = \dfrac{1}{5}\left(9\overset{^}{i} + 13\overset{^}{j} - 15\overset{^}{k}\right)$

So, the $value of5\overset{\to}{\beta}2 \cdot \left(\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}\right) will be,$

$= 5 \times \dfrac{1}{5} ($ 9\overset{^}{i} + 13\overset{^}{j} - 15\overset{^}{k} ) \cdot $\left(\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}\right)$ = 9 + 13 - 15 = 7$

$

questions.q: Let $\overset{\to}{a} = \overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + \lambda\overset{^}{k}$, $\overset{\to}{b} = 3\overset{^}{i} - 5\overset{^}{j} - \lambda\overset{^}{k}$, $\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{c} = 7$, $2\left(\overset{\to}{b} \cdot \overset{\to}{c}\right) + 43 = 0$, $\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{c} = \overset{\to}{b} \times \overset{\to}{c}$, then $\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{b}$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Given:

$\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{c} = \overset{\to}{b} \times \overset{\to}{c}$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{c} - \overset{\to}{b} \times \overset{\to}{c} = 0$

$⇒ \left(\overset{\to}{a} - \overset{\to}{b}\right) \times \overset{\to}{c} = 0$

So, $\left(\overset{\to}{a} - \overset{\to}{b}\right) ∥ \overset{\to}{c}$, hence

$\overset{\to}{a} - \overset{\to}{b} = \mu\overset{\to}{c}$

where, $\mu$ is any scalar.

$⇒ - 2\overset{^}{i} + 7\overset{^}{j} + 2\lambda\overset{^}{k} = \mu\overset{\to}{c} . . . . \left(1\right)$

Taking dot product with $\overset{\to}{a}$, we get

$⇒ - 2 + 14 + 2{\lambda}^{2} = 7\mu$

$⇒ 7\mu = 2{\lambda}^{2} + 12 . . . \left(2\right)

Taking dot product$ with \overset{\to}{b} in $\left(1\right)$, we get

$- 6 - 35 - 2{\lambda}^{2} = - \dfrac{43}{2}\mu$

$⇒ 82 + 4{\lambda}^{2} = 43\mu . . . . \left(3\right)

Solving \left(2\right)\text{$ and }$\left(3\right), we get

${\lambda}^{2} = 1, \mu = 2$

So,

$\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{b} = 3 - 10 - {\lambda}^{2} = - 8$

$⇒ $\left|\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{b}\right|$ = 8$

$

questions.solution:
Given:

$\overset{\to}{v} \times \overset{\to}{w} = \overset{\to}{u} + \lambda\overset{\to}{v} . . . . \left(1\right)

Taking dot product$ with \overset{\to}{w}$, we get

$\overset{\to}{w} \cdot $\left(\overset{\to}{v} \times \overset{\to}{w}\right) = \overset{\to}{w} \cdot \overset{\to}{u} + \lambda\left(\overset{\to}{w} \cdot \overset{\to}{v}\right)

$⇒ \overset{\to}{u} \cdot \overset{\to}{w} + \lambda$\left(\overset{\to}{w} \cdot \overset{\to}{v}\right)$ = 0$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{u} \cdot \overset{\to}{w} = - 2\lambda . . . . $\left(2\right)$

Taking dot product with $\overset{\to}{v} in \left(1\right), we get

$\overset{\to}{v} \cdot $\left(\overset{\to}{v} \times \overset{\to}{w}\right)$ = \overset{\to}{v} \cdot \overset{\to}{u} + \lambda$\left(\overset{\to}{v} \cdot \overset{\to}{v}\right)$

$⇒ \left(2 - 1 + 2\right) + \lambda\left(6 + 1 + 1\right) = 0$

$⇒ \lambda = - \dfrac{1}{2}$

So, by $\left(2\right)$, we get

$\overset{\to}{u} \cdot \overset{\to}{w} = - 2\lambda = 1$

questions.q: Let $PQR$be a triangle. The points$A, B$ and $C$ are on the sides $QR, RP$ and $PQ$ respectively such that $\dfrac{QA}{AR} = \dfrac{RB}{BP} = \dfrac{PC}{CQ} = \dfrac{1}{2}$. Then $\dfrac{Area\left(∆ PQR\right)}{Area\left(∆ ABC\right)}$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Let the position vector of $P$ is $\overset{\to}{O}$, $Q$ is $\overset{\to}{q}$ and $R$ is $\overset{\to}{r}$.

Now, position vector of $A$ is

$\dfrac{2\overset{\to}{q} + \overset{\to}{r}}{3}$

Position vector of $B$ is $\dfrac{2\overset{\to}{r}}{3}$.

Position vector of $C$ is $\overset{\to}{q}3$.

$\overset{\to}{AB} = \dfrac{\overset{\to}{r} - 2\overset{\to}{q}}{3}$

$\overset{\to}{AC} = \dfrac{- \overset{\to}{r} - \overset{\to}{q}}{3}$

So,

$\overset{\to}{AB} \times \overset{\to}{AC} = \dfrac{1}{3}\left[\left(\overset{\to}{r} - 2\overset{\to}{q}\right) \times \left(- \overset{\to}{r} - \overset{\to}{q}\right)\right]$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{AB} \times \overset{\to}{AC} = \dfrac{1}{3}\left[- \left(\overset{\to}{r} \times \overset{\to}{q}\right) + 2\left(\overset{\to}{q} \times \overset{\to}{r}\right)\right]$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{AB} \times \overset{\to}{AC} = \left(\overset{\to}{q} \times \overset{\to}{r}\right)$

Area of $∆ PQR$ is $= \dfrac{1}{2}\left|\overset{\to}{q} \times \overset{\to}{r}\right|$

Area of $∆ ABC$ is $\dfrac{1}{2}\left|\overset{\to}{AB} \times \overset{\to}{AC}\right|$

Area of $∆ ABC = \dfrac{1}{2}\left|\overset{\to}{q} \times \overset{\to}{r}\right|$

Position vector of $C$ is $\overset{\to}{q}3$.

$\overset{\to}{AB} = \dfrac{\overset{\to}{r} - 2\overset{\to}{q}}{3}$

$\overset{\to}{AC} = \dfrac{- \overset{\to}{r} - \overset{\to}{q}}{3}$

So,

$\overset{\to}{AB} \times \overset{\to}{AC} = \dfrac{1}{3}\left[\left(\overset{\to}{r} - 2\overset{\to}{q}\right) \times \left(- \overset{\to}{r} - \overset{\to}{q}\right)\right]$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{AB} \times \overset{\to}{AC} = \dfrac{1}{3}\left[- \left(\overset{\to}{r} \times \overset{\to}{q}\right) + 2\left(\overset{\to}{q} \times \overset{\to}{r}\right)\right]$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{AB} \times \overset{\to}{AC} = \left(\overset{\to}{q} \times \overset{\to}{r}\right)$

$\dfrac{Area\left(∆ PQR\right)}{Area\left(∆ ABC\right)} = 1$
