Points $A\left(2, 3, 9\right), B\left(5, 2, 1\right), C\left(1, \lambda, 8\right) \text{$ and $} D\left(\lambda, 2, 3\right)$ are coplanar,

Now we know that condition of coplanarity is $\left[\begin{cases}\overset{\to}{AB} & \overset{\to}{AC} & \overset{\to}{AD}\end{cases}\right] = 0$

So product of roots will be $\dfrac{95}{8}$

questions.q: Let $\overset{\to}{a}, \overset{\to}{b}, \overset{\to}{c}$ be three coplanar concurrent vectors such that angles between any two of them is same. If the product of their magnitudes is $14 and \left(\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b}\right) \cdot \left(\overset{\to}{b} \times \overset{\to}{c}\right) + \left(\overset{\to}{b} \times \overset{\to}{c}\right) \cdot \left(\overset{\to}{c} \times \overset{\to}{a}\right) + \left(\overset{\to}{c} \times \overset{\to}{a}\right) \cdot \left(\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b}\right) = 168$ then $\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right| + \left|\overset{\to}{b}\right| + \left|\overset{\to}{c}\right|$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Given, product of magnitudes is $14$

So, $\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|\left|\overset{\to}{c}\right| = 14$

Also given angles between any two of them is same

So, angle between $\overset{\to}{a} \text{ and } \overset{\to}{b} = \overset{\to}{b} \text{ and } \overset{\to}{c} = \overset{\to}{c} \text{ and } \overset{\to}{a} = \theta = \dfrac{2\pi}{3}$

So, $\overset{\to}{a} . \overset{\to}{b} = - \dfrac{1}{2}ab, \overset{\to}{b} . \overset{\to}{c} = - \dfrac{1}{2}bc \text{ and } \overset{\to}{a} . \overset{\to}{c} = - \dfrac{1}{2}ac$

Now solving $\left(\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b}\right) \cdot \left(\overset{\to}{b} \times \overset{\to}{c}\right) = \left(\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{b}\right)\left(\overset{\to}{b} \cdot \overset{\to}{c}\right) - \left(\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{c}\right)\left(\overset{\to}{b} \cdot \overset{\to}{b}\right)$

$= \left(\dfrac{- 1}{2}ab\right)\left(\dfrac{- 1}{2}bc\right) - \left(\dfrac{- 1}{2}ac\right)\left({b}^{2}\right)$

$= \dfrac{1}{4}a{b}^{2}c + \dfrac{1}{2}a{b}^{2}c$

$= \dfrac{3}{4}a{b}^{2}c . . . . . . . \left(1\right)$

Similarly for

$\left(\overset{\to}{b} \times \overset{\to}{c}\right) \cdot \left(\overset{\to}{c} \times \overset{\to}{a}\right) = \dfrac{3}{4}ab{c}^{2} . . . . . . . . . \left(2\right)$

And $\left(\overset{\to}{c} \times \overset{\to}{a}\right) \cdot \left(\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b}\right) = \dfrac{3}{4}{a}^{2}bc . . . . . . \left(3\right)$

Now adding equation $\left(1\right), \left(2\right) \text{ and } \left(3\right)$ we get,

$\left(\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b}\right) \cdot \left(\overset{\to}{b} \times \overset{\to}{c}\right) + \left(\overset{\to}{b} \times \overset{\to}{c}\right) \cdot \left(\overset{\to}{c} \times \overset{\to}{a}\right) + \left(\overset{\to}{c} \times \overset{\to}{a}\right) \cdot \left(\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b}\right) = 168$

$⇒ \dfrac{3}{4}abc\left(a + b + c\right) = 168$

$⇒ \left(a + b + c\right) = \dfrac{168 \times 4}{14 \times 3}$

So, $\left(a + b + c\right) = 16$

questions.q: Let $\overset{\to}{a}$ and $\overset{\to}{b}$ be two vectors such that ${\left|\overset{\to}{a} + \overset{\to}{b}\right|}^{2} = {\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|}^{2} + 2{\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|}^{2}, \overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{b} = 3$ and ${\left|\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b}\right|}^{2} = 75$. Then ${\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|}^{2}$ is equal to ______.
questions.solution:
Given,

${\left|\overset{\to}{a} + \overset{\to}{b}\right|}^{2} = {\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|}^{2} + 2{\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|}^{2} \text{ and } \overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{b} = 3$

We know that

${\left|\overset{\to}{a} + \overset{\to}{b}\right|}^{2} = {\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|}^{2} + {\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|}^{2} + 2\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{b}$

Now using the above formula in ${\left|\overset{\to}{a} + \overset{\to}{b}\right|}^{2} = {\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|}^{2} + 2{\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|}^{2}$ we get,

${\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|}^{2} + {\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|}^{2} + 2\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{b} = {\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|}^{2} + 2{\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|}^{2}$

Now on comparing both side we get, ${\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|}^{2} = 2\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{b} = 6 . . . . . . . . . \left(1\right)$

Also given ${\left|\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b}\right|}^{2} = 75$

$⇒ {\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|}^{2}{\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|}^{2}\sin^{2}\theta = 75$

$⇒ {\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|}^{2}{\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|}^{2}\left(1 - \cos^{2}\theta\right) = 75$

$⇒ {\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|}^{2}{\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|}^{2} - {\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|}^{2}{\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|}^{2}\cos^{2}\theta = 75$

$⇒ {\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|}^{2}{\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|}^{2} - {\left(\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{b}\right)}^{2} = 75$

Now putting the value of ${\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|}^{2} = 2\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{b} = 6$ we get, $6{\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|}^{2} - 9 = 75 ⇒ {\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|}^{2} = 14$

questions.q: Let $\overset{^}{a}$ and $\overset{^}{b}$ be two unit vectors such that the angle between them is $\dfrac{\pi}{4}$. If $\theta$ is the angle between the vectors $\left(\overset{^}{a} + \overset{^}{b}\right)$ and $\left(\overset{^}{a} + 2\overset{^}{b} + 2\left(\overset{^}{a} \times \overset{^}{b}\right)\right)$ then the value of $164\cos^{2}\theta$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Let $\overset{^}{a}$ and $\overset{^}{b}$ be two unit vectors such that the angle between them is $\dfrac{\pi}{4}$. If $\theta$ is the angle between the vectors $\left(\overset{^}{a} + \overset{^}{b}\right)$ and $\left(\overset{^}{a} + 2\overset{^}{b} + 2\left(\overset{^}{a} \times \overset{^}{b}\right)\right)$ then the value of $164\cos^{2}\theta$ is equal to

Now let angle between $\overset{^}{a} \text{ and } \overset{^}{b} = \dfrac{\pi}{4} = ϕ$

So, $\overset{^}{a} \cdot \overset{^}{b} = \left|\overset{^}{a}\right|\left|\overset{^}{b}\right|cosϕ$

$⇒ \overset{^}{a} \cdot \overset{^}{b} = cosϕ = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

Now finding angle between $\left(\overset{^}{a} + \overset{^}{b}\right) \text{ and } \left(\overset{^}{a} + 2\overset{^}{b} + 2\left(\overset{^}{a} \times \overset{^}{b}\right)\right)$ we get,

$cos\theta = \dfrac{\left(\overset{^}{a} + \overset{^}{b}\right) \cdot \left(\overset{^}{a} + 2\overset{^}{b} + 2\left(\overset{^}{a} \times \overset{^}{b}\right)\right)}{\left|\overset{^}{a} + \overset{^}{b}\right|\left|\overset{^}{a} + 2\overset{^}{b} + 2\left(\overset{^}{a} \times \overset{^}{b}\right)\right|} . . . . \left(1\right)$

Now finding the value of ${\left|\overset{^}{a} + \overset{^}{b}\right|}^{2} = \left(\overset{^}{a} + \overset{^}{b}\right) \cdot \left(\overset{^}{a} + \overset{^}{b}\right)$

$⇒ {\left|\overset{^}{a} + \overset{^}{b}\right|}^{2} = 2 + 2\overset{^}{a} \cdot \overset{^}{b}$= 2 + \sqrt{2}$

Also value of $\overset{^}{a} \times \overset{^}{b} = \left|\overset{^}{a}\right|\left|\overset{^}{b}\right|sinϕ\overset{^}{n}$

$⇒ \overset{^}{a} \times \overset{^}{b} = \overset{^}{n}\sqrt{2}$ when $\overset{^}{n}$ is vector $⊥$to $\overset{^}{a}$ and $\overset{^}{b}$

Let $\overset{\to}{c} = \overset{^}{a} \times \overset{^}{b}$

We know that, $\overset{\to}{c} \cdot \overset{\to}{a} = 0$ and $\overset{\to}{c} \cdot \overset{\to}{b} = 0$ as perpendicular vector dot product is zero.

Now value of ${\left|\overset{^}{a} + 2\overset{^}{b} + 2\overset{\to}{c}\right|}^{2}$

$= 1 + 4 + \dfrac{\left(4\right)}{2} + 4\overset{^}{a} \cdot \overset{^}{b} + 8\overset{^}{b} \cdot \overset{\to}{c} + 4\overset{\to}{c} \cdot \overset{^}{a}$

$= 7 + \dfrac{4}{\sqrt{2}} = 7 + 2\sqrt{2}$

Now finding dot product we get, $\left(\overset{^}{a} + \overset{^}{b}\right) \cdot \left(\overset{^}{a} + 2\overset{^}{b} + 2\overset{\to}{c}\right)$

$= {\left|\overset{^}{a}\right|}^{2} + 2\overset{^}{a} \cdot \overset{^}{b} + 0 + \overset{^}{b} \cdot \overset{^}{a} + 2{\left|\overset{^}{b}\right|}^{2} + 0$

$= 1 + \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{2}} + \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} + 2$

$= 3 + \dfrac{3}{\sqrt{2}}$

Now putting all the values in equation $\left(1\right)$ we get,

$cos\theta = \dfrac{3 + \dfrac{3}{\sqrt{2}}}{\sqrt{2 + \sqrt{2}}\sqrt{7 + 2\sqrt{2}}}$

questions.q: Let a vector $\overset{\to}{a}$ has a magnitude $9$. Let a vector $\overset{\to}{b}$ be such that for every $\left(x, y\right)R \times R - \left\{\left(0, 0\right)\right\}$, the vector $\left(x\overset{\to}{a} + y\overset{\to}{b}\right)$ is perpendicular to the vector $\left(6y\overset{\to}{a} - 18x\overset{\to}{b}\right)$. Then the value of $\left|\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b}\right|$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Given, $\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right| = 9$

And $\left(x\overset{\to}{a} + y\overset{\to}{b}\right) \cdot \left(6y\overset{\to}{a} - 18x\overset{\to}{b}\right) = 0$\left\{\text{as they are perpendicular}\right\}$

$⇒ 6xy{\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|}^{2} - 18{x}^{2}\left(\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{b}\right) + 6{y}^{2}\left(\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{b}\right) - 18xy{\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|}^{2} = 0$

$⇒ 6xy\left({\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|}^{2} - 3{\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|}^{2}\right) + \left(\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{b}\right)\left({y}^{2} - 3{x}^{2}\right) = 0$

This should hold $∀ x, y \in R \times R - \left\{\left(0, 0\right)\right\}$

So, ${\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|}^{2} - 3{\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|}^{2} = 0 \text{ and } \left(\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{b}\right) = 0$

$∴ {\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|}^{2} = 3{\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|}^{2} \text{ and } \left(\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{b}\right) = 0 ⇒ cos\theta = 0 ⇒ \theta = 90 °$

Now ${\left|\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b}\right|}^{2} = {\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|}^{2}{\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|}^{2}\sin^{2}\theta = {\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|}^{2}{\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|}^{2}\left\{\text{as}\theta = {90}^{°}\right\}$

$= {\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|}^{2} \cdot \dfrac{{\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|}^{2}}{3}$\left\{\text{as}{\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|}^{2} = \dfrac{{\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|}^{2}}{3}\right\}$

So, $\left|\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b}\right| = \dfrac{{\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|}^{2}}{\sqrt{3}} = \dfrac{81}{\sqrt{3}} = 27\sqrt{3}$

questions.q:
Let $\overset{\to}{a}, \overset{\to}{b}, \overset{\to}{c}$ be three non-coplanar vectors such that $\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b} = 4\overset{\to}{c}, \overset{\to}{b} \times \overset{\to}{c} = 9\overset{\to}{a}$ and $\overset{\to}{c} \times \overset{\to}{a} = \alpha\overset{\to}{b}, \alpha > 0$
If $\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right| + \left|\overset{\to}{b}\right| + \left|\overset{\to}{c}\right| = 36$, then $\alpha$ is equal to _______.
questions.solution:
Taking cross product of $\overset{\to}{c}$ both side we get,

$\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b} = 4\overset{\to}{c} ⇒ \left(\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b}\right) \times \overset{\to}{c} = 0$

$⇒ \left(\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{c}\right) . \overset{\to}{b} - \left(\overset{\to}{b} \cdot \overset{\to}{c}\right) . \overset{\to}{a} = 0$

$⇒ \left(\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{c}\right) . \overset{\to}{b} = \left(\overset{\to}{b} \cdot \overset{\to}{c}\right) . \overset{\to}{a}$

Since vectors are non-coplanar so,

$⇒ \left(\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{c}\right) = \left(\overset{\to}{b} \cdot \overset{\to}{c}\right) = 0 . . . . . . \left(1\right)$

Similarly for $\overset{\to}{b} \times \overset{\to}{c} = 9\overset{\to}{a} ⇒ \overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{b} = 0 = \overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{c} . . . . . \left(2\right)$

So, from equation $\left(1\right) \text{ and } \left(2\right)$ we can say that $\overset{\to}{a}, \overset{\to}{b}, \overset{\to}{c}$ are mutually $⊥$ set of vectors.

Now taking modulus both side of $\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b} = 4\overset{\to}{c}, \overset{\to}{b} \times \overset{\to}{c} = 9\overset{\to}{a} \text{ and } \overset{\to}{c} \times \overset{\to}{a} = \alpha\overset{\to}{b}$ we get,

$⇒ \left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right| = 4\left|\overset{\to}{c}\right|, \left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|\left|\overset{\to}{c}\right| = 9\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right| \text{ and } \left|\overset{\to}{c}\right|\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right| = \alpha\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|$

$⇒ \dfrac{\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|}{\left|\overset{\to}{c}\right|} = \dfrac{4}{9}\dfrac{\left|\overset{\to}{c}\right|}{\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|}$

$⇒ \dfrac{\left|\overset{\to}{c}\right|}{\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|} = \dfrac{3}{2}$

$∴$ If $\left|a\right| = \lambda, \left|c\right| = \dfrac{3\lambda}{2} \text{ and } \left|b\right| = 6$

Now $\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right| + \left|\overset{\to}{b}\right| + \left|\overset{\to}{c}\right| = 36$

$⇒ \lambda + \dfrac{3}{2}\lambda + 6 = 36$

$⇒ \lambda = 12$

Now given $\left|\overset{\to}{c}\right|\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right| = \alpha\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|$

$⇒ \alpha = \dfrac{\left|\overset{\to}{c}\right|\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|}{\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|} = \dfrac{3 \times 12}{2} \times \dfrac{12}{6}$

$⇒ \alpha = 36$

Similarly for $\overset{\to}{b} \times \overset{\to}{c} = 9\overset{\to}{a} ⇒ \overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{b} = 0 = \overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{c} . . . . . \left(2\right)$

So, from equation $\left(1\right) \text{ and } \left(2\right)$ we can say that $\overset{\to}{a}, \overset{\to}{b}, \overset{\to}{c}$ are mutually $⊥$ set of vectors.

Now taking modulus both side of $\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b} = 4\overset{\to}{c}, \overset{\to}{b} \times \overset{\to}{c} = 9\overset{\to}{a} \text{ and } \overset{\to}{c} \times \overset{\to}{a} = \alpha\overset{\to}{b}$ we get,

$⇒ \left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right| = 4\left|\overset{\to}{c}\right|, \left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|\left|\overset{\to}{c}\right| = 9\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right| \text{ and } \left|\overset{\to}{c}\right|\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right| = \alpha\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|$

$⇒ \dfrac{\left|\overset{\to}{c}\right|}{\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|} = \dfrac{3}{2}$

$∴$ If $\left|a\right| = \lambda, \left|c\right| = \dfrac{3\lambda}{2} \text{ and } \left|b\right| = 6$

Now $\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right| + \left|\overset{\to}{b}\right| + \left|\overset{\to}{c}\right| = 36$

$⇒ \lambda + \dfrac{3}{2}\lambda + 6 = 36$

$⇒ \lambda = 12$

Now given $\left|\overset{\to}{c}\right|\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right| = \alpha\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|$

$⇒ \alpha = \dfrac{\left|\overset{\to}{c}\right|\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|}{\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|} = \dfrac{3 \times 12}{2} \times \dfrac{12}{6}$

$⇒ \alpha = 36$

questions.solution:

questions.q: Let $\overset{\to}{a} = \overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}$ and let $\overset{\to}{b}$ be a vector such that $\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b} = 2\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{k}$ and $\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{b} = 3$. Then the projection of $\overset{\to}{b}$ on the vector $\overset{\to}{a} - \overset{\to}{b}$ is:
questions.solution:
Given,

$\overset{\to}{a} = \overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}$ , $\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b} = 2\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{k}$ and $\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{b} = 3$

Now using the formula ${\left|\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b}\right|}^{2} + {\left|\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{b}\right|}^{2} = \left({\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|}^{2} \cdot {\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|}^{2}\sin^{2}\theta + {\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|}^{2} \cdot {\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|}^{2}\cos^{2}\theta\right)$

$⇒ {\left|\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b}\right|}^{2} + {\left|\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{b}\right|}^{2} = {\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|}^{2} \cdot {\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|}^{2}\left(\sin^{2}\theta + \cos^{2}\theta\right) = {\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|}^{2} \cdot {\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|}^{2}$

We get,

$⇒ {\left|2\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{k}\right|}^{2} + {\left|3\right|}^{2} = {\left|\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}\right|}^{2}{\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|}^{2}$

$⇒ {\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|}^{2} = \dfrac{5 + 9}{6} = \dfrac{14}{6} = \dfrac{7}{3}$

Now finding $\left|\overset{\to}{a} - \overset{\to}{b}\right| = \sqrt{{\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|}^{2} + {\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|}^{2} - 2\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|} = \sqrt{6 + \dfrac{7}{3} - 6} = \sqrt{\dfrac{7}{3}}$

Now projection of $\overset{\to}{b}$ on $\overset{\to}{a} - \overset{\to}{b} = \dfrac{\overset{\to}{b} \cdot \left(\overset{\to}{a} - \overset{\to}{b}\right)}{\left|\overset{\to}{a} - \overset{\to}{b}\right|}$

$= \dfrac{\overset{\to}{b} \cdot \overset{\to}{a} - {\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|}^{2}}{\left|\overset{\to}{a} - \overset{\to}{b}\right|} = \dfrac{3 - \dfrac{7}{3}}{\sqrt{\dfrac{7}{3}}}$

$= \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{21}}$

questions.q:
Let $ABC$ be a triangle such that $\overset{\to}{BC} = \overset{\to}{a}, \overset{\to}{CA} = \overset{\to}{b}$, $\overset{\to}{AB} = \overset{\to}{c}, \left|\overset{\to}{a}\right| = 6\sqrt{2}, \left|\overset{\to}{b}\right| = 2\sqrt{3}$ and $\overset{\to}{b} \cdot \overset{\to}{c} = 12$ Consider the statements :

$\left(S1\right)$: $\left|\left(\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b}\right) + \left(\overset{\to}{c} \times \overset{\to}{b}\right)\right| - \left|\overset{\to}{c}\right| = 6 \left(2\sqrt{2} - 1\right)

\left(S2\right): $∠ ABC = \cos^{- 1}$\left(\sqrt{\dfrac{2}{3}}\right)$. Then
questions.solution:
We know that by triangle law of vector addition,

$\overset{\to}{a} + \overset{\to}{b} + \overset{\to}{c} = 0$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{b} + \overset{\to}{c} = - \overset{\to}{a}$

Squaring both side we get,

${\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|}^{2} + {\left|\overset{\to}{c}\right|}^{2} + 2\overset{\to}{b} \cdot \overset{\to}{c} = {\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|}^{2}$

Now putting the given value $\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right| = 6\sqrt{2}, \left|\overset{\to}{b}\right| = 2\sqrt{3} \text{ and } \overset{\to}{b} . \overset{\to}{c} = 12$

We get, ${\left|\overset{\to}{c}\right|}^{2} = 36$

So, $\left|\overset{\to}{c}\right| = 6$

Now, $S1: \left|\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b} + \overset{\to}{c} \times \overset{\to}{b}\right| - \left|\overset{\to}{c}\right|$

$⇒ \left|\left(\overset{\to}{a} + \overset{\to}{c}\right) \times \overset{\to}{b}\right| - \left|\overset{\to}{c}\right|$

$⇒ 0 - 6 = - 6$

And $S2: \overset{\to}{a} + \overset{\to}{b} + \overset{\to}{c} = 0$

$\overset{\to}{a} + \overset{\to}{b} = - \overset{\to}{c}$

Squaring both side we get,

${\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|}^{2} + {\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|}^{2} - 2\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|cos\left(∠ ACB\right) = {\left|\overset{\to}{c}\right|}^{2}$

$⇒ 72 + 12 - 24\sqrt{6}cos\left(∠ ACB\right) = 36$

$⇒ cos\left(∠ ACB\right) = \dfrac{48}{24\sqrt{6}} = \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{6}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2}{3}}$

$\left(S1\right)$: $\left|\left(\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b}\right) + \left(\overset{\to}{c} \times \overset{\to}{b}\right)\right| - \left|\overset{\to}{c}\right| = 6 \left(2\sqrt{2} - 1\right)

\left(S2\right): $∠ ABC = \cos^{- 1}$\left(\sqrt{\dfrac{2}{3}}\right)$. Then
questions.explanation:
We know that by triangle law of vector addition,

$\overset{\to}{a} + \overset{\to}{b} + \overset{\to}{c} = 0$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{b} + \overset{\to}{c} = - \overset{\to}{a}$

Squaring both side we get,

${\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|}^{2} + {\left|\overset{\to}{c}\right|}^{2} + 2\overset{\to}{b} \cdot \overset{\to}{c} = {\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|}^{2}$

Now putting the given value $\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right| = 6\sqrt{2}, \left|\overset{\to}{b}\right| = 2\sqrt{3} \text{ and } \overset{\to}{b} . \overset{\to}{c} = 12$

We get, ${\left|\overset{\to}{c}\right|}^{2} = 36$

So, $\left|\overset{\to}{c}\right| = 6$

Now, $S1: \left|\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b} + \overset{\to}{c} \times \overset{\to}{b}\right| - \left|\overset{\to}{c}\right|$

$⇒ \left|\left(\overset{\to}{a} + \overset{\to}{c}\right) \times \overset{\to}{b}\right| - \left|\overset{\to}{c}\right|$

$⇒ 0 - 6 = - 6$

And $S2: \overset{\to}{a} + \overset{\to}{b} + \overset{\to}{c} = 0$

$\overset{\to}{a} + \overset{\to}{b} = - \overset{\to}{c}$

Squaring both side we get,

${\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|}^{2} + {\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|}^{2} - 2\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|cos\left(∠ ACB\right) = {\left|\overset{\to}{c}\right|}^{2}$

$⇒ 72 + 12 - 24\sqrt{6}cos\left(∠ ACB\right) = 36$

$⇒ cos\left(∠ ACB\right) = \dfrac{48}{24\sqrt{6}} = \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{6}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2}{3}}$

questions.q:
Let $A, B, C$ be three points whose position vectors respectively are:

$\overset{\to}{a} = \overset{^}{i} + 4\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}$

$\overset{\to}{b} = 2\overset{^}{i} + \alpha\overset{^}{j} + 4\overset{^}{k}, \alpha \in R$

$\overset{\to}{c} = 3\overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} + 5\overset{^}{k}$

If $\alpha$ is the smallest positive integer for which $\overset{\to}{a}, \overset{\to}{b}, \overset{\to}{c}$ are non-collinear, then the length of the median, $△ ABC$, through $A$ is:
questions.solution:
Let us assume that vectors are collinear so, $\overset{\to}{AB} ∥ \overset{\to}{AC}$ if $\dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{\alpha - 4}{- 6} = \dfrac{1}{2} ⇒ \alpha = 1$

Now, for $\overset{\to}{a}, \overset{\to}{b}, \overset{\to}{c}$ to be non-collinear smallest positive integer will be $\alpha = 2$

So, mid-point of $BC = M\left(\dfrac{5}{2}, 0, \dfrac{9}{2}\right)$

Now, $AM = \sqrt{\dfrac{9}{4} + 16 + \dfrac{9}{4}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{82}}{2}$

questions.q: Let $\overset{\to}{a} = \overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}, \overset{\to}{b} = \overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$ and $\overset{\to}{c}$ be a vector such that $\overset{\to}{a} \times ( \overset{\to}{b} + \overset{\to}{c} ) = \overset{\to}{0}$, then the value of $3\left(\overset{\to}{c} . \overset{\to}{a}\right)$ is equal to _______.
questions.solution:
Given, $\overset{\to}{a} = \overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}, \overset{\to}{b} = \overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$

And $\overset{\to}{a} \times ( \overset{\to}{b} + \overset{\to}{c} ) = \overset{\to}{0}$,

Let $\overset{\to}{c} = x\overset{^}{i} + y\overset{^}{j} + z\overset{^}{k}$

So, $\overset{\to}{a} \times \left(\overset{\to}{b} + \overset{\to}{c}\right) = \overset{\to}{0} ⇒ \overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b} + \overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{c} = \overset{\to}{0}$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b} = - \overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{c} ⇒ \overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b} = \overset{\to}{c} \times \overset{\to}{a}$

$⇒ \left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 1 & - 2 & 3 \\ 1 & 1 & 1\end{cases}\right| = \left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ x & y & z \\ 1 & - 2 & 3\end{cases}\right|$

$⇒ - 5\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k} = \overset{^}{i}\left(3y + 2z\right) + \overset{^}{j}\left(z - 3x\right) + \overset{^}{k}\left(- 2x - y\right)$

On comparing we get,

$3y + 2z = - 5$ .....(i)

$z - 3x = 2$ ............(ii)

$- 2x - y = 3$ ........(iii)

On solving equation (i), (ii) and (iii) we get,

$x = \dfrac{- 1}{6}, y = \dfrac{- 8}{3}, z = \dfrac{3}{2}$

So, $\overset{\to}{c} = \dfrac{- 1}{6}\overset{^}{i} + \dfrac{- 8}{3}\overset{^}{j} + \dfrac{3}{2}\overset{^}{k}$

So, $\overset{\to}{c} . \overset{\to}{a} = \left(\dfrac{- 1}{6}\overset{^}{i} + \dfrac{- 8}{3}\overset{^}{j} + \dfrac{3}{2}\overset{^}{k}\right) . \left(\overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}\right) = \dfrac{29}{3}$

So, $3\overset{\to}{c} . \overset{\to}{a} = 29$

Note: This question appeared in JEE Main 2022, 29th june shift 2. The question was incorrect, so it is modified to make it correct.

questions.q: Let $\overset{\to}{a} = \alpha\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}, \overset{\to}{b} = 3\overset{^}{i} - \beta\overset{^}{j} + 4\overset{^}{k}$ and $\overset{\to}{c} = \overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} - 2\overset{^}{k}$ where $\alpha, \beta \in R$ be three vectors. If the projection of $\overset{\to}{a}$ on $\overset{\to}{c}$ is $\dfrac{10}{3}$ and$\overset{\to}{b} \times \overset{\to}{c} = - 6\overset{^}{i} + 10\overset{^}{j} + 7\overset{^}{k}$ , then the value of $\alpha + \beta$ equal to
questions.solution:
Given $\overset{\to}{a} = \alpha\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}, \overset{\to}{b} = 3\overset{^}{i} - \beta\overset{^}{j} + 4\overset{^}{k}$ and $\overset{\to}{c} = \overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} - 2\overset{^}{k}$ where $\alpha, \beta \in R$ be three vectors.

Projection of $\overset{\to}{a}$ on $\overset{\to}{c}$ is $\dfrac{\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{c}}{\left|\overset{\to}{c}\right|} = \dfrac{10}{3}$ (given)

$⇒ \dfrac{\alpha + 6 + 2}{\sqrt{1 + 4 + 4}} = \dfrac{10}{3} ⇒ \alpha = 2$

and $\overset{\to}{b} \times \overset{\to}{c} = \left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 3 & - \beta & 4 \\ 1 & 2 & - 2\end{cases}\right| = - 6\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$

$⇒ 2\beta - 8 = - 6 ⇒ \beta = 1$

Hence $\alpha + \beta = 3$

questions.q: Let $\overset{\to}{a} = \alpha\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}$ and $\overset{\to}{b} = - 2\overset{^}{i} + \alpha\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$, where $\alpha \in R$. If the area of the parallelogram whose adjacent sides are represented by the vectors $\overset{\to}{a}$ and $\overset{\to}{b}$ is $\sqrt{15\left({\alpha}^{2} + 4\right)}$, then the value of $2{\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|}^{2} + \left(\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{b}\right){\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|}^{2}$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Given,

$\overset{\to}{a} = \alpha\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}, \overset{\to}{b} = - 2\overset{^}{i} + \alpha\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$,

Area of parallelogram $= \left|\overset{^}{a} \times \overset{^}{b}\right|

$\overset{^}{a} \times \overset{^}{b} = \sqrt{{$\left(\alpha + 2\right)$}^{2} + {$\left(\alpha - 2\right)$}^{2} + {$\left({\alpha}^{2} + 4\right)$}^{2}}$

Given \left|\overset{^}{a} \times \overset{^}{b}\right|$ = \sqrt{15 $\left({\alpha}^{2} + 4\right)$}$

So, $2$\left({\alpha}^{2} + 4\right)$ + {$\left({\alpha}^{2} + 4\right)$}^{2} = 15 $\left({\alpha}^{2} + 4\right)$

$⇒ {\left({\alpha}^{2} + 4\right)$}^{2} = 13 $\left({\alpha}^{2} + 4\right)$

$⇒ {\alpha}^{2} + 4 = 13 ∴ {\alpha}^{2} = 9$

Now, $2{\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|}^{2} + \left(\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{b}\right){\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|}^{2}$

${\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|}^{2} = {\alpha}^{2} + 4 + 1 = {\alpha}^{2} + 5$

${| \overset{\to}{b} |}^{2} = 4 + {\alpha}^{2} + 1 = {\alpha}^{2} + 5$

$\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{b} = - 2\alpha + 2\alpha - 1 = - 1$

$∴ 2{\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|}^{2} + \left(\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{b}\right){\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|}^{2}$

$2\left({\alpha}^{2} + 5\right) - 1\left({\alpha}^{2} + 5\right) = {\alpha}^{2} + 5 = 14$

questions.q: Let $\overset{\to}{a}$ be a vector which is perpendicular to the vector $3\overset{^}{i} + \dfrac{1}{2}\overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}$. If $\overset{\to}{a} \times \left(2\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{k}\right) = 2\overset{^}{i} - 13\overset{^}{j} - 4\overset{^}{k}$, then the projection of the vector $\overset{\to}{a}$ on the vector $2\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$ is
questions.solution:
Given, $\overset{\to}{a} \times \left(2\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{k}\right) = 2\overset{^}{i} - 13\overset{^}{j} - 4\overset{^}{k}$

Now multiplying both side by $\left(3\overset{^}{i} + \dfrac{1}{2}\overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}\right)$ we get,

$⇒ \left(\overset{\to}{a} \times \left(2\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{k}\right)\right) \times \left(3\overset{^}{i} + \dfrac{1}{2}\overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}\right)$

$= \left(2\overset{^}{i} - 13\overset{^}{j} - 4\overset{^}{k}\right) \times \left(3\overset{^}{i} + \dfrac{1}{2}\overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}\right)$

$⇒ \left(\left(3\overset{^}{i} + \dfrac{1}{2}\overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}\right) . \overset{\to}{a}\right)\left(2\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{k}\right) - \left(6 + 2\right)\overset{\to}{a} = \left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 2 & - 13 & - 4 \\ 3 & \dfrac{1}{2} & 2\end{cases}\right|$

$⇒ 0 - \left(6 + 2\right)\overset{\to}{a} = \left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 2 & - 13 & - 4 \\ 3 & \dfrac{1}{2} & 2\end{cases}\right|$

$\overset{\to}{a} = 3\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} - 5\overset{^}{k}$

Now, projection of $\overset{\to}{a}$ on vector $2\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$ is $\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \dfrac{\left(2\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}\right)}{3} = \dfrac{5}{3}$

questions.q: If $\overset{\to}{a} = 2\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}, \overset{\to}{b} = 3\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$ and $\overset{\to}{c} = {c}_{1}\overset{^}{i} + {c}_{2}\overset{^}{j} + {c}_{3}\overset{^}{k}$ are coplanar vectors and $\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{c} = 5, \overset{\to}{b} ⊥ \overset{\to}{c}$, then $122\left({c}_{1} + {c}_{2} + {c}_{3}\right)$ is equal to ______.
questions.solution:
As the given vectors are coplanar, so $\left|\begin{cases}2 & 1 & 3 \\ 3 & 3 & 1 \\ {c}_{1} & {c}_{2} & {c}_{3}\end{cases}\right| = 0$

$⇒ 8{c}_{1} - 7{c}_{2} - 3{c}_{3} = 0 . . . \left(i\right)$

Then the number of vectors $\overset{\to}{b}$ such that $\overset{\to}{b} \times \overset{\to}{c} = \overset{\to}{a}$ and $\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right| \in\left\{1, 2, \ldots , 10\right\} is$
questions.solution:
Given, $\overset{\to}{a} = i + j - k$ and $\overset{\to}{c} = 2i - 3j + 2k$

$\overset{\to}{b} \times \overset{\to}{c} = \overset{\to}{a}$ and $\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right| \in\left\{1, 2 \ldots \ldots 10\right\}

$∵ \overset{\to}{b} \times \overset{\to}{c} = \overset{\to}{a}$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{a}$ is perpendicular to $\overset{\to}{b}$ as well as $\overset{\to}{a}$ is perpendicular to $\overset{\to}{c}$ , so $\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{c} = 0$ as they are perpendicular.

Now checking $\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{c} = 2 - 3 - 2 = - 3 \ne 0$

This $\overset{\to}{b} \times \overset{\to}{c} = \overset{\to}{a}$ is not possible.

So, number of vectors $\overset{\to}{b} = 0$

$

Let $\overset{\to}{v}$ be a vector in the plane of $\overset{\to}{a}$ and $\overset{\to}{b}$ whose projection on $\overset{\to}{c}$ is $\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{3}}$. If $\overset{\to}{v}, \overset{^}{j} = 7$, then $\overset{\to}{v} \cdot \left(\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{k}\right)$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Since vector $\overset{\to}{v}, \overset{\to}{a} \text{$ and $} \overset{\to}{b}$ are coplanar then, $\overset{\to}{v} = {\lambda}_{1}\overset{\to}{a} + {\lambda}_{2}\overset{\to}{b}$, where ${\lambda}_{1}, {\lambda}_{2} \in \mathbb{R}$.

$⇒ \overset{\to}{v} = \left({\lambda}_{1} + 2{\lambda}_{2}\right)\overset{^}{i} + \left({\lambda}_{1} - 3{\lambda}_{2}\right)\overset{^}{j} + \left(2{\lambda}_{1} + {\lambda}_{2}\right)\overset{^}{k}$

$∵$ Projection of $\overset{\to}{v}$ on $\overset{\to}{c}$ is $\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{3}}$

$∴ \dfrac{{\lambda}_{1} + 2{\lambda}_{2} - {\lambda}_{1} + 3{\lambda}_{2} + 2{\lambda}_{1} + {\lambda}_{2}}{\sqrt{3}} = \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{3}}$

$∴ {\lambda}_{1} + 3{\lambda}_{2} = 1 . . . \left(1\right)$

and $\overset{\to}{v} \cdot \overset{^}{j} = 7 ⇒ {\lambda}_{1} - 3{\lambda}_{2} = 7 . . . \left(2\right)

$⇒ \overset{\to}{v} = $\left({\lambda}_{1} + 2{\lambda}_{2}\right)$\overset{^}{i} + $\left({\lambda}_{1} - 3{\lambda}_{2}\right)$\overset{^}{j} + $\left(2{\lambda}_{1} + {\lambda}_{2}\right)$\overset{^}{k}$

$∴ {\lambda}_{1} + 3{\lambda}_{2} = 1 . . . $\left(1\right)$

$⇒ {\lambda}_{1} - 3{\lambda}_{2} = 7\left(2\right)
From equation \left(1\right)$ and $\left(2\right), we get

${\lambda}_{1} = 4, {\lambda}_{2} = - 1$

$∴ \overset{\to}{v} = 2\overset{^}{i} + 7\overset{^}{j} + 7\overset{^}{k}$

$∴ \overset{\to}{v} \cdot $\left(\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{k}\right)$ = 2 + 7 = 9$

$

$⇒ \lambday - z = 13, z - \lambdax = - 1, x - y = - 4$

questions.q:
Let $a and b$ be two unit vectors such that $\left|\left(a + b\right) + 2\left(a \times b\right)\right| = 2$. If $\theta \in \left(0, \pi\right)$ is the angle between $\overset{^}{a} and \overset{^}{b}$, then among the statements:
$\left(S1\right): 2\left|\overset{^}{a} \times \overset{^}{b}\right| = \left|\overset{^}{a} - \overset{^}{b}\right|
\left(S2\right) : The projection of $\overset{^}{a}$ on \left(\overset{^}{a} + \overset{^}{b}\right) is \dfrac{1}{2}$
questions.solution:
Given,

$\left|\left(\overset{^}{a} + \overset{^}{b}\right) + 2\left(\overset{^}{a} \times \overset{^}{b}\right)\right| = 2, \theta \in \left(0, \pi\right)$

Squaring both side we get,

$\left(\left(\overset{^}{a} + \overset{^}{b}\right) + 2\left(\overset{^}{a} \times \overset{^}{b}\right)\right) \cdot \left(\left(\overset{^}{a} + \overset{^}{b}\right) + 2\left(\overset{^}{a} \times \overset{^}{b}\right)\right) = 4$

${\left|\overset{^}{a} + \overset{^}{b}\right|}^{2} + 4{\left|\left(\overset{^}{a} \times \overset{^}{b}\right)\right|}^{2} + 0 = 4$

Let the angle be $\theta$ between $\overset{^}{a}$ and $\overset{^}{b}$

$⇒ {\left|\overset{^}{a}\right|}^{2} + {\left|\overset{^}{b}\right|}^{2} + 2\left|\overset{^}{a}\right|\left|\overset{^}{b}\right|cos\theta + 4\left(\left|\overset{^}{a}\right|\left|\overset{^}{b}\right|sin\theta\right) = 4$

$⇒ 2 + 2cos\theta + 4\sin^{2}\theta = 4$

$⇒ 2 + 2cos\theta - 4\cos^{2}\theta = 0$

Let $cos\theta = t$ then

$⇒ 2{t}^{2} - t - 1 = 0$

$⇒ 2{t}^{2} - 2t + t - 1 = 0$

$⇒ 2t\left(t - 1\right) + \left(t - 1\right) = 0$

$\left(2t + 1\right)\left(t - 1\right) = 0$

So, $t = - \dfrac{1}{2}$ or $t = 1$

Then, $cos\theta = - \dfrac{1}{2}$ or $cos\theta = 1$ which is not possible as $0 \in \left(0, \pi\right)$

So, $\theta = \dfrac{2\pi}{3}$

Now,

${S}_{1} ⇒ 2\left|a \times b\right| = 2sin\left(\dfrac{2\pi}{3}\right) = 2 \times \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} = \sqrt{3}$

And $\left|\overset{^}{a} - \overset{^}{b}\right| = \sqrt{1 + 1 - 2cos\left(\dfrac{2\pi}{3}\right)}$

$= \sqrt{2 - 2 \times \left(- \dfrac{1}{2}\right)}$

$= \sqrt{3}$

${S}_{1}$ is correct.

${S}_{2}$ projection of $\overset{^}{a}$ on $\left(\overset{^}{a} + \overset{^}{b}\right)$

$⇒ \dfrac{\overset{^}{a} . \left(\overset{^}{a} + \overset{^}{b}\right)}{∣ \overset{^}{a} + \overset{^}{b} )} = \dfrac{1 + cos\left(\dfrac{2\pi}{3}\right)}{\sqrt{2 + 2cos\dfrac{2\pi}{3}}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{1 - \dfrac{1}{2}}{\sqrt{1}} = \dfrac{1}{2}$

Which is true, So both are true.

questions.q: Let $\overset{^}{a}, \overset{^}{b}$ be unit vectors. If $\overset{\to}{c}$ be a vector such that the angle between $\overset{^}{a}$ and $\overset{\to}{c}$ is $\dfrac{\pi}{12}$, and $\overset{^}{b} = \overset{\to}{c} + 2\left(\overset{\to}{c} \times \overset{^}{a}\right)$, then ${\left|6\overset{\to}{c}\right|}^{2}$ is equal to:
questions.solution:
We have, $\overset{^}{b} = \overset{\to}{c} + 2\left(\overset{\to}{c} \times \overset{^}{a}\right)$,

$\overset{^}{b} \cdot \overset{^}{b} = \left(\overset{\to}{c} + 2\left(\overset{\to}{c} \times \overset{^}{a}\right)\right) \cdot \left(\overset{\to}{c} + 2\left(\overset{\to}{c} \times \overset{^}{a}\right)\right)$

$⇒ 1 = \left(\overset{\to}{c} \cdot \overset{\to}{c}\right) + \overset{\to}{c} \cdot 2\left(\overset{\to}{c} \times \overset{^}{a}\right) + 2\left(\overset{\to}{c} \times \overset{^}{a}\right) \cdot \overset{\to}{c} + 4\left(\overset{\to}{c} \times \overset{^}{a}\right) \cdot \left(\overset{\to}{c} \times \overset{^}{a}\right)$

$⇒ 1 = {\left|\overset{\to}{c}\right|}^{2} + 0 + 0 + {\left|\overset{\to}{c} \times \overset{^}{a}\right|}^{2}$⇒ 1 = {\left|\overset{\to}{c}\right|}^{2} + 4{\left|\overset{\to}{c}\right|}^{2}{\left|\overset{^}{a}\right|}^{2}\sin^{2}\dfrac{\pi}{12}$

$⇒ 1 = {\left|\overset{\to}{c}\right|}^{2} + 4{\left|\overset{\to}{c}\right|}^{2}\left(\dfrac{1 - cos\dfrac{\pi}{6}}{2}\right)$

$⇒ 1 = {\left|\overset{\to}{c}\right|}^{2}\left[1 + 2\left(1 - \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)\right]$⇒ 1 = {\left|\overset{\to}{c}\right|}^{2}\left[3 - \sqrt{3}\right]$⇒ {\left|\overset{\to}{c}\right|}^{2} = \dfrac{1}{3 - \sqrt{3}} = \dfrac{3 + \sqrt{3}}{6}$

$∴ 36{\left|\overset{\to}{c}\right|}^{2} = \dfrac{3 + \sqrt{3}}{6} \times 36 = 6\left(3 + \sqrt{3}\right)$

questions.q: Let $\overset{\to}{a} = 2\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}$ and $\overset{\to}{b} = \overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k} .$ Let a vector $\overset{\to}{v}$ be in the plane containing $\overset{\to}{a}$ and $\overset{\to}{b} .$ If $\overset{\to}{v}$ is perpendicular to the vector $3\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}$ and its projection on $\overset{\to}{a}$ is $19$ units, then $| 2\overset{\to}{v}{|}^{2}$ is equal to _____.

$\overset{\to}{v}, \overset{\to}{a}, \overset{\to}{b}$ are coplanar

$⇒ 3 ( 2\lambda + \mu ) + 2 ( 2\mu - \lambda ) - ( 2\lambda - \mu ) = 0$

$⇒ \lambda = - 4\mu . . . ( i )$

and also $\overset{\to}{v} \cdot \overset{^}{a} = 19 ⇒ 9\lambda - 2\mu = 57 . . . \left(ii\right)$

solving $( i ) and ( ii )$ we get

$\lambda = 6, \mu = - \dfrac{3}{2}$
$⇒ 2\overset{\to}{v} = 21\overset{^}{i} - 18\overset{^}{j} + 27\overset{^}{k}$
$⇒ | 2\overset{\to}{v}{|}^{2} = 441 + 324 + 729$
$= 1494$

questions.q: Let $\overset{\to}{a}, \overset{\to}{b}, \overset{\to}{c}$ be three vectors mutually perpendicular to each other and have same magnitude. If a vector $\overset{\to}{r}$ satisfies $\overset{\to}{a} \times { \left(\overset{\to}{r} - \overset{\to}{b}\right) \times \overset{\to}{a} } + \overset{\to}{b} \times { \left(\overset{\to}{r} - \overset{\to}{c}\right) \times \overset{\to}{b} } + \overset{\to}{c} \times { \left(\overset{\to}{r} - \overset{\to}{a}\right) \times \overset{\to}{c} } = \overset{\to}{0},$ then $\overset{\to}{r}$ is equal to:

Given:$\overset{\to}{a} \times { \left(\overset{\to}{r} - \overset{\to}{b}\right) \times \overset{\to}{a} } + \overset{\to}{b} \times { \left(\overset{\to}{r} - \overset{\to}{c}\right) \times \overset{\to}{b} } + \overset{\to}{c} \times { \left(\overset{\to}{r} - \overset{\to}{a}\right) \times \overset{\to}{c} } = \overset{\to}{0}$

$⇒ ( \overset{\to}{a} . \overset{\to}{a} ) ( \overset{\to}{r} - \overset{\to}{b} ) - ( \overset{\to}{a} \cdot ( \overset{\to}{r} - \overset{\to}{b} ) ) \overset{\to}{a} + ( \overset{\to}{b} \cdot \overset{\to}{b} ) ( \overset{\to}{r} - \overset{\to}{c} ) - ( \overset{\to}{b} \cdot ( \overset{\to}{r} - \overset{\to}{c} ) ) \overset{\to}{b} + ( \overset{\to}{c} . \overset{\to}{c} ) ( \overset{\to}{r} - \overset{\to}{a} ) - ( \overset{\to}{c} . ( \overset{\to}{r} - \overset{\to}{a} ) ) \overset{\to}{c} = \overset{\to}{0}$

$⇒ | \overset{\to}{a}{|}^{2} ( \overset{\to}{r} - \overset{\to}{b} ) - ( \overset{\to}{r} \cdot \overset{\to}{a} ) \overset{\to}{a} + | \overset{\to}{b}{|}^{2} ( \overset{\to}{r} - \overset{\to}{c} ) - ( \overset{\to}{r} \cdot \overset{\to}{b} ) \overset{\to}{b} + | \overset{\to}{c}{|}^{2} ( \overset{\to}{r} - \overset{\to}{a} ) - ( \overset{\to}{r} \cdot \overset{\to}{c} ) \overset{\to}{c} = \overset{\to}{0}$

$⇒ | \overset{\to}{a}{|}^{2} [ 3\overset{\to}{r} - ( \overset{\to}{a} + \overset{\to}{b} + \overset{\to}{c} ) ] - [ ( \overset{\to}{r} \cdot \overset{\to}{a} ) \overset{\to}{a} ) + ( \overset{\to}{r} \cdot \overset{\to}{b} ) \overset{\to}{b} + ( \overset{\to}{r} \cdot \overset{\to}{c} ) \overset{\to}{c} ] = \overset{\to}{0}\left[∵ | \overset{\to}{a}{|}^{2} = | \overset{\to}{b}{|}^{2} = | \overset{\to}{c}{|}^{2}\right]$

$⇒ | \overset{\to}{a}{|}^{2} [ 3\overset{\to}{r} - ( \overset{\to}{a} + \overset{\to}{b} + \overset{\to}{c} ) - ( \overset{\to}{r} ) ] = \overset{\to}{0}\left[∵ ( \overset{\to}{r} \cdot \overset{\to}{a} ) \overset{\to}{a} + ( \overset{\to}{r} \cdot \overset{\to}{b} ) \overset{\to}{b} + ( \overset{\to}{r} \cdot \overset{\to}{c} ) \overset{\to}{c} = {\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|}^{2}\overset{\to}{r}, | \overset{\to}{a}{|}^{2} = | \overset{\to}{b}{|}^{2} = | \overset{\to}{c}{|}^{2}\right]$

$⇒ 3\overset{\to}{r} - ( \overset{\to}{a} + \overset{\to}{b} + \overset{\to}{c} ) - \overset{\to}{r} = \overset{\to}{0}$

$∴ \overset{\to}{r} = \dfrac{\overset{\to}{a} + \overset{\to}{b} + \overset{\to}{c}}{2}$

Given that

We know that$\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{b} = \left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|cos\theta,$
$⇒ 4 | \overset{\to}{a}{|}^{2} + 9 | \overset{\to}{b}{|}^{2} + 12 | \overset{\to}{a} | | \overset{\to}{b} | cos60 ° = 9 | \overset{\to}{a}{|}^{2} + | \overset{\to}{b}{|}^{2} + 6 | \overset{\to}{a} | | \overset{\to}{b} | cos60 °$
$⇒ 5 | \overset{\to}{a}{|}^{2} = 8 | \overset{\to}{b}{|}^{2} + 6 | \overset{\to}{a} | | | \overset{\to}{b} ∣ cos60 °$
$⇒ 5\left(64\right) = 8 | \overset{\to}{b}{|}^{2} + 6\left(8\right) \cdot | \overset{\to}{b} | \dfrac{1}{2}$

$⇒ | \overset{\to}{b} | = 5$

questions.q: If the projection of the vector $\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$ on the sum of the two vectors $2\overset{^}{i} + 4\overset{^}{j} - 5\overset{^}{k}$ and $- \lambda\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}$ is $1$, then $\lambda$ is equal to _______.
questions.solution:
Sum of two vectors $= 2\overset{^}{i} + 4\overset{^}{j} - 5\overset{^}{k} + ( - \lambda\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k} ) = ( 2 - \lambda ) \overset{^}{i} + 6\overset{^}{j} - 2\overset{^}{k}$
Projection $= 1 = \dfrac{1 ( 2 - \lambda ) + 2 ( 6 ) + 1 \times ( - 2 )}{\sqrt{( 2 - \lambda{)}^{2} + {6}^{2} + {2}^{2}}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{12 - \lambda}{\sqrt{{\lambda}^{2} - 4\lambda + 44}} = 1$
$⇒ ( 12 - \lambda{)}^{2} = {\lambda}^{2} - 4\lambda + 44$
$⇒ 144 + {\lambda}^{2} - 24\lambda = {\lambda}^{2} - 4\lambda + 44$
$⇒ 100 = 20\lambda$
$⇒ \lambda = 5$

questions.q: Let $\overset{\to}{a} = \overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$ and $\overset{\to}{b} = \overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k} .$ If $\overset{\to}{c}$ is a vector such that $\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{c} = \overset{\to}{b}$ and $\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{c} = 3$, then $\overset{\to}{a} \cdot ( \overset{\to}{b} \times \overset{\to}{c} )$ is equal to:
questions.solution:
We know that, for vectors $\overset{\to}{a}, \overset{\to}{b}$ and $\overset{\to}{c}$
$\overset{\to}{a} \cdot ( \overset{\to}{b} \times \overset{\to}{c} ) = \left[\begin{cases}\overset{\to}{a} & \overset{\to}{b} & \overset{\to}{c}\end{cases}\right] = \left[\begin{cases}\overset{\to}{c} & \overset{\to}{a} & \overset{\to}{b}\end{cases}\right]$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{a} \cdot ( \overset{\to}{b} \times \overset{\to}{c} ) = ( \overset{\to}{c} \times \overset{\to}{a} ) \cdot \overset{\to}{b}$

$= - \overset{\to}{b} \cdot \overset{\to}{b}$

$∵ \overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{c} = \overset{\to}{b} ⇒ \overset{\to}{c} \times \overset{\to}{a} = - \overset{\to}{b}$

$= - {\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|}^{2}$

$= - {\left(\sqrt{{1}^{2} + {\left(- 1\right)}^{2}}\right)}^{2}$

$= - 2$

questions.q: Let $\overset{\to}{a}, \overset{\to}{b}$ and $\overset{\to}{c}$ be three vectors such that $\overset{\to}{a} = \overset{\to}{b} \times \left(\overset{\to}{b} \times \overset{\to}{c}\right) .$ If magnitudes of the vectors $\overset{\to}{a}, \overset{\to}{b}$ and $\overset{\to}{c}$ are $\sqrt{2}, 1$ and $2$ respectively and the angle between $\overset{\to}{b}$ and $\overset{\to}{c}$ is $\theta\left(0 < \theta < \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right),$ then the value of $1 + tan\theta$ is equal to :
questions.solution:
We have, $\overset{\to}{a} = \left(\overset{\to}{b} \cdot \overset{\to}{c}\right)\overset{\to}{b} - \left(\overset{\to}{b} \cdot \overset{\to}{b}\right)\overset{\to}{c}$

$= 1 . 2cos\theta\overset{\to}{b} - \overset{\to}{c}$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{a} = 2cos\theta\overset{\to}{b} - \overset{\to}{c}$

${\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|}^{2} = {\left|2cos\theta\overset{\to}{b}\right|}^{2} + {\left|\overset{\to}{c}\right|}^{2} - 2 . 2cos\theta\left(\overset{\to}{b} \cdot \overset{\to}{c}\right)$

${\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|}^{2} = {\left(2cos\theta\right)}^{2}{\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|}^{2} + {\left|\overset{\to}{c}\right|}^{2} - 2 . 2cos\theta\left(\overset{\to}{b} \cdot \overset{\to}{c}\right)$

Given that, $\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right| = \sqrt{2}, \left|\overset{\to}{b}\right| = 1$ and $\left|\overset{\to}{c}\right| = 2$

${\left(\sqrt{2}\right)}^{2} = {\left(2cos\theta\right)}^{2} + {2}^{2} - 2 . 2cos\theta\left(\overset{\to}{b} \cdot \overset{\to}{c}\right)$

$⇒ 2 = 4\cos^{2}\theta + 4 - 4cos\theta \cdot 2cos\theta$

$\left(∵ \overset{\to}{b} \cdot \overset{\to}{c} = \left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|\left|\overset{\to}{c}\right|cos\theta\right)$

$⇒ - 2 = - 4\cos^{2}\theta$

$⇒ \cos^{2}\theta = \dfrac{1}{2}$

$⇒ cos\theta = \pm \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

$⇒ cos\theta = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

$⇒ \theta = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$

$\left(∵ 0 < \theta < \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$

Hence, $1 + tan\theta = 2 .$

Given that, $\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right| = \sqrt{2}, \left|\overset{\to}{b}\right| = 1$ and $\left|\overset{\to}{c}\right| = 2$

${\left(\sqrt{2}\right)}^{2} = {\left(2cos\theta\right)}^{2} + {2}^{2} - 2 . 2cos\theta\left(\overset{\to}{b} \cdot \overset{\to}{c}\right)$

questions.q: Let $\overset{\to}{a} = \overset{^}{i} - \alpha\overset{^}{j} + \beta\overset{^}{k}, \overset{\to}{b} = 3\overset{^}{i} + \beta\overset{^}{j} - \alpha\overset{^}{k}$ and $\overset{\to}{c} = - \alpha\overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k},$ where $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are integers. If $\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{b} = - 1$ and $\overset{\to}{b} \cdot \overset{\to}{c} = 10,$ then $\left(\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b}\right) \cdot \overset{\to}{c}$ is equal to ______.
questions.solution:
We have, $\overset{\to}{a} = \left(1, - \alpha, \beta\right)$, \overset{\to}{b} = $\left(3, \beta, - \alpha\right)$ and

$\overset{\to}{c} = \left(- \alpha, - 2, 1\right); \alpha, \beta \in I$

$\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{b} = - 1 ⇒ 3 - \alpha\beta - \alpha\beta = - 1$

$⇒ \alpha\beta = 2 . . . \left(1\right)

Now, $\overset{\to}{b} \cdot \overset{\to}{c} = 10$

$⇒ - 3\alpha - 2\beta - \alpha = 10$

$⇒ 2\alpha + \beta + 5 = 0 . . . $\left(2\right)$

From equations $\left(1\right)$ and $\left(2\right)$,

$⇒ 2\alpha + \dfrac{2}{\alpha} +5 = 0$

$⇒ 2{\alpha}^{2} + 2 + 5\alpha = 0$

$⇒ 2{\alpha}^{2} + 5\alpha + 2 = 0$

$⇒ 2{\alpha}^{2} + 4\alpha + \alpha + 2 = 0$

$⇒ 2\alpha\left(\alpha + 2\right) + 1\left(\alpha + 2\right) = 0$

$⇒ \left(2\alpha + 1\right)\left(\alpha + 2\right) = 0$

$\alpha = \dfrac{- 1}{2} is neglected since$\alpha$ is an integer.

$∴ \alpha = - 2$

Put $\alpha = - 2 in $equation \left(1\right), we get$\beta = - 1$.

Now, \left[\overset{\to}{a}\overset{\to}{b}\overset{\to}{c}\right] = \left|$\begin{cases}1 & 2 & - 1 \\ 3 & - 1 & 2 \\ 2 & - 2 & 1\end{cases}$\right|

$= 1$\left(- 1 + 4\right)$ - 2$\left(3 - 4\right)$ - 1 $\left(- 6 + 2\right)$

$= 3 + 2 + 4 = 9 .

questions.solution:

$\overset{\to}{b} = - \overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}$

$\overset{\to}{a} + \overset{\to}{b} = 3\overset{^}{j} + 5\overset{^}{k}; \overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{b} = - 1 + 2 + 6 = 7$

Now $\left(\left(\overset{\to}{a} \times \left(\left(\overset{\to}{a} - \overset{\to}{b}\right) \times \overset{\to}{b}\right)\right) \times \overset{\to}{b}\right)$

$= \left(\left(\overset{\to}{a} \times \left(\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b} - \overset{\to}{b} \times \overset{\to}{b}\right)\right) \times \overset{\to}{b}\right)$

$= \left(\overset{\to}{a} \times \left(\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b} - 0\right)\right) \times \overset{\to}{b}$

$= \left(\overset{\to}{a} \times \left(\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b}\right)\right) \times \overset{\to}{b}$

$= \left(\left(\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{b}\right)\overset{\to}{a} - \left(\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{a}\right)\overset{\to}{b}\right) \times \overset{\to}{b}$

$= \left(\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{b}\right)\left(\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b}\right)$

Here, $\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b} = \left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 1 & 1 & 2 \\ - 1 & 2 & 3\end{cases}\right| = - \overset{^}{i} - 5\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}$

$∴ \left(\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{b}\right)\left(\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b}\right) = 7\left(- \overset{^}{i} - 5\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}\right)$

So, $\left(\overset{\to}{a} + \overset{\to}{b}\right) \times \left(7\left(- \overset{^}{i} - 5\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}\right)\right)$

$= 7\left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 0 & 3 & 5 \\ - 1 & - 5 & 3\end{cases}\right|$

$= 7\left[34\overset{^}{i} - \left(5\right)\overset{^}{j} + \left(3\overset{^}{k}\right)\right]$

questions.q: Let $\overset{\to}{a} = \overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}, \overset{\to}{b}$ and $\overset{\to}{c} = \overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}$ be three vectors such that $\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b} = \overset{\to}{c}$ and $\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{b} = 1 .$ If the length of projection vector of the vector $\overset{\to}{b}$ on the vector $\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{c}$ is $l,$ then the value of $3{l}^{2}$ is equal to _____.
questions.solution:
Given,

$\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b} = \overset{\to}{c}$

$⇒ \left(\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b}\right) \cdot \overset{\to}{c} = {\left|\overset{\to}{c}\right|}^{2} = {\left(\sqrt{{1}^{2} + {1}^{2}}\right)}^{2} = 2$

Here, $\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{c} = \left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & - 1\end{cases}\right| = - 2\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$

Projection of $\overset{\to}{b}$ on $\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{c} = ℓ$

$⇒ \dfrac{\left|\overset{\to}{b} \cdot \left(\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{c}\right)\right|}{\left|\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{c}\right|} = ℓ$

$⇒ \dfrac{\left|\left(\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b}\right) \cdot \overset{\to}{c}\right|}{\sqrt{{2}^{2} + 1 + 1}} = ℓ$

$∴ ℓ = \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{6}} ⇒ {ℓ}^{2} = \dfrac{4}{6}$

So, $3{ℓ}^{2} = 2$

$⇒ 2ab + 2b - 2ab - a - 2bc - c + 2bc = 0$

$⇒ 2b - a - c = 0 ⇒ 2b = a + c$

questions.q: Let a vector $\overset{\to}{a}$ be coplanar with vectors $\overset{\to}{b} = 2\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$ and $\overset{\to}{c} = \overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k} .$ If $\overset{\to}{a}$ is perpendicular to $\overset{\to}{d} = 3\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + 6\overset{^}{k},$ and $| \overset{\to}{a} | = \sqrt{10} .$ Then a possible value of $\left[\begin{cases}\overset{\to}{a} & \overset{\to}{b} & \overset{\to}{c}\end{cases}\right] + \left[\begin{cases}\overset{\to}{a} & \overset{\to}{b} & \overset{\to}{d}\end{cases}\right] + \left[\begin{cases}\overset{\to}{a} & \overset{\to}{c} & \overset{\to}{d}\end{cases}\right]$ is equal to:
questions.solution:
Given, a vector $\overset{\to}{a}$ is coplanar with vectors $\overset{\to}{b} = 2\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$ and $\overset{\to}{c} = \overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$ and $\overset{\to}{a}$ is perpendicular to $\overset{\to}{d} = 3\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + 6\overset{^}{k},$ and $| \overset{\to}{a} | = \sqrt{10} .$

If a vector $\overset{\to}{a}$ is coplanar with the vectors $\overset{\to}{b} \text{ and } \overset{\to}{c}$ then it can be expressed as the linear combination of the vectors.

Thus, $\overset{\to}{a} = \lambda\overset{\to}{b} + \mu\overset{\to}{c}$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{a} = \lambda\left(2\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + k\right) + \mu\left(\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + k\right)$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{a} = \overset{^}{i}\left(2\lambda + \mu\right) + \overset{^}{j}\left(\lambda - \mu\right) + \overset{^}{k}\left(\lambda + \mu\right)$

Also, it is given that $\overset{\to}{a}$ is perpendicular to $\overset{\to}{d},$ and we know that if two vectors are perpendicular, then $\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{d} = 0$

$⇒ 3\left(2\lambda + \mu\right) + 2\left(\lambda - \mu\right) + 6\left(\lambda + \mu\right) = 0$

$⇒ 14\lambda + 7\mu = 0$

$⇒ \mu = - 2\lambda$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{a} = \left(0\right)\overset{^}{i} + 3\lambda\overset{^}{j} + \left(- \lambda\right)\overset{^}{k}$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{a} = \lambda\left(3\overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}\right)$

$⇒ | \overset{\to}{a} | = \sqrt{10} | \lambda |$

Given $\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right| = \sqrt{10}$

$⇒ | \lambda | = 1$

$⇒ \lambda = 1$ or $- 1$

Also, if $\overset{\to}{a}, \overset{\to}{b} \text{ and } \overset{\to}{c}$ are coplanar, then $[ \overset{\to}{a}\overset{\to}{b}\overset{\to}{c} ] = 0$

Now, $[ \overset{\to}{a}\overset{\to}{b}\overset{\to}{c} ] + [ \overset{\to}{a}\overset{\to}{b}\overset{\to}{d} ] + [ \overset{\to}{a}\overset{\to}{c}\overset{\to}{d} ]$

$= 0 + [ \overset{\to}{a}\overset{\to}{b}\overset{\to}{d} ] + [ \overset{\to}{a}\overset{\to}{c}\overset{\to}{d} ] = [ \overset{\to}{a}\overset{\to}{b} + \overset{\to}{c}\overset{\to}{d} ]$

On putting the values of the vectors for finding the box product, we get

$= \left|\begin{cases}0 & 3\lambda & - \lambda \\ 3 & 0 & 2 \\ 3 & 2 & 6\end{cases}\right|$

$= - 3\lambda ( 12 ) - \lambda ( 6 ) = - 42\lambda = - 42$ or $42 .$

questions.q: Let three vectors $\overset{\to}{a}, \overset{\to}{b}$ and $\overset{\to}{c}$ be such that $\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b} = \overset{\to}{c}, \overset{\to}{b} \times \overset{\to}{c} = \overset{\to}{a}$ and $| \overset{\to}{a} | = 2 .$ Then which one of the following is not true?
questions.solution:
The first option is $\overset{\to}{a} \times \left(\left(\overset{\to}{b} + \overset{\to}{c}\right) \times \left(\overset{\to}{b} - \overset{\to}{c}\right)\right)$

$= \overset{\to}{a} \times \left(\left(\overset{\to}{b} \times \overset{\to}{b} - \overset{\to}{b} \times \overset{\to}{c} + \overset{\to}{c} \times \overset{\to}{b} - \overset{\to}{c} \times \overset{\to}{c}\right)\right)$

But, we know that $\overset{\to}{b} \times \overset{\to}{b} = 0 = \overset{\to}{c} \times \overset{\to}{c}$

$= \overset{\to}{a} \times \left(\overset{\to}{c} \times \overset{\to}{b} - \overset{\to}{b} \times \overset{\to}{c}\right)$

Given, $\overset{\to}{b} \times \overset{\to}{c} = \overset{\to}{a}, ⇒ \overset{\to}{c} \times \overset{\to}{b} = - \overset{\to}{a}$

$= \overset{\to}{a} \times \left(- \overset{\to}{a} - \overset{\to}{b} \times \overset{\to}{c}\right)$

$= \left(- \overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{a}\right) - \left(\overset{\to}{a} \times \left(\overset{\to}{b} \times \overset{\to}{c}\right)\right)$

$= 0 - \left(\overset{\to}{a} \times \left(\overset{\to}{b} \times \overset{\to}{c}\right)\right) = - \left(\overset{\to}{a} \times \left(\overset{\to}{b} \times \overset{\to}{c}\right)\right)$

$= - ( \overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{a} ) = \overset{\to}{0}$

$∵ \overset{\to}{b} \times \overset{\to}{c} = \overset{\to}{a}$

Hence, the option $\left(A\right)$ is correct.

For the second option, we have

Projection of $\overset{\to}{a}$ on $\overset{\to}{b} \times \overset{\to}{c}$ is

$= \dfrac{\overset{\to}{a} \cdot ( \overset{\to}{b} \times \overset{\to}{c} )}{| \overset{\to}{b} \times \overset{\to}{c} |} = \dfrac{\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{a}}{| \overset{\to}{a} |}$

Using, $\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{a} = {\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|}^{2},$ we get

$= \dfrac{{\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|}^{2}}{\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|} = \left|\overset{\to}{a}\right| = 2 .$

Hence, the option $\left(B\right)$ is correct.

For the third option, we have $\left[\begin{cases}\overset{\to}{a} & \overset{\to}{b} & \overset{\to}{c}\end{cases}\right] + \left[\begin{cases}\overset{\to}{c} & \overset{\to}{a} & \overset{\to}{b}\end{cases}\right]$

We know that $\left[\begin{cases}\overset{\to}{a} & \overset{\to}{b} & \overset{\to}{c}\end{cases}\right] = \left[\begin{cases}\overset{\to}{c} & \overset{\to}{a} & \overset{\to}{b}\end{cases}\right],$ and $\left[\begin{cases}\overset{\to}{a} & \overset{\to}{b} & \overset{\to}{c}\end{cases}\right] = \overset{\to}{a} \cdot ( \overset{\to}{b} \times \overset{\to}{c} ) ,$

$⇒ \left[\begin{cases}\overset{\to}{a} & \overset{\to}{b} & \overset{\to}{c}\end{cases}\right] + \left[\begin{cases}\overset{\to}{c} & \overset{\to}{a} & \overset{\to}{b}\end{cases}\right] = 2\left[\begin{cases}\overset{\to}{a} & \overset{\to}{b} & \overset{\to}{c}\end{cases}\right] = 2\overset{\to}{a} \cdot ( \overset{\to}{b} \times \overset{\to}{c} )$

$= 2\left(\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{a}\right) = 2 | \overset{\to}{a}{|}^{2} = 2 \times {2}^{2} = 8 .$

Hence, the option $\left(C\right)$ is correct.

For the fourth option, we have

$\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b} = \overset{\to}{c}$ and $\overset{\to}{b} \times \overset{\to}{c} = \overset{\to}{a}$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{a}, \overset{\to}{b}, \overset{\to}{c}$ are mutually perpendicular vectors.

$∴ | \overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b} | = | \overset{\to}{c} | ⇒ \left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right| = \left|\overset{\to}{c}\right|$

$⇒ \left|\overset{\to}{b}\right| = \dfrac{\left|\overset{\to}{c}\right|}{2} . . . \left(i\right)$

Also, $| \overset{\to}{b} \times \overset{\to}{c} | = | \overset{\to}{a} |$

$⇒ | \overset{\to}{b} | | \overset{\to}{c} | = 2$

On putting the value from equation $\left(i\right),$ we get

$⇒ \left(\dfrac{| \overset{\to}{c} |}{2}\right) | \overset{\to}{c} | = 2$

$⇒ | \overset{\to}{c}{|}^{2} = 4$

$⇒ | \overset{\to}{c} | = 2$ and $| \overset{\to}{b} | = 1$

$| 3\overset{\to}{a} + \overset{\to}{b} - 2\overset{\to}{c}{|}^{2} = ( 3\overset{\to}{a} + \overset{\to}{b} - 2\overset{\to}{c} ) \cdot ( 3\overset{\to}{a} + \overset{\to}{b} - 2\overset{\to}{c} )$

The vectors are mutually perpendicular to each other, hence

$| 3\overset{\to}{a} + \overset{\to}{b} - 2\overset{\to}{c}{|}^{2} = 9 | \overset{\to}{a}{|}^{2} + | \overset{\to}{b}{|}^{2} + 4 | \overset{\to}{c}{|}^{2}$\left[∵ \overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{b} = \overset{\to}{b} \cdot \overset{\to}{c} = \overset{\to}{c} \cdot \overset{\to}{a} = 0\right]$

$= ( 9 \times 4 ) + 1 + ( 4 \times 4 )$

$= 36 + 1 + 16 = 53 .$

Hence, the option $\left(D\right)$ is not correct.

questions.q: For $p > 0,$ a vector $\overset{\to}{v}2 = 2\overset{^}{i} + \left(p + 1\right)\overset{^}{j}$ is obtained by rotating the vector $\overset{\to}{v}1 = \sqrt{3}p\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j}$ by an angle $\theta$ about origin in counter clockwise direction. If $tan\theta = \dfrac{\left(\alpha\sqrt{3} - 2\right)}{\left(4\sqrt{3} + 3\right)}$, then the value of $\alpha$ is equal to
questions.solution:
We have,

$\overset{\to}{v}1 = \sqrt{3}p\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j}$

$\overset{\to}{v}2 = 2\overset{^}{i} + \left(p + 1\right)\overset{^}{j}$

$tan\theta = \dfrac{\left(\alpha\sqrt{3} - 2\right)}{\left(4\sqrt{3} + 3\right)}$

$\left|\overset{\to}{v}1\right| = \left|\overset{\to}{v}2\right|$

$⇒ 3{p}^{2} + 1 = 4 + ( p + 1{)}^{2}$

$⇒ 2{p}^{2} - 2p - 4 = 0$

$⇒ {p}^{2} - p - 2 = 0$

$⇒ p = 2, - 1$ (rejected)

Now,

$cos\theta = \dfrac{\overset{\to}{v}1 \cdot \overset{\to}{v}2}{\left|\overset{\to}{v}1\right| \cdot \left|\overset{\to}{v}2\right|} = \dfrac{2\sqrt{3}p + ( p + 1 )}{\sqrt{( p + 1{)}^{2} + 4}\sqrt{3{p}^{2} + 1}}$

$⇒ cos\theta = \dfrac{4\sqrt{3} + 3}{\sqrt{13}\sqrt{13}} = \dfrac{4\sqrt{3} + 3}{13}$

$⇒ tan\theta = \dfrac{\sqrt{112 - 24\sqrt{3}}}{4\sqrt{3} + 3} = \dfrac{\sqrt{{\left(6\sqrt{3} - 2\right)}^{2}}}{4\sqrt{3} + 3}$

$⇒ tan\theta = \dfrac{6\sqrt{3} - 2}{4\sqrt{3} + 3} = \dfrac{\alpha\sqrt{3} - 2}{4\sqrt{3} + 3}$

$⇒ \alpha = 6$

$\overset{\to}{v}2 = 2\overset{^}{i} + \left(p + 1\right)\overset{^}{j}$

$tan\theta = \dfrac{\left(\alpha\sqrt{3} - 2\right)}{\left(4\sqrt{3} + 3\right)}$

$\left|\overset{\to}{v}1\right| = \left|\overset{\to}{v}2\right|$

$⇒ 3{p}^{2} + 1 = 4 + ( p + 1{)}^{2}$

$⇒ 2{p}^{2} - 2p - 4 = 0$

$⇒ {p}^{2} - p - 2 = 0$

$⇒ p = 2, - 1$ (rejected)

Now,

$cos\theta = \dfrac{\overset{\to}{v}1 \cdot \overset{\to}{v}2}{\left|\overset{\to}{v}1\right| \cdot \left|\overset{\to}{v}2\right|} = \dfrac{2\sqrt{3}p + ( p + 1 )}{\sqrt{( p + 1{)}^{2} + 4}\sqrt{3{p}^{2} + 1}}$

$⇒ cos\theta = \dfrac{4\sqrt{3} + 3}{\sqrt{13}\sqrt{13}} = \dfrac{4\sqrt{3} + 3}{13}$

$⇒ tan\theta = \dfrac{\sqrt{112 - 24\sqrt{3}}}{4\sqrt{3} + 3} = \dfrac{\sqrt{{\left(6\sqrt{3} - 2\right)}^{2}}}{4\sqrt{3} + 3}$

$⇒ tan\theta = \dfrac{6\sqrt{3} - 2}{4\sqrt{3} + 3} = \dfrac{\alpha\sqrt{3} - 2}{4\sqrt{3} + 3}$

$⇒ \alpha = 6$

questions.q: Let $\overset{\to}{a} = 2\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} - 2\overset{^}{k}$ and $\overset{\to}{b} = \overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j}$. If $\overset{\to}{c}$ is a vector such that $\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{c} = | \overset{\to}{c} | , | \overset{\to}{c} - \overset{\to}{a} | = 2\sqrt{2}$ and the angle between $\left(\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b}\right) and \overset{\to}{c}$ is $\dfrac{\pi}{6}$, then the value of $\left|\left(\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b}\right)$ \times \overset{\to}{c}\right|$ is:$
questions.solution:
We have,

$\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right| = 3 = a$

$\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{c} = \left|\overset{\to}{c}\right| = c$

Now,

$\left|\overset{\to}{c} - \overset{\to}{a}\right| = 2\sqrt{2}$

$⇒ {\left|\overset{\to}{c} - \overset{\to}{a}\right|}^{2} = 8$

$⇒ {c}^{2} + {a}^{2} - 2\overset{\to}{c} \cdot \overset{\to}{a} = 8$

$⇒ {c}^{2} + 9 - 2\left(c\right) = 8$

$⇒ {c}^{2} - 2c + 1 = 0$

$⇒ {\left(c - 1\right)}^{2} = 0$

$⇒ c = 1 = \left|\overset{\to}{c}\right|$

Now,

$\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b} = \left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 2 & 1 & - 2 \\ 1 & 1 & 0\end{cases}\right|$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b} = 2\overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$

$⇒ \left|\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b}\right| = \sqrt{{2}^{2} + {\left(- 2\right)}^{2} + {1}^{2}} = 3$

Now,

$\left|\left(\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b}\right) \times \overset{\to}{c}\right| = \left|\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b}\right|\left|\overset{\to}{c}\right|sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)$

$⇒ \left|\left(\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b}\right) \times \overset{\to}{c}\right| = 3 \cdot 1 \cdot \dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{3}{2}$

questions.q: Let $\overset{\to}{a}, \overset{\to}{b}, \overset{\to}{c}$ be three mutually perpendicular vectors of the same magnitude and equally inclined at an angle $\theta$, with the vector $\overset{\to}{a} + \overset{\to}{b} + \overset{\to}{c}$. Then $36\cos^{2}2\theta$ is equal to
questions.solution:
We have,

$\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right| = \left|\overset{\to}{b}\right| = \left|\overset{\to}{c}\right|

$\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{b} = \overset{\to}{b} \cdot \overset{\to}{c} = \overset{\to}{c} \cdot \overset{\to}{a} = 0$

Since, vectors are mutually perpendicular and of equally magnitude, hence let

$\overset{\to}{a} = \overset{^}{i}, \overset{\to}{b} = \overset{^}{j}, \overset{\to}{c} = \overset{^}{k}$

Now,

\left(\overset{\to}{a} + \overset{\to}{b} + \overset{\to}{c}\right) \cdot \overset{\to}{a} = \left(\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}\right) \cdot \overset{^}{i}$

$⇒ \left(\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}\right) \cdot \overset{^}{i} = \sqrt{3} \cdot 1 \cdot cos\theta$

$⇒ 1 + 0 + 0 = \sqrt{3} \cdot 1 \cdot cos\theta$

$⇒ \sqrt{3}cos\theta = 1$

$⇒ cos\theta = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$

$⇒ cos2\theta = 2$\cos^{2}\theta$ - 1 = \dfrac{2}{3} -1$

$⇒ cos2\theta = - \dfrac{1}{3}$

$⇒ $\cos^{2}2\theta$ = \dfrac{1}{9}$

$⇒ 36\cos^{2}2\theta = 4$

questions.solution:
$\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right| = 8, \left|\overset{\to}{b}\right| = 7, \left|\overset{\to}{c}\right| = 10$

$cos\theta = \dfrac{| \overset{\to}{b}{|}^{2} + | \overset{\to}{c}{|}^{2} - | \overset{\to}{a}{|}^{2}}{2 | \overset{\to}{b} | | \overset{\to}{c} |} = \dfrac{17}{28}$

Projection of $\overset{\to}{c}$ on $\overset{\to}{b}$

$= | \overset{\to}{c} | cos\theta$

$= 10 \times \dfrac{17}{28}$

$= \dfrac{85}{14}$

questions.q: A vector $\overset{\to}{a}$ has components $3p$ and $1$ with respect to a rectangular cartesian system. This system is rotated through a certain angle about the origin in the counter clockwise sense. If, with respect to new system, $\overset{\to}{a}$ has components $p + 1$ and $\sqrt{10},$ then a value of $p$ is equal to:
questions.solution:
$\overset{\to}{a}Old = 3p\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j}$

$\overset{\to}{a}New = ( p + 1 ) \overset{^}{i} + \sqrt{10}\overset{^}{j}$

$⇒ \left|\overset{\to}{a}Old\right| = \left|\overset{\to}{a}New\right|$

$⇒ 9{p}^{2} + 1 = {p}^{2} + 2p + 1 + 10$

$8{p}^{2} - 2p - 10 = 0$

$4{p}^{2} - p - 5 = 0$

$( 4p - 5 ) ( p + 1 ) = 0 ⇒ p = \dfrac{5}{4}, - 1$

questions.q: Let $\overset{\to}{x}$ be a vector in the plane containing vectors $\overset{\to}{a} = 2\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$ and $\overset{\to}{b} = \overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k} .$ If the vector $\overset{\to}{x}$ is perpendicular to $( 3\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k} )$ and its projection on $\overset{\to}{a}$ is $\dfrac{17\sqrt{6}}{2},$ then the value of ${\left|\overset{\to}{x}\right|}^{2}$ is equal to _______.
questions.solution:
A plane containing two vectors can be expressed as a linear combination of the vectors.

Hence, let $\overset{\to}{x} = \lambda\overset{\to}{a} + \mu\overset{\to}{b} ( \lambda$ and $\mu$ are scalars$) .$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{x} = \overset{^}{i} ( 2\lambda + \mu ) + \overset{^}{j} ( 2\mu - \lambda ) + \overset{^}{k} ( \lambda - \mu )$

Since $\overset{\to}{x}$ is perpendicular to $3\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k},$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{x} \cdot \left(3\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}\right) = 0$

$⇒ \left(\overset{^}{i} ( 2\lambda + \mu ) + \overset{^}{j} ( 2\mu - \lambda ) + \overset{^}{k} ( \lambda - \mu )\right) \cdot \left(3\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}\right) = 0$

$⇒ 3 ( 2\lambda + \mu ) + 2 ( 2\mu - \lambda ) - ( \lambda - \mu ) = 0$

$⇒ 3\lambda + 8\mu = 0 . . . \left(1\right)$

Also, the projection of $\overset{\to}{x}$ on $\overset{\to}{a}$ is $\dfrac{17\sqrt{6}}{2}$

$⇒ \dfrac{\overset{\to}{x} \cdot \overset{\to}{a}}{| \overset{\to}{a} |} = \dfrac{17\sqrt{6}}{2}$

$⇒ \dfrac{\left(\overset{^}{i} ( 2\lambda + \mu ) + \overset{^}{j} ( 2\mu - \lambda ) + \overset{^}{k} ( \lambda - \mu )\right) \cdot \left(2\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}\right)}{\sqrt{{2}^{2} + {1}^{2} + {1}^{2}}} = \dfrac{17\sqrt{6}}{2}$

$⇒ \dfrac{2 ( 2\lambda + \mu ) - ( 2\mu - \lambda ) + ( \lambda - \mu )}{\sqrt{6}} = \dfrac{17\sqrt{6}}{2}$

$⇒ 6\lambda - \mu = 51 . . . \left(2\right)$

On solving the equations $( 1 )$ and $( 2 ) ,$ we get $\lambda = 8, \mu = - 3 .$

Thus, $\overset{\to}{x} = 13\overset{^}{i} - 14\overset{^}{j} + 11\overset{^}{k}$

$⇒ \left|\overset{\to}{x}\right| = \sqrt{{13}^{2} + {\left(- 14\right)}^{2} + {11}^{2}}$

$⇒ | \overset{\to}{x}{|}^{2} = 486 .$

questions.q: Let $O$ be the origin. Let $\overset{\to}{OP} = x\overset{^}{i} + y\overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}$ and $\overset{\to}{OQ} = - \overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + 3x\overset{^}{k}, x, y \in R, x > 0,$ be such that $| \overset{\to}{PQ} | = \sqrt{20}$ and the vector $\overset{\to}{OP}$ is perpendicular to $\overset{\to}{OQ} .$ If $\overset{\to}{OR} = 3\overset{^}{i} + z\overset{^}{j} - 7\overset{^}{k}, z \in R,$ is coplanar with $\overset{\to}{OP}$ and $\overset{\to}{OQ},$ then the value of ${x}^{2} + {y}^{2} + {z}^{2}$ is equal to
questions.solution:
If two vectors ${a}_{1}\overset{^}{i} + {b}_{1}\overset{^}{j} + {c}_{1}\overset{^}{k}$ and ${a}_{2}\overset{^}{i} + {b}_{2}\overset{^}{j} + {c}_{2}\overset{^}{k}$ are perpendicular, then ${a}_{1}{a}_{2} + {b}_{1}{b}_{2} + {c}_{1}{c}_{2} = 0 .$

Given $\overset{\to}{OP} ⊥ \overset{\to}{OQ}$

$⇒ - x + 2y - 3x = 0$

$⇒ y = 2x . . . \left(i\right)$

Also, $\overset{\to}{PQ} = \overset{\to}{OQ} - \overset{\to}{OP}$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{PQ} = \left(- 1 - x\right)\overset{^}{i} + \left(2 - y\right)\overset{^}{j} + \left(3x + 1\right)\overset{^}{k}$

And $\left|\overset{\to}{PQ}\right| = \sqrt{20}$

$⇒ \sqrt{{\left(- 1 - x\right)}^{2} + {\left(2 - y\right)}^{2} + {\left(3x + 1\right)}^{2}} = \sqrt{20}$

$⇒ ( x + 1{)}^{2} + ( y - 2{)}^{2} + ( 1 + 3x{)}^{2} = 20$

Put the value from equation $\left(i\right),$ to get

$( x + 1{)}^{2} + ( 2x - 2{)}^{2} + ( 1 + 3x{)}^{2} = 20$

$⇒ {x}^{2} + 2x + 1 + 4{x}^{2} - 8x + 4 + 1 + 6x + 9{x}^{2} = 20$

$⇒ 14{x}^{2} + 6 = 20$

$⇒ 14{x}^{2} = 14$

$⇒ x = \pm 1,$ but given $x > 0$

$⇒ x = 1$ and $y = 2 .$

Now $\overset{\to}{OP}, \overset{\to}{OQ}, \overset{\to}{OR}$ are coplanar and we know that the three vectors ${a}_{1}\overset{^}{i} + {b}_{1}\overset{^}{j} + {c}_{1}\overset{^}{k}, {a}_{2}\overset{^}{i} + {b}_{2}\overset{^}{j} + {c}_{2}\overset{^}{k}$ and ${a}_{3}\overset{^}{i} + {b}_{3}\overset{^}{j} + {c}_{3}\overset{^}{k}$ are coplanar, then $\left|\begin{cases}{a}_{1} & {b}_{1} & {c}_{1} \\ {a}_{2} & {b}_{2} & {c}_{2} \\ {a}_{3} & {b}_{3} & {c}_{3}\end{cases}\right| = 0$

$⇒ \left|\begin{cases}x & y & - 1 \\ - 1 & 2 & 3x \\ 3 & z & - 7\end{cases}\right| = 0$

$⇒ \left|\begin{cases}1 & 2 & - 1 \\ - 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 3 & z & - 7\end{cases}\right| = 0$

$⇒ 1 ( - 14 - 3z ) - 2 ( 7 - 9 ) - 1 ( - z - 6 ) = 0$

questions.question: Let $O$ be the origin. Given $\overset{\to}{OP} ⊥ \overset{\to}{OQ}$

$⇒ - x + 2y - 3x = 0$

$⇒ y = 2x . . . \left(i\right)$

Also, $\overset{\to}{PQ} = \overset{\to}{OQ} - \overset{\to}{OP}$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{PQ} = \left(- 1 - x\right)\overset{^}{i} + \left(2 - y\right)\overset{^}{j} + \left(3x + 1\right)\overset{^}{k}$

And $\left|\overset{\to}{PQ}\right| = \sqrt{20}$

$⇒ \sqrt{{\left(- 1 - x\right)}^{2} + {\left(2 - y\right)}^{2} + {\left(3x + 1\right)}^{2}} = \sqrt{20}$

$⇒ ( x + 1{)}^{2} + ( y - 2{)}^{2} + ( 1 + 3x{)}^{2} = 20$

Put the value from equation $\left(i\right),$ to get

$( x + 1{)}^{2} + ( 2x - 2{)}^{2} + ( 1 + 3x{)}^{2} = 20$

$⇒ {x}^{2} + 2x + 1 + 4{x}^{2} - 8x + 4 + 1 + 6x + 9{x}^{2} = 20$

$⇒ 14{x}^{2} + 6 = 20$

$⇒ 14{x}^{2} = 14$

$⇒ x = \pm 1,$ but given $x > 0$

$⇒ x = 1$ and $y = 2 .$

$⇒ \left|\begin{cases}x & y & - 1 \\ - 1 & 2 & 3x \\ 3 & z & - 7\end{cases}\right| = 0$

$⇒ \left|\begin{cases}1 & 2 & - 1 \\ - 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 3 & z & - 7\end{cases}\right| = 0$

$⇒ 1 ( - 14 - 3z ) - 2 ( 7 - 9 ) - 1 ( - z - 6 ) = 0$

$⇒ z = - 2$

$∴ {x}^{2} + {y}^{2} + {z}^{2} = 1 + 4 + 4 = 9 .$

${R}_{1} \to {R}_{1} + {R}_{3}$

questions.solution:
Let angle between $\overset{\to}{a}\text{and}\overset{\to}{b} = \alpha$.
So, $\sqrt{3} | \overset{\to}{a} + \overset{\to}{b} | + | \overset{\to}{a} - \overset{\to}{b} | = \sqrt{3}\sqrt{2 + 2cos \alpha} + \sqrt{2 - 2cos \alpha}$
$= \sqrt{3}\sqrt{2 \times 2\cos^{2}\dfrac{\alpha}{2}} + \sqrt{2 \times 2\sin^{2}\dfrac{\alpha}{2}}$
$= 2\left(\sqrt{3}\left|cos\dfrac{\alpha}{2}\right| + \left|sin\dfrac{\alpha}{2}\right|\right)$

As $\alpha \in \left[0, \pi\right] ⇒ \dfrac{\alpha}{2} \in \left[0, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right]$

So, given expression is

$= 2\left(\sqrt{3}cos\dfrac{\alpha}{2} + sin\dfrac{\alpha}{2}\right)$
Thus, maximum value is$= 2\sqrt{{\left(\sqrt{3}\right)}^{2} + {1}^{2}} = 2 \times 2 = 4$

questions.q: If $\overset{\to}{a} = 2\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}$, then, the value of ${\left|\overset{^}{i} \times \left(\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{^}{i}\right)\right|}^{2} + {\left|\overset{^}{j} \times \left(\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{^}{j}\right)\right|}^{2} + \left|\overset{^}{k} \times \left(\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{^}{k}\right)\right|{}^{2}$, is equal to :
questions.solution:
Let $\overset{\to}{a} = x\overset{^}{i} + y\overset{^}{j} + z\overset{^}{k}$, and using vector triple product, we have,
$\overset{^}{i} \times \left(\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{^}{i}\right) = \left(\overset{^}{i} . \overset{^}{i}\right)\overset{\to}{a} - \left(\overset{^}{i} . \overset{\to}{a}\right)\overset{^}{i} = y\overset{^}{j} + z\overset{^}{k}$
Similarly,

$\overset{^}{j} \times \left(\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{^}{j}\right) = x\overset{^}{i} + z\overset{^}{k}$

and $\overset{^}{k} \times \left(\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{^}{k}\right) = x\overset{^}{i} + y\overset{^}{k}$

Thus,

${\left|\overset{^}{i} \times \left(\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{^}{i}\right)\right|}^{2} + {\left|\overset{^}{j} \times \left(\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{^}{j}\right)\right|}^{2} + {\left|\overset{^}{k} \times \left(\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{^}{k}\right)\right|}^{2}$
$= {\left|y\overset{^}{j} + z\overset{^}{k}\right|}^{2} + {\left|x\overset{^}{i} + z\overset{^}{k}\right|}^{2} + {\left|x\overset{^}{i} + y\overset{^}{j}\right|}^{2}$

$= 2 | \overset{\to}{a}{|}^{2} = 2 ( 9 ) = 18$

Thus,

questions.solution:
$f\left(x\right) = \left[\overset{\to}{a}\overset{\to}{b}\overset{\to}{c}\right] = \left|\begin{array}{ll}x - 23 \\ - 2x - 1 \\ 7 - 2x\end{array}\right|$

$\overset{\to}{a} . \overset{\to}{b} + \overset{\to}{b} . \overset{\to}{c} + \overset{\to}{c} . \overset{\to}{a} = - 9 - 13 = - 22$

Let $acos\theta = bcos\left(\theta + \dfrac{2\pi}{3}\right) = ccos\left(\theta + \dfrac{4\pi}{3}\right) = k$

$⇒ a = \dfrac{k}{cos\theta}, b = \dfrac{k}{cos\left(\theta + \dfrac{2\pi}{3}\right)}, c = \dfrac{k}{cos\left(\theta + \dfrac{4\pi}{3}\right)}$

$⇒ ab + bc + ca = {k}^{2}\dfrac{cos\left(\theta + \dfrac{4\pi}{3}\right) + cos\theta + cos\left(\theta + \dfrac{2\pi}{3}\right)}{cos\left(\theta + \dfrac{4\pi}{3}\right)cos\thetacos\left(\theta + \dfrac{2\pi}{3}\right)}$

$= {k}^{2}\left[\dfrac{cos\theta + 2cos\left(\theta + \pi\right) . cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)}{cos\theta . cos\left(\theta + \dfrac{2\pi}{3}\right) . cos\left(\theta + \dfrac{4\pi}{3}\right)}\right]$

$= {k}^{2}\left[\dfrac{cos\theta - 2cos\theta . \dfrac{1}{2}}{cos\theta . cos\left(\theta + \dfrac{2\pi}{3}\right) . cos\left(\theta + \dfrac{4\pi}{3}\right)}\right] = 0$

Let $ϕ$ be the angle between two given vectors.

$∴ cosϕ = \dfrac{\left(a\overset{^}{i} + b\overset{^}{j} + c\overset{^}{k}\right) . \left(b\overset{^}{i} + c\overset{^}{j} + a\overset{^}{k}\right)}{\sqrt{{a}^{2} + {b}^{2} + {c}^{2}} \cdot \sqrt{{b}^{2} + {c}^{2} + {a}^{2}}} = \dfrac{ab + bc + ca}{{a}^{2} + {b}^{2} + {c}^{2}} = 0$

$⇒ ϕ = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$

questions.q: Let $\overset{\to}{a}, \overset{\to}{b}$ and $\overset{\to}{c}$ be three unit vectors such that ${\left|\overset{\to}{a} - \overset{\to}{b}\right|}^{2} + {\left|\overset{\to}{a} - \overset{\to}{c}\right|}^{2} = 8$. Then ${\left|\overset{\to}{a} + 2\overset{\to}{b}\right|}^{2} + {\left|\overset{\to}{a} + 2\overset{\to}{c}\right|}^{2}$ is equal to
questions.solution:
$\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right| = \left|\overset{\to}{b}\right| = \left|\overset{\to}{c}\right| = 1$

${\left|\overset{\to}{a} - \overset{\to}{b}\right|}^{2} + {\left|\overset{\to}{a} - \overset{\to}{c}\right|}^{2} = 8$

$⇒ 1 + 1 - 2\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{b} + 1 + 1 - 2\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{c} = 8$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{b} + \overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{c} = - 2$

Now ${\left|\overset{\to}{a} + 2\overset{\to}{b}\right|}^{2} + {\left|\overset{\to}{a} + 2\overset{\to}{c}\right|}^{2}$

$= {\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|}^{2} + 4{\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|}^{2} + 4\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{b} + {\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|}^{2} + 4{\left|\overset{\to}{c}\right|}^{2} + 4\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{c}$

$= 2{\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|}^{2} + 4{\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|}^{2} + 4{\left|\overset{\to}{c}\right|}^{2} + 4\left(\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{b} + \overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{c}\right)$

$= 2 + 4 + 4 + 4 \left(- 2\right)

$= 2$

$

questions.q: Let $\overset{\to}{a}, \overset{\to}{b}$ and $\overset{\to}{c}$ be three vectors such that $\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right| = \sqrt{3}, \left|\overset{\to}{b}\right| = 5, \overset{\to}{b} ∙ \overset{\to}{c} = 10$ and the angle between $\overset{\to}{b} and \overset{\to}{c}$ is $\dfrac{\pi}{3} .$ If $\overset{\to}{a}$ is perpendicular to the vector $\overset{\to}{b} \times \overset{\to}{c},$ then $\left|\overset{\to}{a} \times \left(\overset{\to}{b} \times \overset{\to}{c}\right)\right|$ is equal to ____________.
questions.solution:
$\overset{\to}{b} . \overset{\to}{c} = 10 ⇒ \left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|\left|\overset{\to}{c}\right|cos ⁡ \left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) = 10 ⇒ 5 . \left|\overset{\to}{c}\right| . \dfrac{1}{2} = 10$

$⇒ \left|\overset{\to}{c}\right| = 4$

Also, $\overset{\to}{a} . \left(\overset{\to}{b} \times \overset{\to}{c}\right) = 0$

$\left|\overset{\to}{a} \times \left(\overset{\to}{b} \times \overset{\to}{c}\right)\right| = \left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|\left|\overset{\to}{b} \times \overset{\to}{c}\right|sin ⁡ \left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$

$⇒ \sqrt{3} \times \left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|\left|\overset{\to}{c}\right|sin ⁡ \dfrac{\pi}{3} \times 1$

$⇒ \sqrt{3} \times 5 \times 4 \times \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} = 30$

questions.q: If the vectors, $\overset{\to}{p} = \left(a + 1\right)\overset{^}{i} + a\overset{^}{j} + a\overset{^}{k}, \overset{\to}{q} = a\overset{^}{i} + \left(a + 1\right)\overset{^}{j} + a\overset{^}{k}$ and $\overset{\to}{r} = a\overset{^}{i} + a\overset{^}{j} + \left(a + 1\right)\overset{^}{k}\left(a \in R\right)$ are coplanar and $3{\left(\overset{\to}{p} . \overset{\to}{q}\right)}^{2} - \lambda{\left|\overset{\to}{r} \times \overset{\to}{q}\right|}^{2} = 0$ , then the value of $\lambda$ is ________
questions.solution:
$\left|\begin{cases}a + 1 & a & a \\ a & a + 1 & a \\ a & a & a + 1\end{cases}\right| = 0 ⇒ a + 1 + a + a = 0 ⇒ a = - \dfrac{1}{3}$
$\overset{\to}{P} = \dfrac{2}{3}\overset{^}{i} - \dfrac{1}{3}\overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}$
$\overset{\to}{Q} = \dfrac{1}{3}\left(- \overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}\right)
$\overset{\to}{R} = $\dfrac{1}{3}\left(- \overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}\right)
$\overset{\to}{P} . \overset{\to}{Q} = $\dfrac{1}{9}\left(- 2 - 2 + 1\right) = - \dfrac{1}{3}$
$\overset{\to}{R} \times \overset{\to}{Q} = \dfrac{1}{9}\left|\begin{cases}i & j & k \\ - 1 & 2 & - 1 \\ - 1 & - 1 & 2\end{cases}\right|$ = $\dfrac{1}{9}\left(i\left(4 - 1\right) - j \left(- 2 - 1\right) + k \left(1 + 2\right)\right) = \dfrac{1}{9}\left(3i + 3j + 3k\right)$ = $\dfrac{i + j + k}{3}
\left|\overset{\to}{R} \times \overset{\to}{Q}\right| = \dfrac{1}{3}\sqrt{3} ⇒ {\left|\overset{\to}{R} \times \overset{\to}{Q}\right|}^{2} = \dfrac{1}{3} 3{\left(\overset{\to}{P} . \overset{\to}{Q}\right)}^{2} - \lambda{\left|\overset{\to}{R} \times \overset{\to}{Q}\right|}^{2} = 0$
$3 . \dfrac{1}{9} -\lambda . \dfrac{1}{3} =0 ⇒ \lambda = 1$

$\overset{\to}{P} . \overset{\to}{Q} = $\dfrac{1}{9}\left(- 2 - 2 + 1\right) = - \dfrac{1}{3}$

\left|\overset{\to}{R} \times \overset{\to}{Q}\right| = \dfrac{1}{3}\sqrt{3} ⇒ {\left|\overset{\to}{R} \times \overset{\to}{Q}\right|}^{2} = \dfrac{1}{3} 3{\left(\overset{\to}{P} . \overset{\to}{Q}\right)}^{2} - \lambda{\left|\overset{\to}{R} \times \overset{\to}{Q}\right|}^{2} = 0$

questions.q: Let $\overset{\to}{a} = \overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$ and $\overset{\to}{b} = \overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$, be two vectors. If $\overset{\to}{c}$, is a vector such that $\overset{\to}{b} \times \overset{\to}{c} = \overset{\to}{b} \times \overset{\to}{a}$ and $\overset{\to}{c} ⋅ \overset{\to}{a} = 0,$ then $\overset{\to}{c} ⋅ \overset{\to}{b}$, is equal to.
questions.solution:
