Using given information $\overset{\to}{a} = \overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$ and $\overset{\to}{b} = \overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$ , we can write $\overset{\to}{a} . \overset{\to}{b} = 4$, $\overset{\to}{a} . \overset{\to}{a} = 6$
$⇒ - 4\overset{\to}{c} = 6\left(\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}\right) - 4\left(\overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}\right)$
$⇒ - 4\overset{\to}{c} = 2\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}$

questions.q: The distance of the point having position vector $- \overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + 6\overset{^}{k}$ from the straight line passing through the point $\left(2, 3, - 4\right)$ and parallel to the vector, $6\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} - 4\overset{^}{k}$ is
questions.solution:
Let, the given point be $P ≡ - \overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + 6\overset{^}{k}$ and $A ≡ \left(2, 3, - 4\right),$ hence the position vector of the point $A$ is $2\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} - 4\overset{^}{k} .$

We know that the vector joining two points $\left({x}_{1}, {y}_{1}, {z}_{1}\right)$ and $\left({x}_{2}, {y}_{2}, {z}_{2}\right)$ is $\left({x}_{2} - {x}_{1}\right)\overset{^}{i} + \left({y}_{2} - {y}_{1}\right)\overset{^}{j} + \left({z}_{2} - {z}_{1}\right)\overset{^}{k},$

Hence, the vector $\overset{\to}{AP} = \left(- 1 - 2\right)\overset{^}{i} + \left(2 - 3\right)\overset{^}{j} + \left(6 + 4\right)\overset{^}{k}$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{AP} = - 3\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + 10\overset{^}{k}$

And, $AD$ is the projection of $\overset{\to}{AP}$ on the given line i.e. $6\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} - 4\overset{^}{k}$

We know that the projection of a vector $\overset{\to}{a}$ on a vector $\overset{\to}{b}$ is $\dfrac{\left|\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{b}\right|}{\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|}$

Hence, $AD = \dfrac{\left|\overset{\to}{AP} ⋅ \overset{\to}{n}\right|}{\left|\overset{\to}{n}\right|}$

$⇒ AD = \dfrac{\left(- 3\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + 10\overset{^}{k}\right) \cdot \left(6\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} - 4\overset{^}{k}\right)}{\sqrt{{6}^{2} + {3}^{2} + {\left(- 4\right)}^{2}}}$

$⇒ AD = \dfrac{\left|- 18 - 3 - 40\right|}{\sqrt{36 + 9 + 16}}$

$⇒ AD = \sqrt{61}$ units

The distance between the points $\left({x}_{1}, {y}_{1}, {z}_{1}\right)$ and $\left({x}_{2}, {y}_{2}, {z}_{2}\right)$ is $\sqrt{{\left({x}_{1} - {x}_{2}\right)}^{2} + {\left({y}_{1} - {y}_{2}\right)}^{2} + {\left({z}_{1} - {z}_{2}\right)}^{2}}$

Thus, $AP = \sqrt{{\left(- 1 - 2\right)}^{2} + {\left(2 - 3\right)}^{2} + {\left(6 + 4\right)}^{2}} = \sqrt{110}$ units

Now, in triangle $ADP,$ by Pythagoras theorem, we have ${\left(AP\right)}^{2} = {\left(PD\right)}^{2} + {\left(AD\right)}^{2}$

$⇒ PD = \sqrt{{\left(AP\right)}^{2} - {\left(AD\right)}^{2}} = \sqrt{110 - 61} = 7$ units.

The distance between the points $\left({x}_{1}, {y}_{1}, {z}_{1}\right)$ and $\left({x}_{2}, {y}_{2}, {z}_{2}\right)$ is $\sqrt{{\left({x}_{1} - {x}_{2}\right)}^{2} + {\left({y}_{1} - {y}_{2}\right)}^{2} + {\left({z}_{1} - {z}_{2}\right)}^{2}}$

Thus, $AP = \sqrt{{\left(- 1 - 2\right)}^{2} + {\left(2 - 3\right)}^{2} + {\left(6 + 4\right)}^{2}} = \sqrt{110}$ units

Now, in triangle $ADP,$ by Pythagoras theorem, we have ${\left(AP\right)}^{2} = {\left(PD\right)}^{2} + {\left(AD\right)}^{2}$

$⇒ PD = \sqrt{{\left(AP\right)}^{2} - {\left(AD\right)}^{2}} = \sqrt{110 - 61} = 7$ units.

questions.q: If a unit vector $\overset{\to}{a}$ makes angles $\dfrac{\pi}{3}$ with $\overset{^}{i}, \dfrac{\pi}{4}$ with $\overset{^}{j}$ and $\theta \in \left(0, \pi\right)$ with $\overset{^}{k},$ then a value of $\theta$ is:
questions.solution:
The unit vector $\overset{\to}{a}$ makes angle $\dfrac{\pi}{3}, \dfrac{\pi}{4}$ and $\theta$ with $\overset{^}{i}, \overset{^}{j} \text{ and } \overset{^}{k}$ respectively.

Hence, the direction cosines of the vector $\overset{\to}{a}$ are $cos\alpha = cos\dfrac{\pi}{3} = \dfrac{1}{2}, cos\beta = cos\dfrac{\pi}{4} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$ and $cos\gamma = cos\theta$

For a line having direction cosines as $cos\alpha, cos\beta, cos\gamma$

$⇒ \cos^{2}\alpha + \cos^{2}\beta + \cos^{2}\gamma = 1$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{4} + \dfrac{1}{2} + \cos^{2}\theta = 1$

$⇒ \cos^{2}\theta = 1 - \dfrac{3}{4} = \dfrac{1}{4}$

$⇒ \cos^{2}\theta = \pm \dfrac{1}{2}$

$⇒ \theta = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$ or $\dfrac{2\pi}{3} .$

questions.q: Let $\overset{\to}{\alpha} = 3\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j}$ and $\overset{\to}{\beta} = 2\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k} .$ If $\overset{\to}{\beta} = \overset{\to}{{\beta}_{1}} - \overset{\to}{{\beta}_{2}},$ where $\overset{\to}{{\beta}_{1}}$ is parallel to $\overset{\to}{\alpha}$ and $\overset{\to}{{\beta}_{2}}$ is perpendicular to $\overset{\to}{\alpha},$ then $\overset{\to}{{\beta}_{1}} \times \overset{\to}{{\beta}_{2}}$ is equal to:
questions.solution:
If two vectors are parallel then they are proportional.

So, let $\overset{\to}{{\beta}_{1}} = k\overset{\to}{\alpha}$

Given $\overset{\to}{\beta} = \overset{\to}{{\beta}_{1}} - \overset{\to}{{\beta}_{2}}$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{\alpha} ⋅ \overset{\to}{\beta} = \overset{\to}{\alpha} ⋅ \overset{\to}{{\beta}_{1}} - \overset{\to}{\alpha} ⋅ \overset{\to}{{\beta}_{2}} . . . \left(i\right)

Now, $\overset{\to}{\alpha} \cdot \overset{\to}{\beta} = $\left(3\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j}\right) \cdot \left(2\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}\right)

$= 6 - 1 = 5$

And, $\overset{\to}{\alpha}$ is perpendicular to $\overset{\to}{{\beta}_{1}},$ hence $\overset{\to}{\alpha} ⋅ \overset{\to}{{\beta}_{1}} = 0$

And, $\overset{\to}{\alpha} ⋅ \overset{\to}{{\beta}_{2}} = \overset{\to}{\alpha} ⋅ $\left(k\overset{\to}{\alpha}\right)$ = k{$\left(\overset{\to}{\alpha}\right)$}^{2} = k{$\left|\overset{\to}{\alpha}\right|$}^{2}$

Also, \left|\overset{\to}{\alpha}\right|$= \sqrt{{3}^{2} + {1}^{2}} = \sqrt{10}

Put, all these values$ in the equation \left(i\right),$ to get $5 = k \times 10$

$∴ k = \dfrac{1}{2}$

$∴ \overset{\to}{{\beta}_{1}} = \dfrac{1}{2} ( 3\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} )$

$= \dfrac{3}{2}\overset{^}{i} + \dfrac{1}{2}\overset{^}{j}$

Now $\overset{\to}{{\beta}_{2}} = \overset{\to}{{\beta}_{1}} - \overset{\to}{\beta} = - \dfrac{1}{2}\overset{^}{i} + \dfrac{3}{2}\overset{^}{j} - 3\overset{^}{k}$

$∴ \overset{\to}{{\beta}_{1}} \times \overset{\to}{{\beta}_{2}} = \left|$\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ $\dfrac{3}{2}$ &$\dfrac{1}{2}$& 0 \\ $- \dfrac{1}{2}$ &$\dfrac{3}{2}$& - 3\end{cases}$\right|

$= \overset{^}{i}$\left(- \dfrac{3}{2} -0\right)$ - \overset{^}{j}$\left(- \dfrac{9}{2} -0\right)$ + \overset{^}{k}$\left(\dfrac{9}{4} + \dfrac{1}{4}$\right)$

$= - $\dfrac{3}{2}\overset{^}{i} + \dfrac{9}{2}$\overset{^}{j} + $\dfrac{5}{2}\overset{^}{k}$

$= \dfrac{1}{2} ($ - 3\overset{^}{i} + 9\overset{^}{j} + 5\overset{^}{k} ) .

As, We know that $\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b} = \left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 3 & 2 & x \\ 1 & - 1 & 1\end{cases}\right|$

$⇒ \left|\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b}\right| \ge 5\sqrt{\dfrac{3}{2}}$

questions.q: The magnitude of the projection of the vector $2\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$ on the vector perpendicular to the plane containing the vectors $\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$ and $\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k},$ is:
questions.solution:
Vector perpendicular to $\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$ and $\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}$

$= \left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 3\end{cases}\right| = \overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$

$∴$ Required projection

$= \dfrac{| ( 2\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k} ) ⋅ ( \overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k} ) |}{| \overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k} |}$

$= \dfrac{| 2 - 6 + 1 |}{\sqrt{6}} = \dfrac{3}{\sqrt{6}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{3}{2}}$

questions.q: Let $\overset{\to}{a}, \overset{\to}{b}$ and $\overset{\to}{c}$ be three unit vectors, out of which vectors $\overset{\to}{b}$ and $\overset{\to}{c}$ are non-parallel. If $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are the angles which vector $\overset{\to}{a}$ makes with vectors $\overset{\to}{b} and \overset{\to}{c}$ respectively and $\overset{\to}{a} \times \left(\overset{\to}{b} \times \overset{\to}{c}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}\overset{\to}{b}$, then $\left|\alpha - \beta\right|$ is equal to :
questions.solution:
$\overset{\to}{a} \times \left(\overset{\to}{b} \times \overset{\to}{c}\right) = \overset{\to}{b}2 ⇒ \left(\overset{\to}{a} . \overset{\to}{c}\right)\overset{\to}{b} - \left(\overset{\to}{a} . \overset{\to}{b}\right)\overset{\to}{c} = \overset{\to}{b}2$

Since, $\overset{\to}{b}$ is not parallel to $\overset{\to}{c} ⇒ \overset{\to}{a} . \overset{\to}{c} = \dfrac{1}{2} ⇒ \left|a\right|\left|c\right|cos\beta = \dfrac{1}{2} ⇒ cos\beta = \dfrac{1}{2}$ and

$\overset{\to}{a} . \overset{\to}{b} = 0 ⇒ \left|a\right|\left|b\right|cos\alpha = 0 ⇒ cos\alpha = 0$

$⇒ \beta = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$ and $\alpha = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$

$∴ \left|\alpha - \beta\right| = \dfrac{\pi}{2} - \dfrac{\pi}{3} = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$

questions.q: The sum of the distinct real values of $\mu$ for which the vectors $\mu\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}, \overset{^}{i} + \mu\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}, \overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \mu\overset{^}{k}$ are co-planar, is
questions.solution:
Given the three vectors are coplanar.

Hence, $\left|\begin{cases}\mu & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & \mu & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & \mu\end{cases}\right| = 0$

$⇒ \mu\left({\mu}^{2} - 1\right) - 1\left(\mu - 1\right) + 1\left(1 - \mu\right) = 0$

$⇒ \mu\left(\mu - 1\right)\left(\mu + 1\right) - 2\left(\mu - 1\right) = 0\left[∵ {a}^{2} - {b}^{2} = \left(a - b\right)\left(a + b\right)\right]$

$⇒ \left(\mu - 1\right)\left(\mu\left(\mu + 1\right) - 2\right) = 0$

$⇒ \left(\mu - 1\right)\left({\mu}^{2} + \mu + 2\right) = 0$

$⇒ \left(\mu - 1\right)\left(\mu - 1\right)\left(\mu + 2\right) = 0$

$⇒ \mu = 1, 1, - 2$

Therefore, the sum of the distinct real values of $\mu = - 2 + 1 = - 1$.

$⇒ \left(\mu - 1\right)\left(\mu\left(\mu + 1\right) - 2\right) = 0$

Therefore, the sum of the distinct real values of $\mu = - 2 + 1 = - 1$.

$\vec{c}=2 \hat{i}+4 \hat{j}+\left(\lambda^{2}-1\right) \hat{k}$ be coplanar vectors. Then the

non-zero vector $\vec{a} \times \vec{c}$ is:
questions.explanation:
$\because \bar{a}, \bar{b}$ and $\bar{c}$ are coplanar

$\therefore\left|\begin{array}{ccc}1 & 2 & 4 \\ 1 & \lambda & 4 \\ 2 & 4 & \left(\lambda^{2}-1\right)\end{array}\right|=0$\Rightarrow \quad \lambda^{3}-\lambda-16+2\left(8-\lambda^{2}+1\right)+4(4-2 \lambda)=0$\Rightarrow \quad \lambda^{3}-2 \lambda^{2}-9 \lambda+18=0$

Since $\overset{\to}{b} = 2\overset{\to}{a},$ so $3 - {\lambda}_{2} = 2{\lambda}_{1}$

${\lambda}_{2} = 3 - 2{\lambda}_{1} . . . \left(1\right)$

Since, $\overset{\to}{a}$ is perpendicular to $\overset{\to}{c}$ so

$6 + 6{\lambda}_{1} + 3\left({\lambda}_{3} - 1\right) = 0$

$\left({\lambda}_{1}, {\lambda}_{2}, {\lambda}_{3}\right) = \left({\lambda}_{1}, 3 - 2{\lambda}_{1}, - 1 - 2{\lambda}_{1}\right)$ where ${\lambda}_{1} \in R$

Then the value of $\mu$ for which the vector $\overset{\to}{AB}$ is parallel to the plane $x - 4y + 3z = 1$ is
questions.solution:
Let A$is \left(1 - 3\mu, \mu - 1, 2 + 5\mu\right)

We know that$ the $vector joining two points \left({x}_{1}, {y}_{1}, {z}_{1}\right) and \left({x}_{2}, {y}_{2}, {z}_{2}\right)$ is $\left({x}_{2} - {x}_{1}\right)$\overset{^}{i} + $\left({y}_{2} - {y}_{1}\right)\overset{^}{j} + \left({z}_{2} - {z}_{1}\right)$\overset{^}{k}$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{AB} = $\left(3\mu + 2\right)\overset{^}{i} + \left(3 - \mu\right)$\overset{^}{j} + $\left(4 - 5\mu\right)\overset{^}{k}$ which is parallel to plane $x - 4y + 3z = 1$

$⇒ 1\left(3\mu + 2\right) - 4\left(3 - \mu\right) + 3\left(4 - 5\mu\right) = 0$

$⇒ 3\mu + 2 - 12 + 4\mu + 12 - 15\mu = 0$

$⇒ - 8\mu + 2 = 0$

$⇒ \mu = \dfrac{1}{4}$ .

questions.q: Let $\overset{\to}{a} = \overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \sqrt{2}\overset{^}{k}, \overset{\to}{b} = {b}_{1}\overset{^}{i} + {b}_{2}\overset{^}{j} + \sqrt{2}\overset{^}{k}$ and $\overset{\to}{c} = 5\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \sqrt{2}\overset{^}{k}$ be three vectors such that the projection vector of $\overset{\to}{b}$ on $\overset{\to}{a}$ is $\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|$ . If $\overset{\to}{a} + \overset{\to}{b}$ is perpendicular to $\overset{\to}{c}$ , then $\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|$ is equal to:
questions.solution:
Since $\left(\overset{\to}{a} + \overset{\to}{b}\right)$ is perpendicular to $\overset{\to}{c}$, hence

$\left(\overset{\to}{a} + \overset{\to}{b}\right) \cdot \overset{\to}{c} = 0$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{c} + \overset{\to}{b} \cdot \overset{\to}{c} = 0$

$⇒ 5 + 1 + 2 + 5{b}_{1} + {b}_{2}^{} + 2 = 0$

$⇒ 5{b}_{1} + {b}_{2} = - 10 . . . \left(1\right)$

Given,

$\dfrac{\overset{\to}{b} \cdot \overset{\to}{a}}{\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|} = \left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|$

$\left\{∵ \overset{\to}{p} = r\overset{^}{i} + s\overset{^}{j} + t\overset{^}{k} ⇒ \left|\overset{\to}{p}\right| = \sqrt{{r}^{2} + {s}^{2} + {t}^{2}}\right\}$

$⇒ {b}_{1} + {b}_{2} + 2 = 4$

$⇒ {b}_{1} + {b}_{2} = 2 . . . \left(2\right)$

Solving $\left(1\right)$ and $\left(2\right),${b}_{1} = - 3, {b}_{2} = 5$

$∴ \left|\overset{\to}{b}\right| = \sqrt{9 + 25 + 2} = 6$

questions.q: Let $\overset{\to}{a} = \overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j}, \overset{\to}{b} = \overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$ and $\overset{\to}{c}$ be a vector such that $\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{c} + \overset{\to}{b} = \overset{\to}{0}$ and $\overset{\to}{a} . \overset{\to}{c} = 4,$ then ${| \overset{\to}{c} |}^{2}$ is equal to:
questions.solution:
Let the angle between $\overset{\to}{a}$ and $\overset{\to}{c}$ is $\theta .$

$∴ cos ⁡ \theta = \dfrac{\overset{\to}{a} . \overset{\to}{c}}{\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|\left|\overset{\to}{c}\right|} = \dfrac{4}{\sqrt{2}\left|\overset{\to}{c}\right|}$

Given, $\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{c} + \overset{\to}{b} = 0$

$⇒ \left|\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{c}\right| = \left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|$

$⇒ \left|\overset{\to}{a}\right| . \left|\overset{\to}{c}\right|sin ⁡ \theta = \left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|$

$⇒ {\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|}^{2}{\left|\overset{\to}{c}\right|}^{2}\sin^{2} ⁡ \theta = {\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|}^{2}$

$⇒ 2{\left|\overset{\to}{c}\right|}^{2}\left(1 - \cos^{2} ⁡ \theta\right) = 3$

$⇒ 2{\left|\overset{\to}{c}\right|}^{2}\left(1 - \dfrac{16}{2{\left|\overset{\to}{c}\right|}^{2}}\right) = 3$

$⇒ 2{\left|\overset{\to}{c}\right|}^{2} - 16 = 3$

$⇒ {\left|\overset{\to}{c}\right|}^{2} = \dfrac{19}{2}$

Then $\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|$ equals
questions.solution:
Given, $\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b} = \overset{\to}{c}$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{a} \times \left(\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b}\right) = \overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{c}$

$⇒ \left(\overset{\to}{a} ⋅ \overset{\to}{b}\right)\overset{\to}{a} - \left(\overset{\to}{a} ⋅ \overset{\to}{a}\right)\overset{\to}{b} = \overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{c}$

$\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{c} = \left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & - 1\end{cases}\right| = - 2\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$

$⇒ 3\overset{\to}{a} - 3\overset{\to}{b} = - 2\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$

$⇒ 3\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k} - 3\overset{\to}{b} = - 2\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{b} = \dfrac{1}{3}\left(5\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}\right)$

$∴ \left|\overset{\to}{b}\right| = \dfrac{\sqrt{25 + 4 + 4}}{3}$

$⇒ \left|\overset{\to}{b}\right| = \sqrt{\dfrac{11}{3}}$

$ D(x, y, z)=\left(\frac{6}{3}, \frac{13}{3}, \frac{18}{3}\right) $ Therefore, position vector of point $ P=\frac{1}{3}(6 i+13 j+18 k) $

questions.q: An angle between the lines whose direction cosines are given by the equations, $l+3 m+5 n=$ 0 and $5 l m-2 m n+6 n l=0$, is
questions.solution:
Given

$\begin{aligned}$&l+3 m+5 n=0 \\
&$\text{$ and }5 l m-2 m n+6 n l=0
\end{aligned}

From eq. (1) we have

l=-3 m-5 n

Put the value of$l$ in eq. (2), we get;

$\begin{aligned}$&5(-3 m-5 n) m-2 m n+6 n(-3 m-5 n)=0 \\
&\Rightarrow 15 m²+45 m n+30 n²=0 \\
&\Rightarrow m²+3 m n+2 n²=0 \\
&\Rightarrow m²+2 m n+m n+2 n²=0 \\
&\Rightarrow(m+n)(m+2 n)=0 \\
&\therefore m=-n $\text{$ or }m=-2 n \\
&$\text{$ For }m=-n, l=-2 n \\
&$\text{ And $for }m=-2 n, l=n
\end{aligned}$\begin{aligned}$&\therefore(l, m, n)=(-2 n,-n, n) $\text{$ Or }(l, m, n) \\
&=(n,-2 n, n) \\
&\Rightarrow(l, m, n)=(-2,-1,1)$\text{$ Or }(l, m, n) \\
&=(1,-2,1)
\end{aligned}

Therefore, angle between the lines is given as:$\begin{aligned}$&\cos ($\theta)=\frac{(-2)(1)+(-1) \cdot(-2)+(1)(1)}{\sqrt{6} \cdot \sqrt{6}}$\\
&\Rightarrow \cos ($\theta)=\frac{1}{6} \Rightarrow \theta=\cos ^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{6}\right)
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: The area (in sq. units) of the parallelogram whose diagonals are along the vectors $8\overset{^}{i} - 6\overset{^}{j}$ and $3\overset{^}{i} + 4\overset{^}{j} - 12\overset{^}{k},$ is:
questions.solution:
Let the given diagonals be $\overset{\to}{{d}_{1}}$ and $\overset{\to}{{d}_{2}}$ , then

${d}_{1} \times {d}_{2} = \left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 8 & - 6 & 0 \\ 3 & 4 & - 12\end{cases}\right|$

$= 72\overset{^}{i} - \left(- 96\right)\overset{^}{j} + 50\overset{^}{k}$

$\left|{d}_{1} \times {d}_{2}\right| = \sqrt{{72}^{2} + {\left(- 96\right)}^{2} + {\left(50\right)}^{2}} = \sqrt{5184 + 9216 + 2500}$

$\left|{d}_{2} \times {d}_{2}\right| = \sqrt{16900} = 130$

$Area = \dfrac{1}{2}\left|{d}_{1} \times {d}_{2}\right| = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 130$

$= 65$

questions.solution:
Given $\overset{\to}{x} = 3\overset{^}{i} - 6\overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}, \overset{\to}{y} = \overset{^}{i} + 4\overset{^}{j} - 3\overset{^}{k}$ and $\overset{\to}{z} = 3\overset{^}{i} - 4\overset{^}{j} - 12\overset{^}{k} .$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{x} \times \overset{\to}{y} = \left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 3 & - 6 & - 1 \\ 1 & 4 & - 3\end{cases}\right|$

$= \overset{^}{i}\left(18 + 4\right) - \overset{^}{j}\left(- 9 + 1\right) + \overset{^}{k}\left(12 + 6\right) = 22\overset{^}{i} + 8\overset{^}{j} + 18\overset{^}{k} = 2\left(11\overset{^}{i} + 4\overset{^}{j} + 9\overset{^}{k}\right)$

Now, we know that the projection of a vector $\overset{\to}{a}$ on $\overset{\to}{b}$ is defined as $\dfrac{\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{b}}{\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|}$

Hence, the magnitude of projection of $\overset{\to}{x} \times \overset{\to}{y}$ on $\overset{\to}{z}$ is $\dfrac{\left(\overset{\to}{x} \times \overset{\to}{y}\right) \cdot \overset{\to}{z}}{\left|\overset{\to}{z}\right|}$

$= \dfrac{\left|2\left(33 - 16 - 108\right)\right|}{\sqrt{{3}^{2} + {4}^{2} + 1{2}^{2}}}$

$= \dfrac{2 \times 91}{\sqrt{169}} = \dfrac{2 \times 91}{13} = 14 .$

&a^2=2 \\

questions.q: A vector $\vec{n}$ is inclined to $x$-axis at $45^{\circ}$, to $y$-axis at $60^{\circ}$ and at an acute angle to $z$-axis. If $\vec{n}$ is a normal to a plane passing through the point $(\sqrt{2},-1,1)$ then the equation of the plane is :
questions.solution:
Direction cosines of $\vec{n}$ are $\frac{1}{2}, \frac{1}{4}, \frac{1}{2}$.
Equation of the plane,

$\begin{aligned}$& $\frac{1}{2}($x-$\sqrt{2})+\frac{1}{4}($y+1)+$\frac{1}{2}($z-1)=0 \\
\Rightarrow & 2(x-$\sqrt{2})+($y+1)+2(z-1)=0 \\
\Rightarrow & 2 x+y+2 z=2 $\sqrt{2}-$1+2 \\
\Rightarrow & 2 x+y+2 z=2 $\sqrt{2}+$1
\end{aligned}

Equation$ of the plane,

\begin{aligned}

\Rightarrow & 2(x-\sqrt{2})+(y+1)+2(z-1)=0 \\
\Rightarrow & 2 x+y+2 z=2 \sqrt{2}-1+2 \\
\Rightarrow & 2 x+y+2 z=2 \sqrt{2}+1
\end{aligned}

questions.q:
Statement 1: The vectors $\vec{a}, \vec{b}$ and $\vec{c}$ lie in the same plane if and only if $\vec{a} \cdot(\vec{b} \times \vec{c})=0$
Statement 2: The vectors $\vec{u}$ and $\vec{v}$ are perpendicular if and only if $\vec{u} \cdot \vec{v}=0$ where $\vec{u} \times \vec{v}$ is a vector perpendicular to the plane of $\vec{u}$ and $\vec{v}$
options:
Statement 1 is false, Statement 2 is true.

Statement 1 is true, Statement 2 is true, Statement 2 is correct explanation for Statement 1.

Statement 1 is true, Statement 2 is false.

Statement 1 is true, Statement 2 is true, Statement 2 is not a correct explanation for Statement 1.
questions.solution:
Statement - 1
The vectors $\vec{a}, \vec{b}$ and $\vec{c}$ lie in the same plane.
$\Rightarrow \vec{a}, \vec{b}$ and $\vec{c}$ are coplanar.
We know, the necessary and sufficient conditions for three vectors to be coplanar is that $[\vec{a} \vec{b} \vec{c}]=0$
i.e. $\vec{a} \cdot(\vec{b} \times \vec{c})=0$
Hence, statement-1 is true.

& =-3 \cos \theta+4 \sin $\theta

|-3 \cos $\theta+4 \sin $\theta|=\sqrt{(-3)^2+(4)^2}=\sqrt{25}=$5

questions.question: The sum of two forces is 18 N and resultant whose direction is at right angles to the smaller force is 12 N. The magnitude of the two forces are
questions.explanation: Let two forces be $P and Q$. Given P+Q=18 and $P \hat{a}+Q \hat{b}=12 \hat{c} \Rightarrow P \hat{a}-12 \hat{c}=\bar{Q} \hat{b}$ \begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow P^2+144=Q^2=(18-P)^2 ; \Rightarrow P^2+144=324-36 P+P^2 \\ & \Rightarrow 36 P=180 \Rightarrow P=5 $\text{ and $} Q=13 \end{aligned} (where$\vec{a} and \vec{b}$ are unit vectors along $P and Q$ ).
